claims.text: Letterhead: 'HARRY REID, MAJORITY LEADER, NEVADA — United States Senate, Washington, DC 20510'. Dated June 24, 2009. Addressed to 'Honorable William Lynn III, Deputy Secretary of Defense, 1010 Defense Pentagon, Washington, DC 20301-1010'. Salutation: 'Dear Secretary Lynn:'
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

claims.text: Text: 'Beginning this past September, the U.S. Senate has mandated that the Defense Intelligence Agency assess far-term foreign advanced aerospace threats to the United States. The scope of program interest covers from the present out to forty years and beyond.'
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

claims.text: Text: 'technical studies are being conducted in regard to advanced lift, propulsion, the use of unconventional materials and controls, signature reduction, weaponry, human interface and human effects.'
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

claims.text: Text: 'Since the Advanced Aerospace Threat and Identification Program (AAITP) and study were first commissioned, much progress has been made with the identification of several highly sensitive, unconventional aerospace-related findings. Given the current rate of success, the continued study of these subjects will likely lead to technology advancements that in the immediate near-term will require extraordinary protection. Due to the sensitivities of the information surrounding aspects of this program, I require your assistance in establishing a [restricted special access program].'
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

claims.text: The USD(I) memorandum to DEPSECDEF confirms receipt and framing: 'Senator Harry Reid sent a letter to you on June 24, 2009 requesting the Department of Defense put the AAITP under "Restricted Special Access Protection" (Tab A).'
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237660/

claims.text: Reid, the sitting Senate Majority Leader, asserted on his own signature that the program had produced 'several highly sensitive, unconventional aerospace-related findings' warranting 'extraordinary protection' — a claim made in writing to the Deputy Secretary of Defense, not to the press.
claims.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

claims.source: https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_15-DIRD_Advanced_Space_Propulsion_Based_on_Vacuum_Spacetime_Metric_Engineer.pdf

claims.text: Assigned to Teofilo on internal evidence: endnote 17 cites "G. Miley, H. Momota, L. Wu, M. Reilley, V. Teofilo, R. Dell, and R. Hargus, Space Probe Application of IEC Thrusters, Fusion Science and Technology 56 1, 533-539, July 2009", the only occurrence of either candidate author's surname in either aneutronic document. It sits immediately adjacent to endnote 16, a citation of AeroJet/Lockheed Martin Space Systems Company Hall thruster hardware that is also named in the body text. The document's framing is industrial rather than academic: GEO comsat markets, a funding table of privately backed fusion companies, and a closing argument that reactor physicists must now work alongside "the space systems companies".

claims.text: THE ZERO-COUNTS, taken over the whole released 45-page PDF on 19 September 2026: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0, and THOMAS TOWNSEND BROWN ABSENT. The three occurrences of 'Brown' are other authors' surnames in the reference list. Alcubierre occurs once, as reference [43], the 1994 Classical and Quantum Gravity citation, and that is its only appearance in this document. A count is checkable and an adjective is not, which is why the node carries numbers.
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: Its contents page, as released: 'Concepts for Antigravity Within Newtonian Physics', 'Negating Newtonian Gravity', 'Energy Estimate for Newtonian Levitation', 'Concepts for Antigravity Within General Relativity', 'Antigravity via Gravitomagnetic Forces', 'Forward's Dipole Gravitational Field Generator', 'Felber's Relativistic Antigravity Effect', 'Negative Energy-Induced Antigravity', 'Cosmological Antigravity', 'Pressure as a Source of Gravity', 'Vacuum Energy of Einstein's Cosmological Constant', 'Dark Energy', 'Antigravity Propulsion Application of Dark/Vacuum Energy', 'Quantum Antigravity Propulsion Concepts', 'Antigravity via Quantum Vacuum Zero-Point Fluctuation Force', 'Antigravity via Nonretarded Quantum Interatomic Dispersion Force', 'Conclusion: The Way Forward', with appendices on static radial fields, squeezed quantum vacuum, gravitationally squeezed electromagnetic zero-point fluctuations and the dynamical Casimir effect.
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: Its conclusion, 'The Way Forward', verbatim in part: 'This report has reviewed and analyzed a number of antigravity concepts that are found within Newtonian gravity theory, General Relativity Theory, semi-classical quantum gravity theory, quantum field theory, and nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion force theory. One found that plausible mechanisms exist within Newtonian and general relativistic theories whereby one could embody a realistic device that produces a significant antigravity force. However, one discovered that there are daunting technical challenges that arise in each of the proposed embodiments.'
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: And: 'Antigravity forces produced by quantum electromagnetic vacuum ZPF or by nonretarded quantum interatomic dispersion forces in a curved spacetime (that is, gravitational field) are very feeble, but there are proposals based on other theoretical and empirical studies which suggest that these forces can be amplified to macroscopic level. However, there are a number of difficult technical challenges to overcome in order to achieve success.' Its first named next step is that 'Presently, the technology does not exist to achieve the astronomical mass densities, extreme velocities or accelerations of mass motion, and the large device dimensions required to produce large enough antigravity forces for useful propulsion'.
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', 30 March 2010, ICOD 1 December 2009, 45 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: ITS OWN SUMMARY, VERBATIM, and it is a document about hypersonic aerodynamics and nothing else: 'The paper reviews novel propulsion concepts utilizing plasmas (ionized gases) and magnetohydrodynamics (MHD). These concepts are shown to be attractive due to their potential to achieve propulsion and aerodynamic performance far beyond current conventional technologies. However, significant difficulties impede the development and application of these technologies; these include weight, complexity, higher power, and the need for complex and energy-consuming artificial ionization in "cold" air (at Mach <12).'
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1011-006, 'MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications', 21 November 2010, ICOD 20 July 2010, 33 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_33-DIRD_MHD_Air_Breathing_Propulsion_and_Power_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: Its finding on the concept the popular literature most often reaches for, verbatim: 'A well-publicized Ajax concept of MHD energy bypass has been shown to be meaningless below at least Mach 12. In contrast, a new "reverse energy bypass" with Virtual Cowl is potentially practical for air-breathing hypersonic vehicles.'
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1011-006, 'MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications', 21 November 2010, ICOD 20 July 2010, 33 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_33-DIRD_MHD_Air_Breathing_Propulsion_and_Power_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: THE ZERO-COUNTS over the whole released 33-page PDF, taken 19 September 2026: UFO 0, unidentified 0, anti-gravity 0, antigravity 0, scalar 0, zero point 0, levitation 0. The word 'gravity' occurs once. Its chapter structure is concept overview, aeronautical applications, space applications, and summary and predictions, with figures on arcjet thrusters, gridded ion thrusters, Hall thrusters, scramjet inlet control by e-beam ionization, the Ajax vehicle concept, the virtual cowl and reentry drag reduction.
claims.source: Defense Intelligence Reference Document DIA-08-1011-006, 'MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications', 21 November 2010, ICOD 20 July 2010, 33 pages as released, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_33-DIRD_MHD_Air_Breathing_Propulsion_and_Power_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

claims.text: Stated inference, and it is the strand's comparison. The board already records that this DIRD is attributed on the DIA list supplied to the Senate Armed Services Committee to 'Dr S Macheret, Lockheed Martin'. A government agency paid a Lockheed Martin plasma physicist to survey magnetohydrodynamic propulsion under the same programme the lore invokes, and what he delivered concerns scramjet inlets, virtual cowls and reentry drag reduction. NOTHING JOINS THIS DOCUMENT TO US 3,322,374 and the edge between them records a similarity of subject only.

entities.label: House Oversight joint hearing, 13 November 2024 - 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth'
entities.sub: congressional-hearings
entities.desc: On 13 November 2024 at 11:30 am in 2154 Rayburn, the House Oversight Committee's Subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Information Technology, and Government Innovation and its Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs held a joint hearing chaired by Rep. Nancy Mace, published by GPO as Serial No. 118-135 (CHRG-118hhrg57440). The witnesses were retired Rear Adm. Tim Gallaudet, former Oceanographer of the Navy and former acting NOAA administrator; Luis Elizondo, former Defense Department official; Michael Gold, former NASA associate administrator for space policy and partnerships and a member of the NASA UAP Independent Study Team; and Michael Shellenberger, founder of Public. This is the hearing at which the Immaculate Constellation report entered the Congressional Record: Mace announced from the dais that committee staff had asked her to enter 'this 12-page document that Michael Shellenberger brought today that describes the Immaculate Constellation government program', and it appears in the Index of Documents as 'Report, Pentagon, Immaculate Constellation; submitted by Rep. Mace.' It is also the hearing at which Elizondo answered Mace's direct question - 'Has the government conducted secret UAP crash retrieval programs? Yes or no?' - with a single word, 'Yes', while declining to discuss whether he was read into such programmes except in closed session. Gallaudet testified about the January 2015 Fleet Forces Command 'urgent safety of flight issue' email containing the GIMBAL video, which was recalled from Navy inboxes. Gold cited Alex Dietrich by name, saying she 'was mocked by her colleagues' and that her incident 'went years without any investigation.' Mace also stated on the record that 'there are certain individuals who did not want this hearing to happen because they feared what might be disclosed', and never named them. The hearing's structural achievement was to move the crash-retrieval allegation from a single whistleblower's second-hand account in 2023 to an affirmative one-word answer from a second former official in 2024, and to place a named alleged special access programme into the permanent record of Congress - where, twenty-one months later, no executive branch office has answered for it.

entities.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)
entities.sub: mechanism
entities.desc: The carve-out is the most important single mechanism on this board, because it is the point at which a special access program held at a private company stops being visible to any government security official who is not inside the program. It is defined identically in DoD Directive 5205.07 (2010) and DoD Manual 5205.07 Volume 1: 'A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its National Industrial Security Program obligation to perform industrial security oversight functions for a DoD SAP.' It is codified in the National Industrial Security Program rule at 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), which provides that 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07'. What is removed is specified in DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1: the SAP security inspections at cleared defense contractor locations, the authorisation of classified contractor SAP information systems and guest systems in contractor SAP facilities, and the coordination with the counterintelligence component for threat and incident cross-sharing. What replaces it is oversight by the cognizant authority's own Program Security Officer - an official appointed by and reporting to the SAP structure itself. The carve-out is requested as line 11.d of the SAP Approval Package Checklist ('Contract strategy (carve-out justification if applicable)'), recommended in the action memo to the Deputy Secretary, and, once approved, must be recorded in the program record file together with 'the identification of SAP facilities ... that have been carved-out based upon this authority'. Neither the number of carve-outs in force, nor the list of carved-out facilities, nor the identity of the approving official for any individual carve-out has ever been published. This is the precise mechanism that would permit a contractor to hold material under a DoD program with no external government inspector ever entering the vault.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 39 of 1170, score 88). 12 connections, 5 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 1 official denial recorded against it. Axes C3/A3/D3.

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 (12 Sep 2024) glossary defines it: 'carve out: A provision approved by the Secretary of Defense or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DCSA of its National Industrial Security Program obligation.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: The regulatory counterpart, 32 CFR 117.6(b): 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07.'
claims.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-32/subtitle-A/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-117/section-117.6

claims.text: MAJOR CHANGE, 2024. DoDI 5205.11 para 1.2.i.: 'Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversight for the administration of the National Industrial Security Program will be phased out in July 2029 in accordance with the carve-out provision.' The 2024 policy therefore schedules a blanket, enterprise-wide withdrawal of DCSA from DoD SAP industrial security by July 2029, rather than a case-by-case carve-out.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: A programmed phase-out of DCSA oversight across the DoD SAP enterprise by July 2029 converts the carve-out from an exception requiring SecDef/DepSecDef signature into the default state. If accurate, after that date no independent DoD agency holds a routine inspection right at SAP contractor facilities, and the record of which facilities host which programs stops accumulating in DCSA's system. Reasoning stated from 1.2.i.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: The carve-out's authority runs to exactly two officials. 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) conditions it on approval by 'the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense', and on no one else.
claims.source: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), eCFR renderer API, read 22 August 2026, https://www.ecfr.gov/api/renderer/v1/content/enhanced/current/title-32?part=117

claims.text: The regulation ties the carve-out to DoDD 5205.07, 'DoD SAP Policy', by name and by URL, so the codified rule and the DoD directive are a matched pair rather than parallel authorities.
claims.source: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), eCFR renderer API, read 22 August 2026, https://www.ecfr.gov/api/renderer/v1/content/enhanced/current/title-32?part=117

claims.text: 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3): 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, "DoD SAP Policy".'

The carve-out is approvable only by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense - no delegation to a service secretary, component head or SAPCO director is provided for in DoDD 5205.07 (2010), DoDI 5205.11 or DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1.
claims.source: DoDD 5205.07 (2010) Glossary; DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c; 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3)

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 6 lists 'Proposals to relieve DSS of NISP security oversight responsibilities (carve-out) when required' among the actions that must be coordinated through the DoD SAPCO to the Deputy Secretary of Defense for decision.
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Enclosure 6, para 5.a(8)

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 requires DoD SAPCO to provide 'DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions', which means a list of carved-out facilities exists as an agency record.
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Enclosure 2, para 2.k

claims.text: After a carve-out, the only recurring security inspection of the contractor facility is conducted by the Program Security Officer, who is 'appointed in writing by the appropriate Director CA SAPCO or designee' and exercises responsibilities 'on behalf of the SAPCO' - that is, by the program inspecting itself. Reasoning: DoDM 5205.07-V1 removes the DSS/DCSA inspection and its glossary defines the PSO's appointment chain as internal to the SAP structure.
claims.source: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1, Enclosure 2 para 2.c and Glossary definition of PSO

claims.text: A carved-out contractor SAP is the smallest documented configuration in U.S. law in which classified material can be physically held by a private company with no inspection by any official outside the program, no external accreditation of the computers holding the program's data, and no independent counterintelligence reporting line. Reasoning: enumeration of the three functions expressly suspended by DoDM 5205.07-V1 Enclosure 2 para 2.c.
claims.source: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1, Enclosure 2, para 2.c

entities.sub: dod-issuance
entities.desc: The current directive, effective 12 September 2024, cancels the 1 July 2010 version as amended and incorporates the Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum 'Implementation Guidance for DoD Special Access Program Enterprise Reform' of 11 July 2023. Two changes matter for this board. First, the governance structure is retained and strengthened: the SAPOC remains 'the senior governing body of the DoD SAP Enterprise for governance, management, and oversight of DoD SAPs', chaired by the Deputy Secretary of Defense, with the Director of DoD SAPCO as Executive Secretary of the SAPOC and the SRG and Chair of the SSWG, reporting directly to the Deputy Secretary. Establishment of new SAP umbrellas and compartments is stated to be 'by exception' and requires Secretary or Deputy Secretary approval. Second, and much more significant, the 2024 directive replaces the acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived taxonomy with two new categories - 'Joint Force Integration SAP', defined as 'A SAP intended for greater integration and sharing across the Joint Force and the broader SAP community', and 'Strategic Enabler SAP', defined as 'A SAP protecting capabilities or information that enable strategic competition and warrant more limited and restrictive sharing'. The words acknowledged, unacknowledged, waived and carve-out do not appear in its definitions section. This does not repeal 10 U.S.C. 119(e), which continues to authorise the reporting waiver, and it does not repeal 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), which continues to authorise the carve-out and still cites this very directive by number. The effect is that the two mechanisms most relevant to a concealed program survive in statute and in the Code of Federal Regulations while ceasing to be defined in the Department's own public charter - the terminology has been removed from the shop window without being removed from the shop. The directive also carries forward the congressional-contact reporting rule: 'All personnel accessed to DoD SAPs will notify the Director, DoD SAPCO ... when briefing or providing DoD SAP material to any member of Congress.'
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 86 of 1170, score 68). 6 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 2 official denials recorded against it. Axes C1/A3/D2.

entities.label: DoDI 5205.11 — Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD SAPs (12 Sep 2024)
entities.sub: dod-issuance
entities.desc: DoDI 5205.11 is the single most useful public document on this board, because it does not merely define the mechanism - it walks through it, with a worked example and a timeline. Enclosure 6 sets out the prospective SAP (PSAP) approval sequence in days from establishment: SSWG review by P+14, draft security classification guide by P+45, approval package to the Senior Review Group by P+90, SRG convenes at P+105, final package to the SAPOC at P+130, SAPOC convenes at P+150, Deputy Secretary of Defense decision and congressional notification or termination at P+180, and 'End of 30-day period without Congressional decision' at P+210. The last line is the statutory clock of 10 U.S.C. 119(f) reduced to a checkbox: Congress is not asked to approve anything, it is notified, and after thirty days of silence the program starts. Appendix 2 to Enclosure 6 is the SAP Approval Package Checklist, whose item 2 requires that 'If unacknowledged and reporting requirements are to be waived, attach justification to waive the requirements of Volumes 2A and 2B of DoD 7000.14-R' - the Financial Management Regulation - and whose item 11.d requires a 'Contract strategy (carve-out justification if applicable)'. Appendix 3 is an unclassified sample Action Memo to the Deputy Secretary of Defense recommending establishment of a fictional unacknowledged operations and support SAP nicknamed GREEN TREE, in which the Director of DoD SAPCO writes: 'The Defense Security Service will be carved out from its normal industrial security oversight responsibilities' and recommends 'that you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize carve-out status and the mandatory administration of CI polygraphs'. Enclosure 7 then requires that each SAP record file contain 'Written approval by SecDef or DepSecDef of carve-out status when DSS is relieved of industrial security oversight responsibilities' and 'The identification of SAP facilities ... that have been carved-out based upon this authority'. Those two records are the FOIA target that would settle the question of how many carved-out facilities exist.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 58 of 1170, score 75). 7 connections, 2 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A3/D2.

claims.text: Header: DoD Instruction 5205.11, 'Management, Administration, and Oversight of DoD Special Access Programs'; effective September 12, 2024; reissues and cancels DoDI 5205.11, February 6, 2013, as amended; also incorporates and cancels the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum, 'Integrated Joint Special Technical Operations (IJSTO) Policy', April 5, 2021; approved by Kathleen H. Hicks, Deputy Secretary of Defense.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: WHAT MAKES A PROGRAM WAIVED, in DoD's own words. Para 1.2.f.: 'The Secretary of Defense may designate select unacknowledged SAPs as "waived" when it is determined that using standard procedures for reporting to Congress would adversely affect national security.' The waiver therefore attaches only to programs that are ALREADY unacknowledged; waived is a subset of unacknowledged, not a parallel category.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Glossary definitions verbatim: 'acknowledged SAP: A SAP whose existence is acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to others, but its specific details are classified.' 'unacknowledged SAP: A SAP having enhanced security measures, ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged.' 'waived SAP: A SAP for which the Secretary of Defense has waived applicable reporting following a determination of adverse effect to national security.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: WHO GETS TOLD. Para 7.2.a.(3): 'Only the chair, the ranking member, the staff directors, and one designated security manager of the defense and intelligence committees will be authorized access to waived DoD SAPs.' Para 7.2.b.: 'Members of Congress assigned to the defense and intelligence committees are authorized access to all DoD SAPs within the respective committee's SAP oversight jurisdiction, except for waived programs.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Para 7.2.f. verbatim: 'The personal staff of a member of Congress will not be granted access to DoD SAPs.' Non-committee members and staff may be granted access only to NON-waived SAPs, and only 'by the Director, DoD SAPCO following consultation with the respective chamber' (7.2.d.). Senate and House leadership may each nominate one professional staff member for access to all DoD SAPs (7.2.e.).
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: BUDGET PAPER TRAIL. Para 7.2.h. (congressional budget justification materials): waived program justification material goes only to committee staff directors, not to the committees as bodies.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: GAO ACCESS IS GATED. Para 7.2.g.: authorized access approval authorities may grant SAP access to GAO staff for specific projects only after the Director, DoD SAPCO consults with the chairman and ranking defense committee members. Congress's own audit arm cannot reach a DoD SAP without the audited department's SAPCO first clearing it with four members.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Para 7.1.: 'All DoD employees accessed to DoD SAPs will coordinate with and notify the DoD and OA SAPCOs through the CA SAPCO when intending to brief or provide DoD SAP material to any appropriately accessed members of Congress or professional staff member.' A cleared DoD employee cannot lawfully brief even an accessed member of Congress without first routing notice through the SAP's own control office.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: PERIODIC REVIEW OF WAIVED STATUS EXISTS. Para 3.5.a.(3)(d) makes the SAPOC annual review cover 'All waived DoD SAPs to determine the need for continued waived status,' as part of the 3.5.a.(3) mandate to 'Conduct an annual review of DoD SAPs to assess the continuing need for protection of CPI within SAP security controls, in accordance with E.O. 13526 and DoDD 5205.07.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: TIER ARCHITECTURE. DoDI 5205.11 establishes a tiered SAP structure: umbrellas at tier 1, compartments at tier 2, sub-compartments at tier 3 and below; only the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense may alter tier 1 structures. It distinguishes 'structural SAP: A SAP that provides organization to the architecture and does not protect discrete CPI' from 'content SAP: A SAP that protects discrete CPI.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: The structural/content distinction is load-bearing for any search of SAP nomenclature: a structural SAP is a container with a codeword and no content of its own, so a program name appearing in budget or security documentation may correspond to no discrete body of protected information at all. Conversely, discrete CPI can be moved between compartments under an unchanged tier-1 umbrella name without any tier-1 action reaching the Secretary. Reasoning stated from the 1.2 tier description.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Para 4.1.a.(2): 'Within 45 calendar days of creation of the SAP project, the CA will submit' the required documentation — establishing an internal 45-day paper deadline for new SAP projects, distinct from the statutory 30-day congressional pre-initiation notice under 10 U.S.C. 119(f).
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Para 5.1.e.(1): 'The use of a polygraph examination as a mandatory access determination requirement must be approved by the Secretary of Defense.' Mandatory-polygraph SAP access is a Secretary-level decision, which makes the presence of a polygraph requirement a marker of a program that reached the top of the department.
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Appendix 3 to Enclosure 6, sample action memo to the Deputy Secretary of Defense: 'The Defense Security Service will be carved out from its normal industrial security oversight responsibilities.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Appendix 3 to Enclosure 6, Figure 4

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 sample action memo recommendation: 'That you approve GTE as an unacknowledged SAP and authorize carve-out status and the mandatory administration of CI polygraphs, and that you sign the notification letters to Congress (TAB C) identifying GREEN TREE as a new SAP.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Appendix 3 to Enclosure 6, Figure 4

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 7 requires each SAP record file to include 'Written approval by SecDef or DepSecDef of carve-out status when DSS is relieved of industrial security oversight responsibilities' and 'The identification of SAP facilities (or identification of the SAPCO-approved database that contains the information) that have been carved-out based upon this authority.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Enclosure 7, para 1.a

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 6 PSAP timeline: 'NLT P+180 - DepSecDef decision. Congressional notification or PSAP termination as appropriate. NLT P+210 - End of 30-day period without Congressional decision.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Appendix 1 to Enclosure 6, Figure 2

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 SAP Approval Package Checklist item 2: 'Type, Category, and Classification of SAP. If unacknowledged and reporting requirements are to be waived, attach justification to waive the requirements of Volumes 2A and 2B of DoD 7000.14-R.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Appendix 2 to Enclosure 6, Figure 3

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Glossary: 'waived SAP. A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting in accordance with Reference (c) following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Glossary Part II

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d requires every DoD SAP to be assigned an unclassified nickname generated under CJCSM 3150.29D, and provides that 'Unclassified nicknames will be used in the annual SAP report to Congress.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, para 5.d

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 Enclosure 2 requires the Director, DoD SAPCO to establish 'policies and applicable procedures to satisfy reporting requirements for DSS carve-outs' and to provide 'DSS confirmation of SAP facilities where the DSS has been carved out of security oversight functions.'
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11, Enclosure 2, para 2.k

claims.text: Because the annual SAP report to Congress uses only unclassified nicknames, a member reading the list sees a word, not a mission. Reasoning: DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d expressly directs nickname use in the annual report and leaves the codeword optional and classified.
claims.source: DoDI 5205.11 para 5.d read against 10 U.S.C. 119(a)(2)(B)(i)

entities.label: DoDM 5205.07 — DoD SAP Security Manual (Volumes 1-4)
entities.sub: dod-issuance
entities.desc: The DoD SAP Security Manual is issued in four volumes under number 5205.07: Volume 1, General Procedures (18 June 2015, Change 1 12 February 2018); Volume 2, Personnel Security; Volume 3, Physical Security; and Volume 4, Marking. Volume 1 is the volume that carries the carve-out definition and the DSS relief provision, and is the only volume this board has been able to obtain in full from an archived copy of the DoD Issuances site; the current live URLs at esd.whs.mil for volumes 1 through 4 return errors to unauthenticated retrieval as of 12 August 2026, which is itself a finding worth recording. Volume 1 states its own lineage: it 'Assigns responsibilities, implements policy established in DoD Instruction (DoDI) 5205.11 ... and describes the general procedures for the administration of DoD SAP security' and 'Incorporates and cancels Revision 1 Department of Defense Overprint to the National Industrial Security Program (NISP) Operating Manual Supplement'. That last clause is the historical bridge: the security rules for contractor SAPs used to live as an overprint to the NISPOM Supplement, i.e. as a special-case annex to the industrial security system, and were pulled out into a standalone DoD manual - moving contractor SAP security further from the NISP baseline that DCSA inspects.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 66 of 1170, score 73). 5 connections, 4 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A3/D1.

claims.text: Volume 1: 'MANUAL NUMBER 5205.07, Volume 1, June 18, 2015, Incorporating Change 1, Effective February 12, 2018, USD(I). SUBJECT: DoD Special Access Program (SAP) Security Manual: General Procedures.' A later Change 2 is effective 30 September 2020 under USD(I&S). Vol 1 'Incorporates and cancels Revision 1 Department of Defense Overprint to the National Industrial Security Program (NISP) Operating Manual Supplement.'
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Volume 2: 'MANUAL NUMBER 5205.07, Volume 2, November 24, 2015, Incorporating Change 2, Effective October 30, 2020, USD(I&S). SUBJECT: Special Access Program (SAP) Security Manual: Personnel Security.' Volume 3: 'MANUAL NUMBER 5205.07, Volume 3, April 23, 2015, Incorporating Change 2, Effective February 12, 2018. SUBJECT: DoD Special Access Program (SAP) Security Manual: Physical Security.' Volume 4: 'MANUAL NUMBER 5205.07, Volume 4, October 10, 2013, Incorporating Change 2, Effective September 8, 2020, USD(I&S). SUBJECT: Special Access Program (SAP) Security Manual: Marking.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507-V4p.PDF

claims.text: THE CARVE-OUT'S OPERATIONAL CONTENT. DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 2, para 2 (Director, DSS): 'Unless a carve-out provision is approved by the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense: (1) Performs SAP security inspections at cleared defense contractor locations in accordance with this volume, Reference (f), and the government contracting activity's completed DD Form 254 ... (2) Authorizes classified contractor SAP information systems (ISs) and the introduction of guest systems in contractor SAP facilities (SAPFs). (3) Coordinates with the designated counterintelligence (CI) component to provide cross-sharing of threat and incident information affecting the security of the facility or its defense information or cleared personnel.' A carve-out removes all three functions at once: physical inspection, IT accreditation, and CI information sharing.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1 glossary: 'carve-out. A provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense that relieves DSS of its NISP obligation to perform industrial security oversight functions for a DoD SAP.'
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Vol 1 states that inspections 'will be coordinated among the SAPCOs and DSS when not carved out and conducted jointly to the greatest extent possible' -- confirming that when a SAP IS carved out, the only remaining inspection is the program's own self-inspection plus SAPCO-internal compliance inspection.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: WHISTLEBLOWING IS ROUTED BACK INSIDE. Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 3: 'Government and industry FWAC SAP reporting involving SAP information will be accomplished through SAP channels. Collateral FWAC reporting channels must not be used for SAP information. b. The PSO will provide the telephone number for the current FWAC hotline for reporting SAP information. FWAC reporting information will be conspicuously posted in the SAP workspace. c. Employees do not need management approval before making reports.' Fraud, waste, abuse and corruption inside a SAP may not be reported through the ordinary DoD IG hotline; it must go through a SAP-channel hotline whose number is issued by the program's own security officer.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 4: 'The CUA documents areas of authorities and responsibilities between cognizant security offices (CSOs) when they share the same SAPF. ... The first CSO in an area, unless otherwise agreed upon, will be considered the host CSO responsible for all security oversight.' And, critically: 'For CUAs, the responsible organization will be identified for executing security cognizance with a carved-out SAP.' Multiple SAPs -- including carved-out ones -- can lawfully co-occupy one accredited facility under a written host/tenant agreement.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 7: 'PATENTS AND INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY. The CA SAPCO will develop procedures for processing patents and intellectual property involving SAP(s).' There is an explicit, standing policy channel for patents arising inside special access programs, delegated to each cognizant-authority SAP central office.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Vol 1, Enclosure 4, para 8 (Arms Control and Treaties): 'DoD SAPs will be protected against unnecessary or inadvertent exposure during USG participation in authorized verification activities, confidence-building measures, and overflights.' Para 9 (Litigation and Public Proceedings): 'Threatened or actual litigation, administrative investigations or inquiries, or public proceedings at the international, federal, State, tribal, or local levels that may involve a SAP will be reported to CA SAPCO.'
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: Vol 1 physical-security/visitor rules acknowledge the existence of undisclosed sites in operative text: 'Federal Government-affiliated identification cards will not be used for positive identification in unacknowledged locations.'
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 2, para 5 (Polygraphs): 'The Deputy Secretary of Defense is the approval authority for the use of polygraph examination as a mandatory access determination requirement; the requirement must be consistently applied to all candidates in accordance with DoDI 5210.91. CI-Scope polygraph examination must not be used as the only basis for granting access to DoD SAPs. Exceptions to these requirements will only be granted by the Deputy Secretary of Defense. ... CI polygraph examinations are considered current when administered within the past 5 years.' Para 6 provides that 'CA SAPCOs may establish or authorize SAP billet structures or access quotas that assign individual access by organization and duty position to SAPs under their cognizance.'
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20250305140253/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol2.pdf

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 states that it 'Incorporates and cancels Revision 1 Department of Defense Overprint to the National Industrial Security Program (NISP) Operating Manual Supplement.'
claims.source: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1, para 1.a(2)

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 applies to all DoD Components, to 'All DoD Component contractors and consultants who require access to DoD SAPs pursuant to the terms and conditions of the contract or agreement', and to non-DoD USG entities requiring access under an MOA.

entities.label: Acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived — the three states of a DoD SAP
entities.sub: taxonomy
entities.desc: The three-state taxonomy is the vocabulary the whole board depends on, and it is defined word for word in DoD's own issuances. An ACKNOWLEDGED SAP is 'A SAP whose existence is acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to others, but its specific details (technologies, materials, techniques, etc.,) are classified as specified in the applicable SCG'. Its name appears in the budget; you may know that it exists and nothing else. An UNACKNOWLEDGED SAP is 'A SAP having enhanced security measures ensuring the existence of the program is not acknowledged, affirmed, or made known to any person not authorized for such information'. The correct response to an inquiry is neither confirmation nor denial; the program's very existence is classified. A WAIVED SAP is 'A SAP for which the SecDef has waived applicable reporting in accordance with Reference (c) following a determination of adverse effect to national security. An unacknowledged SAP that has more restrictive reporting and access controls than other unacknowledged SAPs' - Reference (c) being 10 U.S.C. 119. Cross-cutting the three states are three categories defined by mission: an acquisition SAP protects 'sensitive research, development, testing and evaluation, modification, and procurement activities'; an intelligence SAP protects intelligence activity; and an operations and support SAP is 'established primarily to protect the planning for, execution of, and support to especially sensitive military operations' and 'may protect organizations, property, operational concepts, plans, or activities'. A SAP with subordinate structure is called an 'umbrella', with 'compartments, sub-compartments, or projects' beneath it. The single most important observation for this board is that the alleged legacy recovery effort - if it exists - would sit precisely at the intersection of a waived unacknowledged operations and support SAP with an acquisition SAP for the exploitation work, held under an umbrella whose compartments are known only to the compartment holders. Every element of that description is an ordinary term of art in DoDI 5205.11.

entities.label: Cover mechanisms — HVSACO, nicknames, unacknowledged locations
entities.sub: tradecraft
entities.desc: DoD's own manuals describe, in unclassified text, the tradecraft that keeps an unacknowledged program from surfacing. Every DoD SAP is assigned an unclassified nickname generated through the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff NICKA system under CJCSM 3150.29D, and 'Unclassified nicknames will be used in the annual SAP report to Congress'; whether a classified codeword is also used is decided by the cognizant authority SAPCO. So the artefact Congress receives is a list of two-word nicknames. The marking HANDLE VIA SPECIAL ACCESS CHANNELS ONLY - HVSACO - is applied, expressly, 'When using a SAP nickname for an unacknowledged SAP', and also 'When necessary to protect sensitive relationships' and 'To protect information that does not warrant classification under Executive Order 13526'; the manual states plainly that 'HVSACO is not a classification'. That is a control that restricts distribution of material which is not classified at all, and therefore is not reachable by a mandatory declassification review or by the classification-challenge machinery of E.O. 13526. Physical cover is addressed as well: 'Federal Government-affiliated identification cards will not be used for positive identification in unacknowledged locations' - the manual assumes the existence of facilities at which showing a federal badge would itself be a disclosure. Where two programs share a facility, a Co-Utilization Agreement between cognizant security offices governs, and 'For CUAs, the responsible organization will be identified for executing security cognizance with a carved-out SAP', which is how a carved-out program can sit inside a building that other programs also use without the other programs' security officers acquiring cognizance over it.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 126 of 1170, score 55). 3 connections, 2 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C2/A3/D2.

(2) To minimize OPSEC indicators. (3) To facilitate communication of information within SAPs.' Para 1.b: 'Dissemination of information warranting HVSACO protection will be limited to persons briefed into a SAP and retained within SAP approved channels.'

claims.text: THE UNCLASSIFIED WITHHOLDING. DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 5, para 1 lists when HVSACO is applied, including '(4) To protect information that does not warrant classification under Executive Order 13526' and '(5) When using a SAP nickname for an unacknowledged SAP.' HVSACO is therefore a control expressly designed to hold inside SAP channels material that does NOT meet the standard for classification. Para 1.c requires that on a public release request the originator review the material and either remove the HVSACO marking or 'Inform the requestor of the decision not to release the information, citing an appropriate authority.'

entities.label: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP
entities.sub: agency
entities.desc: DCSA, the successor to the Defense Security Service, is designated by 32 CFR 117.6(b)(1) as the DoD Cognizant Security Office. It administers the National Industrial Security Program 'as a separate program element on behalf of DoD GCAs and those agencies with agreements with DoD for security services' and 'Provides security oversight of the NISP as the DoD CSO on behalf of DoD components and those non-DoD executive branch agencies who enter into agreements with DoD'. It issues facility clearances for defense contractors 'to include contractors performing on DoD SAPs'. It is the only recurring, external, adversarial security inspection that a cleared contractor facility receives - and it is the entity that the carve-out provision at 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) switches off by a signature of the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense. DCSA's own performance without any carve-out was found wanting by GAO in 2004: GAO-04-332 concluded that DoD 'cannot provide adequate assurances that its oversight ensures the protection of classified information' at contractor facilities. The report is doubly relevant because GAO expressly excluded SAPs from the review at the request of committee staff - so the only public audit of the industrial security inspection system deliberately did not look at the programs the board cares about.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 176 of 1170, score 48). 5 connections, 2 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C1/A2/D2.

claims.text: 32 CFR 117.6(b): the Director, DCSA 'Oversees and manages DCSA, which serves as the DoD CSO', 'Administers the NISP as a separate program element on behalf of DoD GCAs and those agencies with agreements with DoD for security services', and 'Provides security oversight of the NISP as the DoD CSO on behalf of DoD components and those non-DoD executive branch agencies who enter into agreements with DoD' -- followed immediately by the carve-out sentence relieving the Director of that function for DoD SAPs on SecDef/DepSecDef approval.
claims.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-32/subtitle-A/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-117/section-117.6

claims.text: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1, Enclosure 2, para 2.b (then DSS, now DCSA): 'Issues facility security clearances (FCLs) for defense contractors performing on all DoD classified contracts, to include contractors performing on DoD SAPs.' Facility clearance issuance is NOT carved out -- only inspection, IS authorization and CI cross-sharing are. A carved-out SAP contractor site still has a DCSA-issued FCL and therefore still exists in DCSA's facility records.
claims.source: https://web.archive.org/web/20191018064106/https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodm/520507_vol1.pdf

claims.text: DoDI 5205.11 para 1.2.i: 'Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversight for the administration of the National Industrial Security Program will be phased out in July 2029 in accordance with the carve-out provision.'
claims.source: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/520511p.pdf

claims.text: Because the FCL function survives a carve-out (DoDM V1 Encl 2 para 2.b) while inspection does not, DCSA's facility clearance database remains the one government-wide index that lists a carved-out SAP contractor location as a cleared facility, even when no inspector may enter it. That makes FCL records a discovery surface that the carve-out does not close. Reasoning stated.

entities.label: Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC)
entities.sub: oversight-body
entities.desc: The SAPOC was established on 5 January 1994, not in 2010. A Deputy Secretary of Defense information bulletin of November 1994 records that 'On January 5th, 1994, the Deputy Secretary of Defense (DEPSECDEF) significantly enhanced changes in the DoD Special Access Program (SAP) management and control structures' and that the plan 'standardized and formalized the SAP approval, termination, revalidation and restructuring process through the Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC). A Senior Review Group (SRG) was established to support the SAPOC principals'; the Joint Security Commission called it a 'recent formation' on 28 February 1994. DoD Directive 5205.07 of 1 July 2010 is therefore a later instrument that re-established a committee which had been running for sixteen years, and it survives in the 12 September 2024 reissue as 'the senior governing body of the DoD SAP Enterprise'. Under the 2013 instruction its chair is the Deputy Secretary of Defense, its vice-chair the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics, and its executive secretary the Director of DoD SAPCO; its general membership is the Under Secretaries for Policy, Comptroller/CFO, Intelligence, and Personnel and Readiness, the Vice Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, the DoD Chief Information Officer, the General Counsel of the Department, the Director of Cost Assessment and Program Evaluation, the Under Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force, the Vice Chiefs of Staff of the Army and Air Force, the Vice Chief of Naval Operations and the Assistant Commandant of the Marine Corps. Its three primary functions are to review issues on which the Senior Review Group could not reach unanimity, to ensure combatant command warfighting needs are reflected in SAP programmatics and budgets, and - the function that matters here - to 'Conduct an annual review and validation of SAP reports sent to the Congressional defense and intelligence committees'. In other words, the document Congress receives about special access programs is written and validated by a committee of roughly eighteen senior officials of the Department the report is about, chaired by the same official who signs the carve-outs. This is the body whose membership a witness alleging concealment would have to say was either complicit or itself deceived; DoD's own directive makes that a binary with no third option.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 113 of 1170, score 58). 5 connections, 0 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C2/A3/D1.

claims.text: A central Army special-access oversight office predates the 1994 reform by ten years. GAO/NSIAD-88-152 records: 'A DOD review of Army special access programs in 1983 revealed systemic weaknesses in various management areas, which resulted in establishment of a central oversight office in September 1984.' The same report states that in 1988 'The Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Policy is required to maintain a listing of all special access programs, but does not do so because of security concerns', and that 'the Secretary's Office has no centralized office with cognizance of all special access programs'. The January 1994 dates this board carries stand; the Army aftermath began in 1983-84.
claims.source: GAO/NSIAD-88-152, B-230522, 24 May 1988, Results in Brief and Recommendations, https://www.gao.gov/assets/nsiad-88-152.pdf

claims.text: The committee was established on 5 January 1994, sixteen years before the directive this node cites. A Deputy Secretary of Defense information bulletin of November 1994 states: 'On January 5th, 1994, the Deputy Secretary of Defense (DEPSECDEF) significantly enhanced changes in the DoD Special Access Program (SAP) management and control structures. ... The plan standardized and formalized the SAP approval, termination, revalidation and restructuring process through the Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC). A Senior Review Group (SRG) was established to support the SAPOC principals.' The DEPSECDEF is the final decision maker in establishing, disestablishing or restructuring SAPs.'

Owens, VCJCS, and the Honorable Emmett Paige Jr., ASD(C3I). BGEN Mike Kostelnik, OUSD(A&T), serves as both member and executive secretary to the SAPOC in his capacity as director of the SAPCO (SAP Coordinating Office). entities.label: Senior Review Group (DoD SAP governance)
entities.sub: oversight-body
entities.desc: The Senior Review Group is described in DoDI 5205.11 as 'the principal working-level body executing the governance process and performing oversight and management of DoD SAPs', and its unanimous recommendations 'may be forwarded directly to the DepSecDef for decision' - bypassing the SAPOC entirely. It is chaired by the Principal Deputy Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition, Technology and Logistics, vice-chaired by the Director of DoD SAPCO and with the Deputy Director of DoD SAPCO as executive secretary; its members are the primary or alternate representatives designated in writing by each SAPOC member, with the Army, Navy and Air Force each casting a single vote. It convenes at the direction of the Deputy Secretary to review proposals to establish or disestablish SAPs, designate cognizant and oversight authorities, remove DoD programs from special access controls, apportion SAPs into and out of integrated joint special technical operations, alter the scope, category or type of a SAP, approve the use of DoD resources to support DoD and non-DoD SAPs, and review foreign access and participation. Two of its enumerated functions are decisive for this board: it 'Reviews all waived DoD SAPs annually' and provides recommendations on continued waived status, and it 'Ensures the accuracy of the SAP list submitted to Congress prior to submission of the SAP annual report'. If a waived program existed that was not on the list submitted to Congress, the SRG is the body that would have had to certify a list it knew to be incomplete - or the body from which the program was itself concealed.

Under Bigelow the property became the field site of the National Institute for Discovery Science, whose investigators included retired Army Col. John B. Alexander and biochemist Colm A. entities.label: KONA BLUE
entities.sub: Proposed DHS special access program, circa 2011
entities.desc: Kona Blue was a Department of Homeland Security prospective special access programme, terminated on 10 February 2012, intended to house UAP recovery and reverse-engineering work after the DIA's AAWSAP/AATIP funding lapsed. AARO surfaced it in the Historical Record Report Volume I and DHS declassified the associated records; on 5 February 2024 DHS Acting Deputy Secretary Kristie Canegallo transmitted them to the Deputy Secretary of Defense, with strike-through formatting preserving the former classification marks and a records search finding no further material. The documents were made public in June 2024. AARO's framing is that Kona Blue was rejected by DHS leadership as lacking merit and that it is the proximate origin of the modern belief in a crash-retrieval programme - people who saw the Kona Blue proposal, on this account, mistook a proposal for an existing capability. The record is more interesting than the framing. A prospective special access programme is a real, chartered vehicle, and the surviving text discusses protection rationales for sensitive personnel and exotic technologies. The federal government did not draft a SAP charter to house nothing; it drafted one because named officials with clearances believed there was something to house, and the charter reached the Acting Deputy Secretary level of DHS before it was killed. AARO uses Kona Blue as a debunking device; on its face it is documentary evidence that in 2011-2012 senior officials at two departments treated recovered exotic material as a programme-management problem.

entities.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters
entities.sub: Executive disclosure channel announced Feb 2026; first drop 8 May 2026
entities.desc: PURSUE is the Department of War's UAP declassification release programme, published at war.gov/UFO and coordinated with ODNI. Its name is confirmed on AARO's own homepage, which links to the war.gov portal - the statutory UAP office pointing away from itself to a release channel it does not run. PURSUE stands on President Trump's 19-20 February 2026 Truth Social direction to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and other relevant departments and agencies to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. Five tranches were published between 8 May and 7 August 2026: R01 on 8 May (160 files - 117 PDFs, 29 sensor videos, 14 photographs - spanning 1944 to 2026, documents bundle 1.2GB, video bundle 1.3GB); R02 on 22 May (64 files including 51 sensor videos in a DOW-UAP-PR050 to PR099 series, 7 NASA crew audio files, 6 documents; video bundle 5.6GB); R03 on 12 June (72 files - 53 documents, 10 images, 6 videos, 3 audio - with FBI records dominating at 29 files); R04 on 10 July (documents 227MB, videos 1.4GB, spanning the 1940s to 2026); and R05 on 7 August (41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - spanning 1953 to 2026 per the portal, with content reaching back to a 1950 Montana case). Files carry structured identifiers - DOW-UAP-PRxxx for imagery, DOW-UAP-Dxxx for documents, ODNI-UAP-Dxxx and FBI-UAP-Dxxx for agency-originated material - which is the first time the US Government has issued UAP material under a single public numbering scheme. The Department's declared posture is total non-assessment: 'We are not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file, so that the American people can make up their own minds regarding the files.' That posture is the programme's defining feature and its defining defect. It released the imagery and withheld the physics: no coordinates, no sensor parameters, no altitude, no chain of custody. At least 100 of the 160 files in R01 carried redactions. PURSUE is nonetheless the strategic fact of 2026. The declassification AARO spent four years explaining was impossible was executed over the office's head, by the Secretary of War, at the President's direction, five weeks after a subcommittee chair wrote demanding AARO's video holdings.

entities.desc: On 8 May 2026 the Department of War announced a release of files relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena, and Senator Gillibrand issued a statement the same day. Her framing is the important part, because she is the author of the surviving statute: she called it 'another important step' while insisting there is 'much more work to do' and committing to 'fight to ensure the administration finally meets its legal obligation to the American people.' The word 'finally' is doing considerable work — it is a sitting senator stating, on her own Senate press page, that the executive branch has not been meeting an existing legal obligation. That obligation is Sections 1841-1843 of P.L. 118-31, whose agency-review deadline expired on 17 October 2024, some nineteen months before this release. The release is therefore best read on this board not as compliance but as discretionary executive action taken in the space left by a statute with no enforcement mechanism — precisely the space created when the Review Board was removed in conference.

entities.label: ADAM Research Project (Acquisition and Data Analysis of Materials)
entities.sub: TTSA materials program run with EarthTech International
entities.desc: The ADAM Research Project is the only publicly documented attempt to move alleged UAP material from private hands into a formal government research relationship, and it is a case study in what a broken chain of custody looks like. To The Stars Academy announced in July 2019 that it had acquired and was studying 'potentially exotic materials'. Its COO Steve Justice - former director of Advanced Systems at Lockheed Martin's Skunk Works - said 'the structure and composition of these materials are not from any known existing military or commercial application' and, with unusual candour, that the materials 'have been collected from sources with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation, so we are focusing on verifiable facts and working to develop independent scientific proof of the materials' properties and attributes.' SEC filings record TTSA paying $35,000 for several items including six pieces of bismuth/magnesium-zinc metal and a piece of aluminium. Those samples had previously been retained and studied by ufologist Linda Moulton Howe, who says she had them tested by the Carnegie Institution's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism in 1996 and subsequently by Harold Puthoff on several occasions. A 2012 letter from Puthoff reported that the tests had not proved alien origin nor produced any 'interesting/anomalous outcome', with one further test outstanding for want of specialised equipment. TTSA then partnered with laboratories founded by Puthoff to continue the work, and on 17 October 2019 entered a five-year cooperative research and development agreement with the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command covering inertial mass reduction, mechanical and structural metamaterials, electromagnetic metamaterial waveguides, quantum physics, quantum communications and beamed energy propulsion. No analytical results have been published. Chemists including Richard Sachleben and May Nyman have said any unknown alloy would be identified within hours at any competent laboratory; Chris Cogswell suggested the bismuth/magnesium-zinc pieces are Betterton-Kroll process slag.

entities.label: CRADA between U.S. Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center and To The Stars Academy
entities.sub: Cooperative Research and Development Agreement, signed 10 October 2019
entities.desc: This is the hardest artifact in the domain: an executed federal research instrument binding the United States Army to a company that publicly claimed custody of material from a vehicle of unknown origin. Signed on 10 October 2019 by Jeffery Langhout, Director of the Army Ground Vehicle Systems Center, and Kari DeLonge for TTSA, and announced on 17 October 2019, it named Bean Soave and Dr. Joseph Cannon as government principal investigators and Luis Elizondo, as TTSA's Director of Global Security & Special Programs, as the collaborator principal investigator. The stated research areas are 'inertial mass reduction, mechanical/structural meta materials, electromagnetic meta material wave guides, quantum physics, quantum communications, and beamed energy propulsion', with 'Active Camouflage' and 'Directed Photon Projection' named as applications. The document runs to 30 September 2023 with annual intellectual property reviews and estimates the value of TTSA's participation at $1 million in in-kind contributions; the Army provided laboratories, expertise and resources reported at not less than $750,000 in value. The Army released the agreement itself on 18 October 2019 but on 21 February 2020 denied in full a FOIA request for the associated correspondence — twenty-nine emails, one hundred pages — under exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5). No technical results have ever been published.

entities.sub: 'Analysis of Reports of Unidentified Aerial Objects', Project No. 10073, 5 May 1955; prepared by Battelle Memorial Institute
entities.desc: The largest statistical study of UFO reports ever conducted by or for the United States government. Prepared by Battelle Memorial Institute under Project Stork and issued 5 May 1955 as Project No. 10073, it analysed roughly 3,200 reports, classified them by quality of evidence, and applied chi-square testing to determine whether the 'unknowns' were statistically distinguishable from the 'knowns'. They were. The report also found - and this is the part the Air Force's public summary buried - that the proportion of unknowns rose with the quality of the sighting: the better the observation, the less likely it was to be explained. The Air Force publicised the study as demonstrating that UFOs were of no consequence. The document itself does not support that reading. It is available today through CIA's CREST reading room as CIA-RDP81R00560R000100060001-5 and was re-released by the Department of War in PURSUE Release 03 in June 2026 as CIA-UAP-015 - meaning the government has now published the same 1955 Battelle report three separate times across seventy years while the underlying case data has never been reanalysed by an independent party. As an artifact this document is doubly useful: it is evidence about the phenomenon, and it is evidence about how a contractor's technical work is converted into an official denial.

Its central record - a complaint-form entry dated 10 November 1980 - documents that Kirtland security police observed unexplained aerial objects over the Coyote Canyon and Manzano Weapons Storage Area, the nuclear-weapons storage complex on the base's eastern edge, and notes the reporting and photographic activity of the Albuquerque physicist Paul Bennewitz. The file matters for two independent reasons. First, it is an official Air Force counterintelligence concession that unidentified objects were seen over a nuclear weapons storage site in 1980, eleven years after the Air Force publicly stopped investigating such things. Second, it is the entry point of an operation: the agent associated with the file, Richard Doty, subsequently supplied Bennewitz with fabricated material, showed a purported classified briefing paper to the documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe, and was linked to the channel through which the MJ-12 material reached Bill Moore and Jaime Shandera. The file has never been the subject of any published official review. AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report Volume I does not mention Kirtland, AFOSI, Bennewitz or Doty.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded B on a global pass (rank 217 of 1170, score 44). 6 connections, 2 of them custody/funding/programmatic. Axes C2/A2/D3.

entities.label: The Wilson-Davis Notes (16 October 2002)
entities.sub: Fifteen handwritten pages by Eric W. Davis of a conversation with VADM Thomas R. Wilson (ret.)
entities.desc: Fifteen typed pages headed 'EWD NOTES', made by the astrophysicist Eric W. Davis on 16 October 2002, recording what retired Vice Admiral Thomas R. Wilson - former Joint Staff J-2 and, until months earlier, Director of the Defense Intelligence Agency - told him at a meeting reported to have taken place at an EG&G facility in Las Vegas; two of the fifteen pages, numbered 3 and 4, are not Davis's notes at all but a paper-clipped letter from Will Miller on United States Navy letterhead dated 25 April 2002, flagged in the notes themselves at the foot of page 2 as '[paper-clipped letter here]'. The notes describe Wilson learning in 1997 of a special access programme holding recovered material of non-human origin in the custody of an aerospace contractor; obtaining a meeting with the programme's gatekeepers, described as a programme security officer, a contractor programme manager and a lawyer; and being refused the read-on because he lacked need-to-know. The notes surfaced publicly in 2019 from material connected to the estate of Apollo 14 astronaut Edgar Mitchell. Davis has confirmed the notes are his. Wilson denies the meeting and its substance. Members of the House Intelligence subcommittee raised the memo directly with Pentagon witnesses at the 17 May 2022 UAP hearing and were told the witnesses were unaware of it. No official US government publication - including AARO's 2024 Historical Record Report Volume I - has ever addressed the document. The board records it in full because its central mechanism (a cleared senior official refused access by contractor gatekeepers) is the same mechanism sworn to by David Grusch in July 2023, and because a document whose author is alive and identified and whose subject is alive and identified is a resolvable question that no institution has chosen to resolve.

entities.label: UAP Science Advisory Council
entities.sub: ODNI/FBI advisory body, est. 2026
entities.desc: Announced on 15 June 2026, the UAP Science Advisory Council is the first standing outside scientific advisory body the US government has assembled on this subject. It was, per the Skeptics Society announcement, 'formed at the request of the White House and in coordination with the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO), the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI), the FBI, and other agencies'. Avi Loeb chairs it. Loeb's own Medium account of 29 June 2026 says 'over the past week, I was tasked by the above organizations to create a research team', naming the White House, AARO, ODNI, the FBI and all Intelligence Community members, and identifies a core team of Richard Cloete (data analysis and AI), Regina Sarmiento (data management with AI), Matthew Szydagis (instrumentation and data collection), Devesh Nandal (numerical analysis and astrophysics) and Omer Eldadi (data management, AI and human psychology). The Skeptics Society listed eleven members including Tim Gallaudet, Garry Nolan, Peter Skafish, Michael Shermer and Jennice Vilhauer; The Sol Foundation described a fourteen-member council reporting to a higher-level UAP Governance Board coordinating across military, law enforcement and intelligence agencies, with all shared data unclassified; the statistician Liberty Vittert was also appointed. The Associated Press reported on 30 June 2026 that the council has no budget and no access to classified material, and The Guardian reported that scientific observers regarded the membership as 'apparently similar minds'. Two things about it matter for this board. First, its personnel came almost entirely from the private technical layer this domain catalogues - Sol, Galileo, UAPx - rather than from federal laboratories or FFRDCs. Second, a body with no money and no clearances cannot examine recovered material, cannot audit a special access programme, and cannot compel anything: it is an advisory council constituted to advise on the unclassified record, which is the part of the record nobody disputes.
entities.tierRationale: Re-graded A on a global pass (rank 49 of 1170, score 82). 17 connections, 1 of them custody/funding/programmatic, 2 official denials recorded against it. Axes C0/A1/D3.

entities.label: McDonnell Douglas Corporation
entities.sub: Prime contractor 1967-1997; Astronautics Company, Huntington Beach
entities.desc: McDonnell Douglas is the earliest documented case of a prime contractor studying the phenomenon on its own money. Robert M. Wood, a Cornell physics PhD who spent his career at the company's Astronautics division in Southern California, ran a company-funded study of unidentified craft and their propulsion out of the Huntington Beach facility in the late 1960s. The rationale he has described is the commercial one and it is the rationale that makes this domain coherent: if the propulsion were real, an aerospace prime could not afford to be the last to know. Nothing about that study was reported to Congress, because nothing required it to be - it was internal corporate research, the same category that DoD Instruction 3204.01 would later formalise as independent research and development, recoverable as an indirect expense on government contracts, and that David Grusch would name under oath in 2023 as the mechanism by which UAP work is funded outside oversight. The company merged into Boeing in 1997. No McDonnell Douglas internal record of the study has been released, and the corporate archive of the Huntington Beach organisation has never been searched by any congressional committee.

entities.label: DoD Instruction 3204.01 - Oversight of Independent Research and Development
entities.sub: The IR&D cost-allowability policy named in statute
entities.desc: DoDI 3204.01 is the policy that makes the funding allegation legally coherent. It establishes that contractor independent research and development costs 'will be allowable as indirect expenses on covered contracts to the extent they are allocable and reasonable' - that is, a defense contractor's self-directed research is reimbursed by the taxpayer through contract overhead. Reporting obligations attach only to major contractors allocating more than $11 million in IR&D and bid-and-proposal costs, and consist of project summaries submitted to a Defense Innovation Marketplace portal for contracting officer and DCAA review of cost allowability, not of program disclosure to Congress. David Grusch named this exact mechanism under oath on 26 July 2023 - 'Correct, through something called IR&D... IR&D is literally internal to the contractors' - and Congress named the instruction by number, date and change number in NDAA FY2024 Sec. 1687(b) five months later, making UAP-related IR&D unallowable as an indirect expense unless disclosed to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership. A statute does not cite an accounting instruction by its change date unless someone has explained precisely how it is being used.

entities.desc: The first tranche, published 8 May 2026: 117 PDFs, 29 sensor videos and 14 photographs, 160 files in total, spanning 1944 to 2026, distributed as a 1.2GB document bundle and a 1.3GB video bundle. At least 100 of the files carried redactions. Its contents cut across seven decades and at least four agencies: the FBI's master flying-disc file 62-HQ-83894 covering 1947 to 1968 as a single 101MB PDF; Apollo 12 and Apollo 17 mission records including cockpit transcript describing 'very bright particles or fragments'; DOW-UAP-PR038, an infrared 'eight-pointed star' formation over a Middle Eastern theatre in 2013; DOW-UAP-PR028, a diamond-shaped object over Greece in January 2024 visible only on infrared; DOW-UAP-PR034, an object executing multiple 90-degree turns over the Aegean in October 2023; FBI infrared imagery of objects over the western United States in September and December 2025; a September 2023 western-US event in which seven federal employees reported orbs and a 'translucent kite'; an FBI bronze-ellipsoid case from September 2023 with multiple credentialed witnesses at a US test site; and a 2026 US Army sensor report of a North American sighting. That last item is the one that most cleanly breaks the historical framing: the tranche is not an archive dump, it contains current-year military sensor material. DNI Tulsi Gabbard described the release as an ongoing joint effort across intelligence and defence agencies.

An ODNI-numbered operational account of an unresolved encounter by a serving officer is a category of document the intelligence community had never previously published. The submarine and Reaper sequences are the two items in the entire PURSUE corpus that most directly implicate transmedium behaviour and weapons-system-grade tracking, and both were released without sensor parameters.

entities.sub: 12 June 2026; 72 files; FBI-dominated
entities.desc: Published 12 June 2026: 72 files comprising 53 documents, 10 images, 6 videos and 3 audio files, with FBI records the single largest contributor at 29 files.
