It carries the same approval date as the Atomic Energy Act of 1946 at 60 Stat. 755, not a date two days later.
timeline.source: An Act to establish an Office of Naval Research in the Department of the Navy, Public Law 79-588, 60 Stat. 779, approved 1 August 1946, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg779.pdf

timeline.label: Atomic Energy Act of 1946 makes classification a property of a category
timeline.text: Public Law 79-585, 60 Stat. 755, chapter 724, S. 1717, is approved. Section 10(b)(1) defines restricted data as all data concerning the manufacture or utilization of atomic weapons, the production of fissionable material or its use in the production of power, excluding only what the Commission affirmatively determines may be published. Section 2(a) establishes the Atomic Energy Commission, section 9(a) transfers the Manhattan Engineer District's holdings to it, section 10(b)(4) reaches concealment and destruction with a capital penalty, and section 10(b)(5)(C) gives the FBI exclusive jurisdiction over violations.
timeline.source: Atomic Energy Act of 1946, Public Law 79-585, 60 Stat. 755, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/STATUTE-60/pdf/STATUTE-60-Pg755.pdf

timeline.label: The Armed Forces Special Weapons Project takes effect, holding the military half of the Manhattan Project
timeline.text: AFSWP is established by joint directive of the Secretaries of War and the Navy 'effective as of midnight 31 December 1946', operating directly under the Army Chief of Staff and the Chief of Naval Operations and responsible for carrying on the military service functions of the Manhattan Project retained under armed forces control. The founding memorandum is signed on 29 January 1947 by Robert P. Patterson and James V. Forrestal; Major General Leslie R. Groves becomes first Chief on 28 February 1947. Its funds come by working fund advances from the Atomic Energy Commission out of money formerly available to the Manhattan Project.
timeline.source: War Department Memorandum No. 850-25-8, 18 March 1947, reproduced in Appendix D of Defense's Nuclear Agency 1947-1997, DTIC ADA412977, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA412977/DTIC_ADA412977_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Kenneth Arnold sighting
timeline.text: Boise pilot Kenneth Arnold reports nine objects near Mount Rainier. Wire coverage coins 'flying saucer' and the national wave begins.

timeline.label: Brazel reports the Foster Ranch debris
timeline.text: Mac Brazel reports the debris to Chaves County Sheriff George Wilcox, who calls Roswell Army Air Field. Maj. Jesse Marcel of the 509th Bomb Group and Capt. Sheridan Cavitt of the CIC are sent to retrieve it.

timeline.label: RAAF announces possession of a disc
timeline.text: Roswell Army Air Field's information office states that the intelligence office of the 509th Bomb Group has gained possession of a disc. The 509th is the only atomic-armed combat group in the world.

timeline.label: Ramey retracts the same day
timeline.text: Brig. Gen. Roger Ramey displays weather balloon and radar target material at Fort Worth and identifies it as the recovered object. The FBI's Dallas office records the same account by teletype.

timeline.label: RAAF announces a disc, and takes it back the same day
timeline.text: 1st Lt. Walter Haut issues the 'flying disc' release; within hours Brig. Gen. Roger Ramey presents the material at Fort Worth as a weather balloon. The Air Force will concede in 1994 that the balloon statement was a cover story.

timeline.label: RAAF press release
timeline.text: Walter Haut, public information officer of the 509th Bomb Group, writes and distributes the release announcing that Roswell Army Air Field has come into possession of a flying disc, naming Maj. Jesse Marcel Sr. as the recovering officer. Fort Worth retracts it the same day.

timeline.label: Roswell announces, Fort Worth retracts
timeline.text: Roswell Army Air Field publicly announces that the 509th Bomb Group has come into possession of a flying disc. The material is flown to Eighth Air Force headquarters at Fort Worth, where it is presented to the press the same day as a weather balloon and radar target. Four official explanations for the event will follow over the next fifty years.

timeline.label: Research and Development Board established
timeline.text: The National Security Act of 1947 (61 Stat. 495) creates the Research and Development Board, the statutory coordinating body for defence research. Truman appoints Vannevar Bush its chairman, continuing him from the Joint Research and Development Board the service secretaries had set up after V-J Day.

timeline.label: The National Security Act creates the NSC and the CIA
timeline.text: Public Law 80-253, 61 Stat. 495. Section 101 creates the National Security Council; section 102(a) establishes the Central Intelligence Agency under it. Section 102(d)(5), permitting such other functions related to intelligence as the Council may direct, will be the authority for the covert-action charters of 1948 and 1954. The Act creates the National Military Establishment, not the Department of Defense; that renaming comes in 1949.

timeline.label: National Security Act signed
timeline.text: President Truman signs the National Security Act of 1947, creating the Central Intelligence Agency, the National Security Council and an independent Air Force. The entire institutional architecture within which the UAP record would be created and concealed comes into being seventeen days after the Roswell press release.

timeline.label: US Air Force established
timeline.text: The Air Force becomes an independent service and inherits the flying disc problem, Wright Field, and the Air Materiel Command intelligence apparatus that would run SIGN, GRUDGE and BLUE BOOK.

timeline.label: Twining memo
timeline.text: Lt. Gen. Nathan Twining writes that 'the phenomenon reported is something real and not visionary or fictitious', and directs consideration of a 'high security project' unknown to his own command.

timeline.label: Schulgen collection memorandum distributed
timeline.text: Air Force intelligence tasks worldwide collectors on disc-type craft, listing near-hover capability, extreme light weight construction and 'Nuclear propulsion (atomic energy)'.

timeline.label: Project SIGN directed
timeline.text: On Twining's recommendation the Air Force establishes its first official UFO project inside Air Materiel Command intelligence at Wright Field. It begins operating 23 January 1948.

timeline.label: Wright-Patterson and Kirtland are both constituted
timeline.text: On the same day the Air Force formally establishes Wright-Patterson AFB, the address of foreign materiel exploitation, and Kirtland AFB, the nuclear weapons and directed energy complex inside Albuquerque.

timeline.label: Edgar Albert Fouche born, Americus, Georgia
timeline.text: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, citing an obituary from Mason Funeral Home, gives the birth date and birthplace. The Library of Congress name authority attached to LCCN 98002961 independently gives 'Fouche, Edgar Rothschild, 1948-'.
timeline.source: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/180498305/edgar-albert-fouch%C3%A9 ; Library of Congress SRU record LCCN 98002961, http://lx2.loc.gov:210/lcdb

timeline.label: RAND incorporated as an independent nonprofit
timeline.text: RAND separates from Douglas Aircraft and incorporates as a nonprofit, establishing the legal template: permanent, sole-source, answerable to a military customer, outside the civil service.

timeline.label: Estimate of the Situation written and destroyed
timeline.text: Project SIGN staff conclude the objects are interplanetary. Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Hoyt Vandenberg rejects the estimate for lacking proof and orders copies destroyed. The Condon Report records this twenty years later.

timeline.label: Scully's Variety columns
timeline.text: Frank Scully publishes two Variety columns describing a recovered saucer and dead occupants, sourced to Silas M. Newton and Leo A. Gebauer.

timeline.label: Project SIGN becomes Project GRUDGE
timeline.text: The successor project concludes reports are misinterpretation, mass hysteria and hoaxes posing no direct threat to national security, and recommends reducing the scope of investigation.

timeline.label: Los Alamos green fireballs conference
timeline.text: Laboratory Director Norris Bradbury, Edward Teller and Frederick Reines meet at Los Alamos with FBI, AEC and military representatives on the green fireballs over the New Mexico nuclear complex. LANL still holds the minutes.

timeline.label: Los Alamos green fireball conference
timeline.text: AEC and Air Force personnel, with Edward Teller and Lincoln LaPaz, meet at Los Alamos over the green fireball incursions above the atomic complex. The Department of Energy's institutional predecessor is in the UAP record from the first decade.

timeline.label: Nuclear scientists meet at Los Alamos about the green fireballs
timeline.text: Edward Teller and Lincoln LaPaz attend a conference on the anomalous objects over northern New Mexico's nuclear installations. LANL's own account records the phenomenon was ultimately dismissed as a national security threat.

timeline.label: CIA Act of 1949 creates unvouchered spending
timeline.text: Section 8 of the Central Intelligence Agency Act, now 50 U.S.C. 3510(b), permits Agency sums to be 'expended without regard to the provisions of law and regulations relating to the expenditure of Government funds', with confidential, extraordinary or emergency objects 'accounted for solely on the certificate of the Director'. The oldest and bluntest black-budget instrument in American law, enacted two years after Roswell and never narrowed.

timeline.label: Project Twinkle established
timeline.text: A network of green fireball observation and photographic stations is stood up over New Mexico. It is never fully implemented and produces no conclusive result.

timeline.label: Behind the Flying Saucers
timeline.text: Henry Holt publishes Scully's book: a 99-foot disc, sixteen bodies, Hart Canyon near Aztec, March 1948. It becomes a bestseller and supplies the genre's narrative furniture.

timeline.label: Guy Hottel FBI memorandum
timeline.text: The special agent in charge of the FBI Washington Field Office records a third-hand account of three 50-foot circular craft recovered in New Mexico, each with three three-foot occupants in metallic cloth, attributed to high-powered radar interference. The memo closes: 'No further evaluation was attempted.'

timeline.label: Smith writes the 'Geo-Magnetics' memorandum
timeline.text: Wilbert Brockhouse Smith, Senior Radio Engineer of the Canadian Department of Transport, writes a Top Secret memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications recording what he had been told in Washington: that the flying saucer question was the most highly classified subject in the United States government, rating higher than the H-bomb, and was being worked by a small group headed by Vannevar Bush. Library and Archives Canada quotes the same memorandum's operative line: 'the correlation between our basic theory and the available information on saucers checks too closely to be mere coincidence'.

timeline.label: A foreign official records the American classification level
timeline.text: Wilbert B. Smith, a radio engineer in Canada's Department of Transport, writes an internal memorandum to the Controller of Telecommunications stating that the flying saucer subject is classified higher in the United States than the hydrogen bomb and that a small group is studying it. Its evidentiary value is its provenance: a foreign government official reporting internally, not a claimant addressing the public.

timeline.label: Project Magnet approved
timeline.text: The Canadian Department of Transport approves Smith's request. Project Magnet is the first government programme anywhere whose stated purpose includes applying recovered UAP data to practical engineering.

timeline.label: MIT Lincoln Laboratory established
timeline.text: Lincoln Laboratory is created to build SAGE, the first continental air defence system - the architecture that determines what American airspace surveillance is built to see.

timeline.label: Battelle contracted to Project GRUDGE
timeline.text: Capt. Edward Ruppelt creates the contract he calls Project BEAR with the Battelle Memorial Institute to supply scientific support to the Air Force UFO investigation. The first private contractor enters the file.

timeline.label: Truman establishes the Psychological Strategy Board by secret directive
timeline.text: A directive to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense and the Director of Central Intelligence, classified secret, establishes a Board reporting to the National Security Council for the formulation of over-all national psychological objectives, policies and programmes. Its editorial footnote names the first Director: 'Gordon Gray, President of the University of North Carolina and former Secretary of the Army, was appointed Director of the new board.' The same directive forbids the Board and the Director to perform any psychological operations themselves.
timeline.source: Directive by the President to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense (Marshall), and the Director of Central Intelligence (Smith), 4 April 1951, FRUS 1951 vol. I doc. 16, https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1951v01/d16

timeline.label: UK Flying Saucer Working Party reports
timeline.text: Britain's first official body on the question reports and recommends no further investigation - the same self-terminating conclusion Project Condign would reach in 2000.

timeline.label: Project Magnet report recommends acquiring the technology
timeline.text: Smith's report concludes that 'we are forced to the conclusion that the vehicles are probably extra-terrestrial, in spite of our prejudices to the contrary' and recommends 'a substantial effort towards the acquisition of as much as possible of this technology, which would without doubt be of great value to us'.

timeline.label: Battelle contracted for Project Stork
timeline.text: The Air Force outsources the statistical analysis of Project Blue Book's case files to Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, under the codename Project Stork.

timeline.label: Ruppelt briefs the Beacon Hill circle
timeline.text: Blue Book director Edward J. Ruppelt gives a 'flying saucer talk' recorded as AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52 - a briefing into the classified summer study on aerial reconnaissance hosted in the MIT/Lincoln Laboratory complex.

timeline.label: Project Blue Book begins under Ruppelt
timeline.text: Capt. Edward Ruppelt renames and professionalises the project, coining the term 'unidentified flying object' to replace 'flying saucer'.

timeline.label: Project Stork begins
timeline.text: Work begins on Project Stork, designation PPS-100, later carried as contract AF-19741, for the Air Technical Intelligence Center. The first status report of 25 April 1952 describes progress 'from its inception on March 31, 1952'. Seven status reports survive, totalling 107 pages, and the transcribing archive records that further reports referenced in the text are not in NARA custody.

timeline.label: Project Second Storey established
timeline.text: The Defence Research Board establishes a committee under NRC astronomer Peter Millman. It builds a standardised report form with a weighting factor to minimise the 'personal equation', meets six times, concludes UFOs are neither a security threat nor of scientific interest, and recommends ending all Canadian military investigation.

timeline.label: Brown files the application that later becomes US 2,949,550, and abandons it
timeline.text: US 2,949,550 states on its face: 'This invention was disclosed and described in my application Serial No. 293,465, filed June 13, 1952, which application has become abandoned.' This dates the electrokinetic disclosure five years earlier than the filing the board previously recorded as its start.
timeline.source: US Patent 2,949,550, complete 6-page text, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Washington DC radar-visual sightings
timeline.text: Unidentified targets are tracked at Washington National, Andrews AFB and the ARTCC over consecutive July weekends, with visual corroboration and scrambled interceptors.

timeline.label: Chadwell memo to the DCI
timeline.text: CIA's Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence tells the Director that July 1952 produced 250 official reports and that the situation 'contains two elements of danger' with national security implications.

timeline.label: NSA established by classified presidential memorandum
timeline.text: Truman creates the National Security Agency by a memorandum that is itself classified - the first of the two agencies on this board whose existence was a secret.

timeline.label: Newton and Gebauer convicted
timeline.text: Scully's two sources are convicted of fraud after millionaire Herman Flader presses charges over 'doodlebug' devices sold on the claim that they used recovered alien technology.

timeline.label: The Pentacle Memorandum
timeline.text: Battelle's H. C. Cross writes to Miles E. Goll at Wright-Patterson under Project Stork, ref. G-1579-4, SECRET, proposing that 'many different types of aerial activity should be secretly and purposefully scheduled' in areas of high UFO reporting.

timeline.label: Robertson Panel convenes uninformed
timeline.text: The CIA-convened panel meets five days after the Pentacle memorandum. Per Jacques Vallee it is never briefed on the Battelle proposals - a separate body had already fixed the boundaries of what it could consider.

timeline.label: Robertson Panel convenes
timeline.text: A CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence panel sits for four days and recommends stripping UFOs of special status through a mass-media 'debunking' programme, canvassing Disney and the Navy Special Devices Center, and monitoring civilian UFO groups.

timeline.label: Robertson Panel reports
timeline.text: The CIA-convened panel under H. P. Robertson recommends stripping the phenomenon of its 'aura of mystery' through education and debunking, and the monitoring of civilian UFO groups 'because of their potentially great influence on mass thinking'. American UFO information management begins here.

timeline.label: The Robertson Panel recommends a debunking programme
timeline.text: A CIA Office of Scientific Intelligence panel recommends that the national security agencies strip UFOs of their special status through a programme of mass-media 'training and debunking', and that civilian UFO groups be watched because of their potential influence on mass thinking. This is the documented origin point of the psychological-operations domain.

timeline.label: Durant records the proceedings
timeline.text: CIA officer Frederick Durant's memorandum to the Assistant Director for Scientific Intelligence becomes the only substantive account of what the panel actually discussed.

timeline.label: The FBI investigates Project Winterhaven as possible fraud
timeline.text: An FBI report out of Cincinnati records that Thomas Townsend Brown 'is apparently in Washington attempting to obtain a research and development contract for his so-called Project Winterhaven' and 'anticipates a contract of approximately a million dollars'. The Washington Field Office is directed to determine any possible violation of the Fraud Against the Government statute, and to review Brown's patents at the Patent Office.

timeline.label: AFR 200-2 issued
timeline.text: The Air Force regulation on UFO reporting restricts public release on unexplained cases to the bare fact that ATIC will analyse the data. Revised 12 August 1954.

timeline.label: AFR 200-2 puts the release restriction in writing
timeline.text: Air Force Regulation 200-2, short title UFOB, signed by order of the Secretary of the Air Force by N. F. Twining, supersedes AFL 200-5 of 29 April 1952. It designates ATIC as the analysis authority, directs that all evidence be forwarded there, and restricts public discussion to cases conclusively identified as conventional. Identified cases could be discussed; unidentified ones could not.

timeline.label: EO 10501 fixes three classification levels and strips 28 agencies of the power to classify
timeline.text: Eisenhower signs EO 10501, effective 15 December 1953, revoking EO 10290 of 1951. It limits defense-information markings to Top Secret, Secret and Confidential, removes original classification authority entirely from 28 named agencies and limits 17 more to the agency head. Section 13 leaves Atomic Energy Act Restricted Data outside the order, which is where the two classification regimes part company.

timeline.label: JANAP 146(C) issued
timeline.text: Unidentified flying objects become a mandatory CIRVIS report for airborne personnel, with unauthorised disclosure of report contents prohibited under 18 U.S.C. 793 and 794.

timeline.label: NSC 5412 replaces the 1948 covert-action charter
timeline.text: The President approves NSC 5412 the day it is circulated. It supersedes NSC 10/2 and NSC 10/5, keeps the authority in section 102(d)(5), restates the plausible-deniability test almost word for word, and makes the Operations Coordinating Board the normal channel for interagency support. It does not create the Special Group; that comes with NSC 5412/2 in December 1955.

timeline.label: The Atomic Energy Act of 1954 makes Restricted Data an Act-wide statutory category
timeline.text: Public Law 83-703, 68 Stat. 919, a complete restatement of the 1946 Act. The Restricted Data definition moves out of section 10 and into the definitions chapter as a capitalised category, gains the word 'design', and swaps fissionable material and the production of power for special nuclear material and the production of energy. Removal from the category now runs through the formal procedure at section 142. The phrase 'born classified' appears nowhere in the Act.

timeline.label: Atomic Energy Act of 1954
timeline.text: Restricted Data is created as a category classified by statute rather than executive order. Any material placed under this authority becomes permanently beyond the reach of presidential declassification directives.

timeline.label: Battelle's authorship of Special Report No. 14 concealed
timeline.text: Battelle completes the statistical study issued as Special Report No. 14 and, per AARO's own history, 'released a report under the cover of ATIC to maintain its anonymity.' Contractor performs, government takes the byline.

timeline.label: ATIC and WADC report jointly on a disc-shaped supersonic aircraft
timeline.text: TR-AC-47, Project No. 9961, is issued at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base on the Avro Canada Project Y2 flat-riser. Its stated purpose is to correct the distorted picture presented in previous releases and to alert the intelligence community to any Soviet interest, and its Summary says the project should in no way be associated with any science fiction or flying saucer stories because of its external appearance. It was declassified on 29 March 1995.
timeline.source: TR-AC-47, Joint ATIC-WADC Report on Project Silver Bug, 15 February 1955, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SilverBug/AFD-070114-006.pdf

timeline.label: The CIA establishes the Groom Lake facility
timeline.text: Project AQUATONE selects the site because U-2 testing cannot be conducted at Edwards or Palmdale given the secrecy of the project. The first U-2 arrives 24 July 1955.

timeline.label: Blue Book Special Report No. 14 issued
timeline.text: Battelle delivers the largest statistical study of UFO reports ever performed for the US government, Project No. 10073. The proportion of unknowns rises with the quality of the sighting; the Air Force publicises the opposite conclusion.

timeline.label: Blue Book Special Report No. 14
timeline.text: ATIC issues the largest statistical study of UFO reports ever produced by the US government: 434 of 2,199 objects unknown, with unknown rates rising with report quality.

timeline.label: An aerospace prime proposes an institute to study gravity
timeline.text: George S. Trimble of the Glenn L. Martin Company writes to Bryce DeWitt that 'our industry was vitally concerned with gravity' and that respectable researchers 'do not wish to get mixed up in the field of gravity research'. He proposes an 'industrial version of the Institute for Advanced Study'. RIAS, Inc. of Baltimore is the result; Louis Witten is its first researcher.

timeline.label: The Institute of Field Physics is incorporated, with an anti-gravity disclaimer written into its publicity
timeline.text: The Institute receives its certificate of incorporation and is placed inside the physics department at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill under Bryce and Cecile DeWitt, funded principally by Agnew Bahnson. George Trimble and the Glenn L. Martin Company buy a Founder's Membership for 5,000 dollars. On John Wheeler's insistence a Protection Clause is attached to every publicity statement declaring that the work 'has no connection with so-called "anti-gravity research" of whatever kind and for whatever purposes'.
timeline.source: History of the Institute of Field Physics (1955-1959), Dean Rickles, UNC Chapel Hill Department of Physics and Astronomy department history, Section II, https://physics.unc.edu/department-history/section-ii/

timeline.label: NICAP incorporated in the District of Columbia
timeline.text: The National Investigations Committee on Aerial Phenomena states in its own 1964 volume that it is a non-profit organization incorporated in the District of Columbia in 1956. A Washington Daily News report of 23 October 1956, filed in the FBI's NICAP file, records the organisation forming at 1536 Connecticut Avenue NW under T. Townsend Brown of Leesburg, Virginia, executive vice chairman pro tempore, with a nine-man board of governors still to be elected on 1 November. The District's own corporate register was not opened.
timeline.source: The UFO Evidence, NICAP, May 1964, CIA filed copy CIA-RDP81R00560R000100010001-0, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp81r00560r000100010001-0 ; FBI file 100-35992, part 1, https://archive.org/details/NICAP

timeline.label: RIAS at the Chapel Hill gravitation conference
timeline.text: The participants list of the conference on the role of gravitation in physics prints 'Witten, L. | RIAS, Inc., Baltimore' and 'Bass, R.W. | RIAS , Inc., Baltimore'. The conference report is WADC Technical Report 57-216, produced under a funding agreement with the Wright Air Development Center. The participants record their own concern to avoid identification with anti-gravity research.

timeline.label: US 2,949,550 filed, Serial No. 669,830, assigned to Whitehall-Rand Inc
timeline.text: Thomas Townsend Brown of Umatilla, Florida files 'Electrokinetic Apparatus', assignor to Whitehall-Rand, Inc. of Washington D.C., a Delaware corporation. 12 claims, Class 310-5. A private corporate assignee and no government interest statement.
timeline.source: US Patent 2,949,550, printed header block, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: CIA resolves to route Keyhoe's UFO inquiries to the Air Force, and to make it a precedent
timeline.text: A CIA memorandum for record on 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects' notes that the Air Force was 'most insistent' on answering his letters itself, that 'the Air Force is endeavoring to impress upon Major Keyhoe and others in a similar position, that his office is the proper place to come for such information', and concludes: 'I think we can use this procedure as a precedent henceforth in all inquiries regarding UFO's.'
timeline.source: CIA memorandum for record, 'Comments on Letters Dealing with Unidentified Flying Objects', CIA reading room document 0005516043, reading-room date 4 April 1958, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-0005516043

timeline.label: US 3,187,206 filed, Serial No. 734,342, assigned to Electrokinetics Inc
timeline.text: Thomas Townsend Brown of Walkertown, North Carolina files the second 'Electrokinetic Apparatus', assignor by mesne assignments to Electrokinetics, Inc., a Pennsylvania corporation. 23 claims, Class 310-5.
timeline.source: US Patent 3,187,206, printed header block, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/fd/fa/17/a3da8c41817315/US3187206.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: MITRE incorporated
timeline.text: The MITRE Corporation is incorporated as a nonprofit, taking Robert Everett and 485 Lincoln Laboratory staff to continue SAGE systems engineering under Air Force sponsorship rather than university administration.

timeline.label: Canada-US joint UFO reporting system
timeline.text: Library and Archives Canada records that an agreement was finalised between the United States and Canada to institute a joint reporting system for UFOs under CIRVIS/MERINT, 'to extend the early warning coverage for the defence of North America'. Posters depicted a saucer-like object alongside missiles and submarines as examples of objects to be reported.

timeline.label: A Study of Lunar Research Flights delivered to the Air Force Special Weapons Center
timeline.text: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, by L. Reiffel of the Armour Research Foundation with contributions including C. E. Sagan, is dated 19 June 1959 under Contract AF 29(601)-1164. Its introduction states that the motivation for detonating a nuclear weapon on or near the Moon is threefold, scientific, military and political, and that positive effects would accrue to the nation first performing the feat. Copies went to ARPA at the Pentagon, to the AEC for the Division of Military Application, to Sandia, to Los Alamos, to the Lawrence Radiation Laboratory and to WADD at Wright-Patterson. The string A119 appears nowhere in it.
timeline.source: AFSWC TR-59-39 Vol I, DDC AD 425380, https://archive.org/details/DTIC_AD0425380

timeline.label: JASON established under IDA administration
timeline.text: The government's standing panel of elite scientists is created - and housed inside an FFRDC operator rather than inside the government. It has never been anywhere else since.

timeline.label: The first DCI asks Congress to investigate
timeline.text: A Worcester Gazette report, filed in CIA records and released in 2014, quotes Adm. Roscoe H. Hillenkoetter, DCI from May 1947 to October 1950: 'The unknown objects are operating under intelligent control. It is imperative that we learn where the UFO's come from and what their purpose is.' He is by then a NICAP board member and has referred his conclusions to the Senate Space Committee.

timeline.label: The Aerospace Corporation founded
timeline.text: Announced by Lt. Gen. Bernard Schriever, Aerospace is created to provide dedicated technical planning for military space and ballistic missile programmes, with charter restrictions the Air Force had not imposed on earlier FFRDCs.

timeline.label: US 2,949,550 granted. The word 'gravity' appears zero times in it
timeline.text: Claim 1 as granted: 'Thrust producing apparatus comprising an electroconductive body having a relatively large, substantially smooth area thereof exposed to the surrounding medium, an electrode supported on said body, insulated therefrom and shaped to produce a concentrated electrostatic field when electrically charged with respect to said body, and power means connected between said body and electrode to impress high voltage thereon whereby to cause relative movement of an ionizable dielectric medium surrounding said electrodes.' Word counts over all six pages: gravity 0, anti-gravity 0, levitation 0, electrogravitics 0.
timeline.source: US Patent 2,949,550, complete 6-page text, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/20/38/0f/252396dd3aadcb/US2949550.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: MOON DUST / BLUE FLY stood up
timeline.text: The Air Force establishes a named worldwide capability to collect and exploit unidentified objects and debris surviving re-entry, with a quick-reaction airlift arm routing material to technical intelligence at Wright-Patterson.

timeline.label: ATIC is discontinued and the Foreign Technology Division is constituted the same day
timeline.text: The Air Force organizational-history record gives a discontinuation and a new constitution rather than a renaming: 'Air Technical Intelligence Center established 21 May 1951; redesignated Aerospace Technical Intelligence Center, 21 September 1959; discontinued 1 July 1961. Foreign Technology Division constituted, activated, and organized 1 July 1961', with the mission and resources absorbed by FTD on that date. The board's prose in more than one node says ATIC 'became' FTD; the record calls it a discontinuation and an absorption. Carried at Tier 2 because the compilation is a private site citing the Air Force Historical Research Agency, whose own pages return 403 to this environment.
timeline.source: AEROSPACE TECHNICAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER, Department of the Air Force Organizational Histories compilation, sourced to the Air Force Historical Research Agency, https://www.usafunithistory.com/PDF/A-E/AEROSPACE%20TECHNICAL%20INTELLIGENCE%20CENTER.pdf

timeline.label: NRO established as a classified entity
timeline.text: The National Reconnaissance Office is created as a joint DoD-CIA activity under a classified directive. Its existence will be an official secret for the next 31 years - the working proof that concealment at agency scale is achievable.

timeline.label: An agency whose existence is a secret
timeline.text: The National Reconnaissance Office is established with its very existence classified - a status maintained until September 1992. For thirty-one years the legally required answer to whether the organisation existed was no, which is the documented proof that a categorical official denial can be false and lawful at the same time.

timeline.label: The Joint Chiefs forward fabricated pretexts for invading Cuba to the Secretary of Defense
timeline.text: A memorandum for the Secretary of Defense, subject 'Justification for US Military Intervention in Cuba (TS)', serial JCS 1969/321, forwards an annex headed 'PRETEXTS TO JUSTIFY US MILITARY INTERVENTION IN CUBA' and recommends that responsibility for both overt and covert military operations under the resulting plan be assigned to the Joint Chiefs of Staff. It is signed 'For the Joint Chiefs of Staff, L. L. LEMNITZER, Chairman'.
timeline.source: Memorandum for the Secretary of Defense, 13 March 1962, JCS 1969/321, https://archive.org/download/OperationNorthwoods/operation_northwoods_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Corso becomes Chief, Foreign Technology Division, OCRD
timeline.text: Philip J. Corso's own DA Form 66 records him as 'Chief Foreign Technology Div, OCRD USA' from 18 April to 18 July 1962, after a year as a staff officer in the same division. Three months. The same form records him on the Operations Coordinating Board from 1954 to 1957, which his later affidavit describes as membership of the National Security Council.

timeline.label: Bluegill Triple Prime detonates over Johnston Island
timeline.text: The Defense Nuclear Agency's Operation DOMINIC I report records the shot at 25 October 1962, 2359 local, the fourth and first successful attempt to launch the BLUEGILL device on a Thor missile, submegaton, tens of kilometres over Johnston Island, with 22 Air Force aircraft arrayed and nine Navy ships positioned. The report carries no unidentified object, no recovery and no debris, and the photographic aircraft were three KC-135s under the call sign KETTLE.
timeline.source: DNA 6040F, Operation DOMINIC I--1962, Defense Nuclear Agency, https://archive.org/download/DTIC_ADA136820/DTIC_ADA136820_djvu.txt

timeline.label: The Special Group 5412 is renamed the 303 Committee, and nothing else changes
timeline.text: McGeorge Bundy signs a two-sentence National Security Action Memorandum renaming the Special Group 5412 as the 303 Committee, expressly altering nothing about its composition, function or responsibility. It contains no secrecy policy of any kind, which matters because it is routinely cited as though it did.

timeline.label: Atlas launch 'Buzzing Bee' filmed from Big Sur at dawn
timeline.text: The project engineer's published account fixes the event at dawn on 22 September 1964, on an Atlas launch nicknamed 'Buzzing Bee', photographed by a borrowed Boston University 24-inch telescope with an image orthicon tube sited in the Los Padres National Forest above Big Sur. Lt. Robert Jacobs, the on-site commander, later published that the film showed a saucer-shaped object firing a beam at the warhead; the project engineer published that it showed decoy deployment and trailing packing material. Jacobs's own article gives the date as 2, 3 or 15 September 1964.
timeline.source: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Vol. 17, No. 2, Winter 1993, pages 180 to 186; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/1993/01/22165151/p77.pdf

timeline.label: James F. King Jr. files US 3,322,374 from a home address, with no assignee
timeline.text: Serial No. 400,456, filed from 925 Goodwood Road, Winston-Salem, North Carolina. No assignee, no government interest statement and no secrecy order appear anywhere in the document.
timeline.source: US Patent 3,322,374, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/6f/35/54/257dd6cdb01efc/US3322374.pdf , opened 2026-09-18 and recorded in notes/PROPULSION-CLAIMS-2026-09-18.md

timeline.label: Contemporaneous Air Force staff study on the Big Sur imagery
timeline.text: 'Preliminary Report on Image Orthicon Photography from Big Sur', Headquarters 1st Strategic Aerospace Division Operations Analysis Staff Study, 13 October 1964, by Kingston A. George. Cited by title and date in his 1993 article. NOT OPENED. It is the best unopened lead this cluster produced: a contemporaneous Air Force document about the filming, written three weeks afterwards.
timeline.source: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Vol. 17, No. 2, Winter 1993, pages 180 to 186; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/1993/01/22165151/p77.pdf

timeline.label: US 3,187,206 granted. It opens by describing itself as an electrical thrust device
timeline.text: First sentence of the specification: 'This invention relates to an electrical device for producing thrust by the direct operation of electrical fields.' It states that in a dielectric fluid medium 'the forces of reaction appear to be present in that medium', and in vacuum 'on the solid environmental bodies, such as the walls of the vacuum chamber'. Word counts over all six pages: gravity 0, anti-gravity 0, scalar 0, electrogravitics 0.
timeline.source: US Patent 3,187,206, complete 6-page text, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/fd/fa/17/a3da8c41817315/US3187206.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Project Blue Book logs calls from the F. E. Warren base commander
timeline.text: Between about 0130 and 0440 on 1 August 1965, Lt. Anspaugh at Project Blue Book fielded and logged telephone calls from F. E. Warren AFB reporting objects over the Warren Minuteman complex, including calls from Capt. Snelling of the Air Force command post, Col. Johnson the base commander, Col. Williams commanding the Sioux Army Depot at Sidney, Nebraska, and Capt. Howell. Sites named include E Site, G Flight, Quebec Flight, H-2 and B-4. The memorandum summarising the calls was published by J. Allen Hynek in 1972.
timeline.source: rr0.org mirror of Hastings's F. E. Warren 1965 material, https://rr0.org/time/2/0/0/6/02/24/Hastings_UfosightingsAtIcbmSites/Warren_1965/

timeline.label: Kecksburg
timeline.text: A fireball crosses eight states at about 4:44pm EST. Kecksburg residents report an object down in the woods. The Greensburg Tribune-Review reports the area 'immediately sealed off on the order of U.S. Army and State Police officials'. A later edition: 'Searchers Fail to Find Object.'

timeline.label: Michigan sightings and 'swamp gas'
timeline.text: Mass sightings near Dexter and Hillsdale are met with J. Allen Hynek's provisional swamp gas explanation, reported as a blanket dismissal and met with public fury.

timeline.label: First congressional hearing
timeline.text: After House Minority Leader Gerald Ford demands an inquiry, the House Armed Services Committee holds a one-day hearing on unidentified flying objects — the first in nineteen years of official investigation.

timeline.label: The Low memo
timeline.text: Two months before the Air Force contract is signed, project coordinator Robert Low writes that 'the trick would be' to appear a totally objective study to the public while presenting the image of nonbelievers to scientists.

timeline.label: The conclusion is written before the study
timeline.text: Robert Low's memorandum proposes a study 'conducted almost entirely by non-believers' with 'almost zero expectation of finding a saucer'. McDonald finds it in the project files in July 1967.

timeline.label: Lunar Orbiter 1 launched; programme managed by NASA Langley Research Center
timeline.text: NASA's NSSDCA master catalogue records the launch of Lunar Orbiter 1 on 10 August 1966, photographic data acquired from 18 to 29 August 1966, and that 'The Lunar Orbiter program was managed by NASA Langley Research Center'. This is the agency record against which Karl Wolfe's account of seeing Lunar Orbiter mosaics at an NSA facility on Langley Air Force Base must be measured.
timeline.source: NASA NSSDCA master catalogue, spacecraft record for Lunar Orbiter 1 (1966-073A), https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1966-073A

timeline.label: Minot AFB documents
timeline.text: Three Air Force documents record unexplained aerial activity around Minot AFB, North Dakota, home of the 91st Strategic Missile Wing. Published in facsimile by Robert Hastings.

timeline.label: AFR 80-17 assigns the Blue Book effort to the Foreign Technology Division by name
timeline.text: Air Force Regulation 80-17 provides that 'The Air Force Systems Command will support the program with current resources within the Foreign Technology Division (FTD) at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, Ohio, to continue Blue Book effort', requires FTD to 'Analyze and evaluate all information and evidence reported to bases on those UFOs which are not identified at the base level', and requires FTD to 'prepare a final case report on each sighting reported to it'. Six months earlier the USAF Scientific Advisory Board's ad hoc committee had recorded the resources behind the whole programme as 'only one officer, a sergeant, and secretary'.
timeline.source: Air Force Regulation 80-17, Research and Development - UNIDENTIFIED FLYING OBJECTS (UFO), 19 September 1966, https://nicap.org/afr80-17.htm

timeline.label: Condon Committee established
timeline.text: The University of Colorado UFO Project is formed under USAF contract 44620-67-C-0035 with Edward Condon as scientific director.

timeline.label: All ten Echo Flight missiles lose strategic alert at 0845
timeline.text: The 341st Strategic Missile Wing history: 'On 16 March 1967 at 0845, all sites in Echo (E) Flight, Malmstrom AFB, shutdown with No-Go indication of Channels 9 and 12 on Voice Reporting Signal Assemble (VRSA). All LF's in E Flight lost strategic alert nearly simultaneously. No other Wing I configuration lost strategic alert at that time.' By about 1400 the same day SAC Headquarters had called in Ogden Air Materiel Area support for a complete engineering analysis.
timeline.source: 341st SMW history, Jan-Mar 1967, p 32, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf

timeline.label: Malmstrom Echo Flight shutdown
timeline.text: All ten Minuteman missiles of Echo Flight, 341st Strategic Missile Wing, go off alert status. An Air Force teletype the following day concerns loss of strategic alert. Robert Salas would later attribute the cause to an object over the front gate.

timeline.label: The engineering investigation reports it cannot determine a cause
timeline.text: The Engineering Investigation Team's 'Report of Engineering Investigation of Echo Flight Incident, Malmstrom AFB, Mont. - 16 Mar 67', dated 23 March 1967 and classified Secret, is the document the entire Malmstrom controversy turns on. It is footnoted on almost every page of the wing history's Echo Flight section and has never been opened by this board. Through the history it states: 'The investigation teams at Malmstrom, were unable to determine a logical cause for the incident.'
timeline.source: 341st SMW history, Jan-Mar 1967, citing the report at p 17, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf

timeline.label: US 3,322,374 granted: magnetohydrodynamic propulsion, 9 claims, Class 244-62
timeline.text: What it claims is a linear induction motor using the surrounding ionised atmosphere as its armature. Word counts across all seven pages: scalar 0, spin 0, gravity 0, anti-gravity 0, zero point 0. Fifty-nine years later it was offered as evidence that the 'Scalar Physics' callout on the McCandlish ARV drawing refers to spin-zero scalar particles.
timeline.source: US Patent 3,322,374, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/6f/35/54/257dd6cdb01efc/US3322374.pdf , opened 2026-09-18 and recorded in notes/PROPULSION-CLAIMS-2026-09-18.md

timeline.label: OOAMA concludes the cause appears to be EMP or electrostatic, by elimination
timeline.text: In an interim report of 2 June 1967 to Ballistic Systems Division at Norton AFB, Ogden Air Materiel Area reported that Boeing bench tests in its Network Resolution Area had reproduced the Echo Flight fault signature in 60 per cent of twenty applications of a 30 microsecond pulse to the C-53P Logic Coupler, and concluded: 'Due to the fact that the power tests were essentially negative, it appears that the cause of the Echo Flight problem was of the EMP or electrostatic nature.' The conclusion follows from a run of negative tests rather than from reproducing the event in the field.
timeline.source: 341st SMW history, Apr-Jun 1967, citing OOAMA msg 01787 to BSD Norton AFB, 2 June 1967, pp 37-38, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/ufos/malmstromufo.pdf

timeline.label: The 1127th's own history names the recovery pipeline
timeline.text: The 1127th USAF Field Activities Group's semiannual history, doc. AFNIABA 014-67, lists Project BLUE FLY, MIG-17 Exploitation and Project MOON DUST together under FOREIGN MATERIEL PROGRAM. It records exploitation personnel from FTD Detachment 3 deployed to crash sites and about three tons of parts airlifted to Wright-Patterson, and SPADATS notifying the unit of 37 Soviet deorbits.

timeline.label: Shag Harbour
timeline.text: An object enters the water off Shag Harbour, Nova Scotia at about 11:20pm ADT before at least eleven witnesses. RCC Halifax telexes the RCAF Air Desk in Ottawa having eliminated all aircraft; the Navy tasks Fleet Diving Unit Atlantic to a three-day underwater search. Nothing is found.

timeline.label: AEC detonates 29 kilotons at 4,227 feet, twelve miles from Dulce
timeline.text: The US Atomic Energy Commission detonated a 29-kiloton-yield nuclear device in the emplacement well GB-E at a depth of 4,227 feet, twelve miles southwest of Dulce in the Carson National Forest, to stimulate natural gas production from the Pictured Cliffs Formation. The first reservoir-stimulation experiment of the Plowshare programme, jointly sponsored by the AEC, the Department of the Interior and El Paso Natural Gas. THE EARLIEST DATED ARTEFACT IN THE CLUSTER, and it is a government record, twelve years before the rumour begins.
timeline.source: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

timeline.label: McDonnell Douglas funds an internal study
timeline.text: Robert M. Wood begins a company-funded study of unidentified craft and their propulsion at McDonnell Douglas Astronautics, Huntington Beach. No government contract, no reporting obligation, no released record.

timeline.label: Look publishes 'Flying Saucer Fiasco'
timeline.text: John G. Fuller publishes the Low memo, calling the project a $500,000 trick. Condon fires investigators David Saunders and Norman Levine.

timeline.label: Production testing begins; the gas comes back radioactive
timeline.text: Testing through the reentry well GB-ER ran from July 1968 to October 1969 across five tests, producing 213 million cubic feet of natural gas that retained measurable radioactive constituents and a significantly lower heat value than expected.
timeline.source: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

timeline.label: Clifford Stone enters the US Army
timeline.text: Per the service record Philip J. Klass obtained from the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis and printed in 2001: Stone entered the Army on 8 July 1968 and after several months of basic training 'he was trained to be a clerk/typist'. The assignment history that follows is clerical and administrative throughout.
timeline.source: Philip J. Klass, Skeptics UFO Newsletter (SUN) #68, Summer 2001, 'Dr. Greer's Disclosure Conference Reveals His New Strategy'; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/2022/09/26195512/SUN-68-Summer-2001.pdf

timeline.label: Chile's first official UAP circular
timeline.text: Colonel Sergio Bravo Flores, Director of the Chilean Meteorological Office, sends the first official circular to 43 aeronautical installations from Arica to the Chilean Antarctic Territory requesting reports. Part of the resulting dozen reports are forwarded to the University of Colorado, where the Condon Committee is working.

timeline.label: House Science Committee UFO symposium
timeline.text: Hynek, James McDonald, Carl Sagan and others testify. McDonald tells Congress that 'credible observers are observing relatively incredible objects'. No legislation follows.

timeline.label: Minot B-52 incident
timeline.text: Ground radar, base weather radar, airborne radar and visual observation converge on an object near B-52H JAG 31; the bomber's transmitter fails for four minutes; Minuteman sites of N, O, J and M Flights report alarms and an inner door combination lock moved. Blue Book sends no field investigators.

timeline.label: Lt Col Werlich files eight pages of Basic Reporting Data on the Minot case
timeline.text: Lt Col Arthur J. Werlich of the 862nd Combat Support Group Operations Division prepared eight pages of Basic Reporting Data on the 24 October 1968 Minot events and transmitted it to multiple Air Force agencies. Seven airmen completed AF Form 117 questionnaires, thirteen B-52 ASQ-38 radarscope photographs were printed with data plates, and Werlich drew an overlay map at 1:200,000. Every witness statement in the file is contemporaneous and official.
timeline.source: Documentation index for the Minot AFB case, https://minotb52ufo.com/doc.php

timeline.label: RAND publishes 'UFOs: What To Do?'
timeline.text: George Kocher's draft DRU-1571 examines UFO brightness, size and manoeuvres and recommends a course of action - two months before the Condon report tells the public the subject is closed.

timeline.label: The Condon Report closes the official file
timeline.text: The University of Colorado study directed by Edward Condon publishes 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects', including Martin Altschuler's chapter on atmospheric electricity and plasma interpretations. Project Blue Book is terminated the following year, ending official American investigation for the next four decades.

timeline.label: Condon Report released
timeline.text: 'Scientific Study of Unidentified Flying Objects' concludes further study is unwarranted, while its Section V Chapter 2 documents the 1948 Estimate of the Situation and its destruction.

timeline.label: Bolender memo
timeline.text: Brig. Gen. Carroll Bolender recommends terminating Blue Book, explaining that UFO reports affecting national security go via JANAP 146 or AFM 55-11 and 'are not part of the Blue Book system'.

timeline.label: Project Blue Book terminated
timeline.text: Secretary of the Air Force Robert C. Seamans Jr. closes the program citing the Condon Report. Final tally: 12,618 sightings, 701 never identified.

timeline.label: Secretary of the Air Force terminates Project BLUE BOOK
timeline.text: After 12,618 reported sightings of which 701 remain unidentified, the Air Force closes its public UFO channel on the strength of the Condon Report and a National Academy of Sciences review. No document terminating classified collection is ever produced.

timeline.label: Blue Book is terminated on the Condon findings
timeline.text: The Air Force closes its public reporting channel citing the University of Colorado report. The Bolender memo of the same period records that reports affecting national security were never in that channel.

timeline.label: SCANATE begins
timeline.text: The CIA initiates 'scan by coordinate' in response to assessments of Soviet psychotronic spending. SRI research under Puthoff and Targ follows in 1972.

timeline.label: CIA funds SRI psychoenergetics
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin CIA-funded remote-viewing research at Stanford Research Institute - the start of a 23-year compartmented programme in a publicly ridiculed domain.

timeline.label: SRI psychoenergetics
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin the SRI International programme that becomes the government's Stargate effort - the template for outsourcing an unwanted phenomenon to a private laboratory.

timeline.label: Federal funding of anomalous cognition begins
timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin remote viewing work at Stanford Research Institute under federal sponsorship. The programme runs through Grill Flame, Center Lane, Sun Streak and Star Gate until 1995, establishing beyond argument that the US government funds research of this kind for decades at a time before terminating it and denying it produced anything.

timeline.label: EO 11652 puts classified material on an automatic declassification timetable
timeline.text: Nixon signs EO 11652, effective 1 June 1972, superseding EO 10501 and six amending orders. It creates the General Declassification Schedule, under which Top Secret declassifies after ten years and Confidential after six, adds a thirty-year rule that only a Department head can override in writing, and creates an Interagency Classification Review Committee under the NSC that takes complaints from outside the government.

timeline.label: JASON moves from IDA to SRI International
timeline.text: The advisory panel's administration transfers between FFRDC-adjacent operators for the first time, establishing the pattern of contractor custody of the government's most sensitive scientific advice.

timeline.label: Targ and Puthoff publish in Nature
timeline.text: 'Information transmission under conditions of sensory shielding' appears in Nature vol. 251, pp. 602-607 - the open-literature face of a classified programme.

timeline.label: The USIB charters a standing committee tasked with anomalies by name
timeline.text: The charter of the Scientific and Technical Intelligence Committee records the renaming from the Scientific Intelligence Committee and lists among its Priority Group II objectives the 'Assessment and establishment of an Intelligence Community position regarding certain unidentified foreign activities and anomalies in the S&T area'. The committee advises the United States Intelligence Board and coordinates collection and production in those areas. Nothing in the charter mentions the Robertson Panel.
timeline.source: CHARTER, Scientific and Technical Intelligence Committee, 23 October 1974, CIA-RDP79M00098A000500020010-4, https://archive.org/download/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp79m00098a000500020010-4/cia-rdp79m00098a000500020010-4_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Ben Rich takes over Skunk Works
timeline.text: Rich succeeds Kelly Johnson as director of Lockheed's Advanced Development Projects, holding the deepest black-aerospace access available to a private citizen for the next sixteen years.

timeline.label: Loring AFB overflights begin
timeline.text: Unidentified aerial incursions are logged over Loring AFB, Maine, opening a three-week sequence across SAC nuclear installations.

timeline.label: NMCC logs an 'AFB Penetration' at Loring and runs it up the Joint Staff
timeline.text: At 0605 EST on 29 October 1975 the National Military Command Center issued a Memorandum for Record subject 'AFB Penetration', signed C. D. Roberts, Jr., Brigadier General, USMC, Deputy Director for Operations, recording that an unidentified helicopter, possibly two, had been sighted flying low over Loring AFB in proximity to a weapons storage area, that an Army National Guard helicopter had failed to locate it, and that NORAD had obtained Canadian authority to pursue across the border. Distribution ran to CJCS, DJS, J-30 through J-38, the service chiefs and the DIA, NSA and CIA representatives.
timeline.source: NMCC Memorandum for Record, 29 October 1975, http://www.nicap.org/reports/751027loring_1-6.htm

timeline.label: A KC-135 pursues an object from the Wurtsmith weapons storage area over Lake Huron
timeline.text: The NORAD Senior Director's Log for 31 October 1975 records: 'Alerted by NCOC of a helicopter sighted over Wurtsmith AFB Wpns storage area, a tanker sighted same and pursued it 35 SE over Lake Huron.' A Joint Chiefs of Staff operational report of 30 October 1975 records that the Michigan Department of Natural Resources was contacted about aircraft searching for hunters spotting deer, and the explanation did not fit.
timeline.source: NICAP, 'Wurtsmith and Others', http://www.nicap.org/articles/CI-Wurtsmith.htm

timeline.label: Malmstrom AFB and Minuteman fields overflown
timeline.text: DoD records later released under FOIA case 97-F-1677 describe numerous unidentified craft over Malmstrom AFB and its missile fields, which multiple F-106 interceptors could not acquire.

timeline.label: Two F-106s scrambled over the Malmstrom missile field; radar contact lost
timeline.text: The 24th NORAD Region Senior Director's Log for 8 November 1975: height-finder personnel picked up objects at 10,000 to 13,000 feet on track J330; two F-106s were scrambled at 0754Z; at 0820Z 'Lost radar contact, fighters broken off at 0825'; at 0905Z 'L-sites had fighters and objects; fighters did not get down to objects'; and at 0915Z, from four different points, 'when fighters arrived in the area, the lights went out; when fighters departed, the lights came back on'.
timeline.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 8 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt

timeline.label: NMCC memorandum for the record
timeline.text: At 0253 EST Malmstrom takes seven height-finder radar cuts between 9,500 and 15,500 feet with simultaneous ground witnesses; FAA cross-tell shows no jet within 100NM; two F-106s are scrambled at 0254 and airborne at 0257; at 0344 the objects cannot be intercepted.

timeline.label: CINCNORAD summarises the sequence across five installations
timeline.text: 'Since 28 Oct 75 numerous reports of suspicious objects have been received at the NORAD CU; reliable military personnel at Loring AFB, Maine, Wurtsmith AFB, Michigan, Malmstrom AFB, Mt, Minot AFB, ND, and Canadian Forces Station, Falconbridge, Ontario, Canada have visually sighted suspicious objects.' The message names Minot AFB where the 24th NORAD Region's own log had named Minot Air Force Station the day before.
timeline.source: NICAP, quoting the CINCNORAD four-part message of 11 November 1975, http://www.nicap.org/intsac.htm

timeline.label: NORAD summary document
timeline.text: A NORAD document records that reliable military personnel at Loring, Wurtsmith, Malmstrom, Minot and CFS Falconbridge had visually sighted suspicious objects during October and early November 1975.

timeline.label: The NORAD log closes the Malmstrom sequence
timeline.text: '19 Nov 75 (1327Z) - SAC command post report UFO observed by FSC & a cook, observed object travelling NE between M-8 and M-l at a fast rate of speed. Object bright white light seen 45 to 50 sec following terrain 200 ft off ground. The light was two to three times brighter than landing lights on a jet.' The original marks this as the last entry pertaining to these incidents.
timeline.source: 24th NORAD Region Senior Directors Log, 19 November 1975, https://archive.org/download/MalmstromAirForceBaseIncident/Malmstrom%20Air%20Force%20Base%20Incident%20%E2%80%93%20March%2016,%201967%20NORAD%20logs_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Gabe Valdez stationed at Dulce, begins the livestock investigations
timeline.text: A New Mexico State Police officer stationed in Dulce in 1976 began investigating cattle and other animals found dead with soft tissue removed, and became the central official figure in the region's caseload. The only official investigator anywhere in this story.
timeline.source: Tom Sharpe, The Santa Fe New Mexican, 23 September 2013, https://www.santafenewmexican.com/news/local_news/book-claims-government-behind-cattle-mutilations/article_5c78559b-39a3-5610-b49b-df0a8a327af8.html

timeline.label: IHEDN committee opens the French file
timeline.text: A committee of the Institut des Hautes Études de Défense Nationale chaired by General Blanchard of the Gendarmerie Nationale opens the unidentified flying objects file with the objective of proposing how to organise research and data collection. Its recommendations are adopted.

timeline.label: Church Committee files Book I and records that it never examined an agency file itself
timeline.text: Senate Report 94-755, Book I, Foreign and Military Intelligence, is filed. Its section on the obstacles the committee met states that despite its legal Senate mandate and the issuance of subpoenas, in no instance had the committee been able to examine the agencies' files on its own. Its publication note records that three chapters, Cover, Espionage and Budgetary Oversight, were deleted at the request of the agencies.
timeline.source: S. Rept. 94-755, Book I, 26 April 1976, https://www.intelligence.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/sites-default-files-94755-i.pdf

timeline.label: GEPAN created inside CNES
timeline.text: The French national space agency establishes GEPAN under Claude Poher with the authority of director general Yves Sillard - the world's first and still only permanent civilian government UAP office with a public case archive. The Gendarmerie Nationale routes sighting reports to it by teletype.

timeline.label: CAUS founded
timeline.text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy is established under attorney Peter Gersten and begins FOIA litigation against the CIA.

timeline.label: JANAP 146 still lists UFOs, eight years after Blue Book closed
timeline.text: Change No. 2 to JANAP 146(E) is promulgated. Unidentified flying objects remain a reportable CIRVIS category at Article 201, and Article 208 continues to incorporate 18 U.S.C. 793 and the Canadian Official Secrets Act. Project Blue Book closed in December 1969. The document was released under FOIA on 28 February 1994.

timeline.label: The Petrozavodsk phenomenon
timeline.text: A luminous object is reported from Copenhagen and Helsinki to Vladivostok. Northern European governments write to the president of the USSR Academy of Sciences asking whether it was Soviet weapons testing. The Academy's own preliminary report concludes that 'based on the available data, it is unfeasible to satisfactorily understand the observed phenomenon'.

timeline.label: Operação Prato begins on Colares
timeline.text: The Brazilian Air Force and the National Information Service open the first Brazilian military operation mounted solely to investigate UAP, at the request of the mayor of Colares after residents report burns and puncture wounds from descending lights. Captain Uyrangê Hollanda commands.

timeline.label: HAVE BLUE flies at Groom Lake
timeline.text: Lockheed's stealth demonstrator first flies from a facility whose existence the government will not acknowledge for another twenty-one years.

timeline.label: Council Bluffs fall
timeline.text: Five independent witness groups see a luminous mass descend near Big Lake Park, Council Bluffs, Iowa; police photograph a four-by-six-foot molten metal mass. The sample survives into the modern literature.

timeline.label: CAUS FOIA request
timeline.text: Citizens Against UFO Secrecy files for the Loring, Wurtsmith and Malmstrom case files. On 6 February 1978 the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense identifies twenty-four Joint Chiefs documents; after an internal dispute Assistant Secretary Thomas Ross orders the withheld fifteen released.

timeline.label: AEC decommissions the site and injects liquid radioactive waste into the cavity
timeline.text: Structures and equipment were decontaminated and removed, liquid radioactive waste was injected into the former cavity now forming the lower part of the collapse chimney, solid radioactive waste went to the Nevada Test Site, and test wells were plugged. Soil sampling followed in 1978, 1986, 2000 and 2002.
timeline.source: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

timeline.label: GRILL FLAME formalised
timeline.text: Army INSCOM and DIA formalise operational remote viewing at Fort Meade using SRI methodology - the first of four codenames for one continuous seventeen-year effort.

timeline.label: First Council Bluffs analysis
timeline.text: The Des Moines Register reports the initial materials analyses identifying the metal as high-carbon steel and slag - the baseline the 2022 Stanford work would revisit.

timeline.label: Friedman meets Marcel
timeline.text: Stanton Friedman is put in touch with retired Lt. Col. Jesse Marcel Sr. in Baton Rouge. Marcel states the weather balloon account was a cover and that the material was not of this earth. Roswell restarts after thirty-one years.

timeline.label: Jesse Marcel breaks silence
timeline.text: The 509th's intelligence officer tells researcher Stanton Friedman that the 1947 weather balloon explanation was a cover story, restarting the Roswell inquiry after thirty-one years.

timeline.label: GEPAN's classified five-volume report
timeline.text: GEPAN reports to its scientific council in five volumes and about 500 pages, limited to 120 or 140 copies and secret. Of eleven high-strangeness cases studied by four-person teams including psychologists, ten were concluded to be material phenomena not explicable as natural or human. A document in the US NSA's declassified UFO collection assesses that its method makes 'the bulk of the Condon Report seem very poor by comparison'.

timeline.label: EO 12065 requires the public interest in disclosure to be weighed
timeline.text: Carter's classification order revokes EO 11652 and, at section 3-303, requires an official to determine whether the public interest in disclosure outweighs the damage to national security. It is the only classification order to have carried such a test, and it lasts four years.

timeline.label: Retrievals of the Third Kind
timeline.text: Leonard Stringfield delivers Status Report I at the ninth annual MUFON Symposium in Dayton, Ohio. The crash-retrieval literature begins as a research field.

timeline.label: Founding meeting of SETKA at the USSR Academy of Sciences
timeline.text: Migulin and Platov of IZMIRAN, Narimanov and Petrovskaya of the Institute for Space Studies, Balashov and Volga of secret military unit 67947, Gindilis of the Shternberg Institute and others meet. SETKA-AN and SETKA-MO are established on the order of the Military-Industrial Commission. The official history later gives as one reason for secrecy the possibility 'that some of the UFO characteristics could be used for military purposes'.

timeline.label: Bennewitz becomes the origin point of the Dulce claim
timeline.text: From about 1979 Paul Bennewitz, an Albuquerque instrument manufacturer whose company overlooked the Manzano storage area, began the personally funded study that made him the first person to attach a facility claim to Dulce. He later connected Myrna Hansen's 1980 account to the same place.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 29 August 2016, https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2016/08/29/enigmatic-personalities-behind-the-initial-dulce-underground-base-rumors/comment-page-1/

timeline.label: A wing historian records that his own wing history omits the incursion
timeline.text: SSgt Paul J. Cahill, historian of the 379th Bombardment Wing, wrote in a Research Record of Events: 'Following that request, I checked the Oct-Dec 75 Wing History and found no references to the incident.' The following day Capt. Myron Taylor wrote him a Memo for the Record giving the KC-135 crew's account. This is the board's one documented instance of an Air Force unit history omitting an event that other Air Force paper records, found and written down by the unit historian himself.
timeline.source: NICAP, 'Wurtsmith and Others', http://www.nicap.org/articles/CI-Wurtsmith.htm

timeline.label: THE COUNTERWEIGHT: TSgt Fouche assigned temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3, Nellis AF Range
timeline.text: An AF Form 77a signed 24 August 1979 by MSgt Brewer of 57 CRS, Nellis AFB Nevada records: 'This out of cycle report is generated because TSgt Fouche was assigned TDY to the AFFTC-DET 3, Nellis AF Range from 1 June 79 to 14 August 79. His duties and responsibilities for this period have been verified via a separate report.' Peter Merlin's published reference work identifies Detachment 3 AFFTC as the unit operating the Groom Lake facility. The form does not say what he did there, and the separate report it refers to is not in the file.
timeline.source: AF Form 77a, 24 August 1979, page 3 of https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf ; Peter W. Merlin, https://www.dreamlandresort.com/black_projects/black_projects_history.html

timeline.label: Bennewitz begins his Manzano study
timeline.text: The Albuquerque businessman starts a self-funded study of lights and signals over the Kirtland/Manzano nuclear weapons storage area. He contacts the base 24 October 1980 and briefs officials 10 November 1980.

timeline.label: The Roswell Incident
timeline.text: Berlitz and Moore publish, combining Marcel's account with the second-hand Barney Barnett material and creating the two-site structure that no later Roswell scenario has reconciled. Haut is described in it as 'not a witness'.

timeline.label: Status Report II
timeline.text: 'The UFO Crash/Retrieval Syndrome: New Sources, New Data', published by MUFON, introduces the letter-number case coding and the first Del Rio and Wright-Patterson entries.

timeline.label: Soviet Navy anomalous phenomena reporting instruction
timeline.text: Guidelines for the Soviet Navy on collecting anomalous phenomena data are signed by the Deputy Commander of the Main Headquarters of the Navy, Vice Admiral Saakyan.

timeline.label: CAUS sues NSA
timeline.text: Civil Action No. 80-1562 is filed. NSA locates UFO-related records, withholds them, and defends the withholding with a classified affidavit by its Chief of Policy, Eugene Yeates.

timeline.label: Named 1608 SPS personnel report unidentified objects over Manzano
timeline.text: SSGT Stephen Ferenz, area supervisor, ATC Martin W. Rist and AMN Anthony D. Frazier of the 1608 Security Police Squadron reported at approximately 2350 hrs on 8 August 1980; a Sandia security guard who requested anonymity reported at approximately 0020 hrs on 9 August. The record establishes that guards at a nuclear weapons storage area reported what they could not identify. It establishes nothing about what the objects were.
timeline.source: AFOSI complaint form, District File No. 8017D93-0/29, reproduced by NICAP from the CUFON archive, https://www.nicap.org/foia_003.htm

timeline.label: Kirtland AFB / Manzano incident
timeline.text: Three 1608 SPS airmen watch an object make stop-and-go manoeuvres near the Manzano restricted test range, descend into Coyote Canyon and depart vertically at high speed; a Sandia security guard reports a disc near an alarmed structure hours later.

timeline.label: Manzano intrusions and the Bennewitz operation
timeline.text: AFOSI at Kirtland AFB investigates intrusions at the Manzano Weapons Storage Area adjacent to Sandia while simultaneously feeding fabricated crash-retrieval material to the physicist Paul Bennewitz through Special Agent Richard Doty.

timeline.label: AFOSI complaint form filed, District File No. 8017D93-0/29, SA Richard C Doty
timeline.text: The form carries AFOSI Det 1700, Kirtland AFB, New Mexico, the district file number and 'Richard C Doty, SA' on its face. THIS IS THE TIER 1 SOURCE FOR DOTY'S AFOSI SERVICE and needs no interview to support it. The board's existing claim dates the form 9 September 1980; the NICAP page as rendered gives '2-9 Sept 80'; the discrepancy is unresolved.
timeline.source: AFOSI complaint form, District File No. 8017D93-0/29, reproduced by NICAP from the CUFON archive, https://www.nicap.org/foia_003.htm

timeline.label: AFOSI complaint form filed by Richard Doty
timeline.text: District File No. 8017D93-0/29 documents the Kirtland sightings. The same AFOSI office would shortly begin running fabricated material at Albuquerque physicist Paul Bennewitz.

timeline.label: AFOSI Kirtland record on Coyote Canyon
timeline.text: An AFOSI document records Kirtland AFB security police observing unexplained aerial objects over the Coyote Canyon / Manzano Weapons Storage Area, and notes Paul Bennewitz's reporting and photography.

timeline.label: Larry Warren says his PRP clearance came through at Bentwaters
timeline.text: In the Disclosure Project Briefing Document: 'On December 11th, 1980, my security clearance notice, PRP, came through and I was approved. My clearance was a secret clearance at that time.' His assignment to the 81st Tactical Fighter Wing is not the disputed part of his account; his presence at the events of later that month is.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Rendlesham Forest incident begins
timeline.text: USAF security patrolmen at the RAF Woodbridge east gate report lights descending into the forest; three enter on foot and report a metallic triangular object.

timeline.label: Cash-Landrum encounter
timeline.text: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum stop on FM 1485 near Huffman, Texas before a bright diamond-shaped object expelling flame, followed by a formation of tandem-rotor helicopters. All three report illness; Cash is hospitalised from 2 January 1981.

timeline.label: Bennewitz writes his own report, 'Project Beta'
timeline.text: Roughly five thousand words, titled 'Project Beta: SUMMARY OF REPORT AND STATUS (WITH SUGGESTED GUIDELINES)'. The claimant's own dated statement of his own claim, and the artefact the board had been missing. Read only in two fragments quoted by a 2025 newsletter. NOT to be confused with Greg Bishop's 2005 book of the same name.
timeline.source: Stephen Fisher, The Trenchant Edges Newsletter, 29 November 2025, https://www.trenchantedges.com/p/what-did-they-do-to-paul-bennewitz

timeline.label: Halt signs the 'Unexplained Lights' memo
timeline.text: The deputy base commander documents the object, three ground depressions and beta/gamma readings of 0.1 milliroentgens in an official memorandum to the RAF station commander.

timeline.label: D.C. Circuit affirms NSA withholding
timeline.text: The court of appeals affirms judgment for NSA on the basis of an affidavit the plaintiffs were never permitted to see.

timeline.label: D.C. Circuit affirms NSA's total withholding
timeline.text: The Court of Appeals sustains the withholding on the classified showing; the Supreme Court denies certiorari on 8 March 1982. A federal court has now confirmed that a US intelligence agency holds UFO material it cannot describe in public.

timeline.label: The courts sustain the NSA wall
timeline.text: The D.C. Circuit upholds NSA's withholding of its UFO-related holdings in Citizens Against UFO Secrecy v. NSA, on the strength of a classified affidavit the plaintiffs never see; certiorari is denied in March 1982. This sets the practical ceiling on FOIA litigation in this field.

timeline.label: Army IG investigation
timeline.text: Lt. Col. George Sarran of the Office of the Inspector General of the US Army conducts the only thorough formal government investigation of the Cash-Landrum encounter. He finds no evidence the helicopters were US armed forces aircraft, while stating the witnesses were credible and no one appeared to be exaggerating.

timeline.label: Northrop TACIT BLUE first flight
timeline.text: The U.S. Air Force fact sheet states 'The aircraft made its first flight in February 1982, and by the conclusion of the program in 1985, had flown 135 times.' This is what a real black aircraft programme of the era looks like in the primary record: 48 ft 2 in span, curved surfaces, two Garrett turbofans, no armament.
timeline.source: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF

timeline.label: Supreme Court denies certiorari
timeline.text: The withholding of UFO-related signals intelligence becomes settled law. The government's position has never been that the records do not exist.

timeline.label: EO 12356 removes the public-interest test and permits reclassification after a FOIA request
timeline.text: Reagan's classification order, effective 1 August 1982, revokes EO 12065. The phrase 'public interest' occurs nowhere in it. Section 1.6(c) permits reclassifying information already declassified and disclosed where it may reasonably be recovered, and 1.6(d) permits classification or reclassification after a Freedom of Information Act request has been received. Doubt about the level is resolved upward.

timeline.label: The F-117 moves to Tonopah
timeline.text: The 4450th Tactical Group relocates from Groom Lake to the Tonopah Test Range. A manned operational combat squadron will fly from a hidden base for six years before acknowledgement in November 1988.

timeline.label: Los Alamos Monitor front page calls Lazar a physicist at LAMPF
