timeline.text: The Los Alamos Monitor of Sunday 27 June 1982, pages A1 and A8, carries 'LA Man Joins The Jet Set - At 200 Miles An Hour' by staff writer Terry England, about a jet-powered Honda Lazar had built, and says in the paper's own voice: 'To Lazar, a physicist at the Los Alamos Meson Physics Facility, the important thing is the jet engine.' The earliest dated artefact in the cluster, seven years before the UFO claim.
timeline.source: Los Alamos Monitor, 27 June 1982, A1 and A8, reprinted at https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/bobs-jetcar-article/

timeline.label: Edward Teller lectures at Los Alamos the day after the jet-car story
timeline.text: Tom Mahood's 2018 retrospective places Teller's Los Alamos lecture on the day after the Monitor article, calling the timing an 'amazing display of totally fucked synchronicity'. Lazar's own 1991 narration instead places the newspaper story and the Teller speech on the same day. The newspaper's date is fixed, so both cannot be right, and the board carries the anecdote as 'within a day'. No newspaper notice of the lecture was opened.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood, 2018 retrospective, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/looking-at-the-bob-lazar-story-from-the-perspective-of-2018/ ; and The Lazar Tape, 1991, captions at 35:48

timeline.label: CUFON goes online
timeline.text: The Computer UFO Network begins publishing full-text FOIA releases electronically from Seattle, establishing the document-with-case-number standard of evidence.

timeline.label: Doty shows Howe the AQUARIUS paper
timeline.text: AFOSI Special Agent Richard Doty shows documentary producer Linda Moulton Howe a purported government briefing paper at Kirtland AFB. She may read but not copy it; the promised film footage never materialises.

timeline.label: INSCOM puts a written assessment of the Monroe Institute's Gateway Process on the record
timeline.text: A twenty-nine page memorandum from the US Army Operational Group, US Army Intelligence and Security Command, Fort George G. Meade, analyses the Gateway Experience on tasking from its own commander and states that it is meant as 'a useful guide for other USAINSCOM personnel who are required to take the Gateway training or work with Gateway materials'. It names remote viewing as a follow-on technique inside the method and concludes that there is 'a sound, rational basis in terms of physical science parameters for considering Gateway to be plausible in terms of its essential objectives'.
timeline.source: Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process, US Army Operational Group, INSCOM, 9 June 1983, CIA-RDP96-00788R001700210016-5, https://archive.org/details/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp96-00788r001700210016-5

timeline.label: Stone files a FOIA request about Bentwaters, from his home address
timeline.text: Klass records that on 23 December 1983 Clifford Stone filed a Freedom of Information Act request with the USAF for information on the Bentwaters incident, 'used his home address and did not show that he was an Army sergeant'. Stone had told the Disclosure Project that an Army team took him there officially in late December 1980. THIS IS AN AFFIRMATIVE ACT INCONSISTENT WITH HIS OWN ACCOUNT, NOT AN ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE.
timeline.source: Philip J. Klass, Skeptics UFO Newsletter (SUN) #68, Summer 2001, 'Dr. Greer's Disclosure Conference Reveals His New Strategy'; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/2022/09/26195512/SUN-68-Summer-2001.pdf

timeline.label: Clear Intent
timeline.text: Fawcett and Greenwood publish the FOIA-sourced counterweight to the anonymous-testimony literature, reproducing the NORAD, NMCC and Joint Chiefs documents on the 1975 overflights.

timeline.label: Cash v. United States filed
timeline.text: Betty Cash, Vickie Landrum and Colby Landrum sue the United States in the Southern District of Texas under the Federal Tort Claims Act, Civil Action No. H-84-348. Peter A. Gersten is attorney in charge.

timeline.label: The letter Fouche later calls the 'SAC/DARPA Classified Document' is written
timeline.text: A Headquarters Strategic Air Command letter of 10 July 1984, 'REPLY TO ATTN OF: DARPA', addressed to office code LGMQ, states 'HQ AFMPC has approved an AAR 51[redacted] on MSgt (32674) Fouche as requested. MSgt Fouche's date of availability is Aug 87.' It is signed by DALE E. HAGERMAN, TSgt, USAF, NCOIC, Amn Acft Maint Asgns Sec, Dir of Asgns, DCS/Pers. The page image carries no classification marking of any kind, and all redactions on it were applied by Fouche himself on his own caption's admission.
timeline.source: Page 1 image of https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf , rendered at 190 dpi and read

timeline.label: The MJ-12 film arrives
timeline.text: William L. Moore and Jaime Shandera receive an anonymous roll of undeveloped 35mm film containing the Eisenhower Briefing Document and the Truman-Forrestal memorandum. The delivery falls inside the period Moore later says he was cooperating with AFOSI.

timeline.label: MJ-12 film arrives postmarked Albuquerque
timeline.text: An anonymous roll of undeveloped 35mm film reaches Jaime Shandera in Los Angeles, containing the purported 1952 Eisenhower briefing on Operation Majestic-12 - mailed from the city where the AFOSI operation was running.

timeline.label: The Majestic-12 film arrives
timeline.text: Unsolicited film purporting to show an Eisenhower-era briefing document on recovered craft is delivered to Jaime Shandera. The FBI investigates and its file records an AFOSI assessment that the documents are bogus. Whatever their origin, their circulation imposes a permanent evidentiary tax on every genuine document in the field.

timeline.label: USAF fact sheet denies Wright-Patterson holdings
timeline.text: Wright-Patterson's public affairs office states: 'There are not now nor ever have been, any extraterrestrial visitors or equipment on Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.'

timeline.label: IASA founded
timeline.text: Puthoff establishes the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin, incorporated under EarthTech International in 1991.

timeline.label: NSDD 159 orders a compartmented access system over covert-action policy itself
timeline.text: Reagan signs NSDD 159, directing the national security adviser to establish a separate, specially compartmented control and access system at the Top Secret level for all policy matters concerning covert action. Each agency designates one senior officer as its sole focal point. Knowledge of policy, of operations and of supporting activity is to be strictly compartmented from each other, the minimum possible number of documents is to be created, and one NSC officer holds the only record copies of approved Findings. The implementing procedures are promulgated under separate cover and are not in the released document.

timeline.label: Aurora appears in the Pentagon's unclassified procurement list
timeline.text: The Washington Post reports that the Pentagon's own unclassified P-1 document shows spending on an Air Force programme called Aurora rising from zero to $80 million in FY1986 and $2.27 billion in FY1987. Reminded that its own department had published the figures, an Air Force spokesman said his orders were to say only 'It's a classified program.' Five years before the Aviation Week story.

timeline.label: INSCOM deactivates CENTER LANE and attaches its assets to DIA
timeline.text: INSCOM notifies the Department of the Army of 'the deactivation of the INSCOM CENTER LANE Project, the attachment OPCON of CENTER LANE assets and resources to the Defense Intelligence Agency, and the retirement of CENTER LANE as an active project nickname', and asks HQDA to officially discontinue CENTER LANE 'as a Secretary of the Army designated Special Access Program'. The initiative was INSCOM's own: its commanding general had recommended discontinuing the work in July 1984.
timeline.source: Letter, Deactivation of INSCOM CENTER LANE Project (ICLP) as a Special Access Program (SAP) (U), 2 March 1985, CIA-RDP96-00789R002100120002-4, https://archive.org/download/cia-readingroom-document-cia-rdp96-00789r002100120002-4/cia-rdp96-00789r002100120002-4_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Status Report IV
timeline.text: 'The Fatal Encounter at Ft. Dix-McGuire' opens with a prologue titled 'The Burden of Proof' in which Stringfield states that public research does not have proof and that affidavits, leaked documents and photographs are not proof.

timeline.label: Remote viewing transfers to DIA as SUN STREAK
timeline.text: The programme moves from Army INSCOM to the Defense Intelligence Agency - the same agency that will contract BAASS twenty-two years later.

timeline.label: The Brazilian 'Night of the UFOs'
timeline.text: Twenty-one unidentified radar plots over four Brazilian states. Five Brazilian Air Force fighters are scrambled from Santa Cruz and Anápolis. One Mirage closes to two miles of a contact that zigzags and then accelerates away from a supersonic interceptor; the pilot later estimates Mach 15. Thirteen plots appear astern of an F-5 which turns 180 degrees and sees nothing.

timeline.label: Moreira Lima's press conference
timeline.text: At 16:30 the Brazilian Minister of Aeronautics convenes the press with the five intercept pilots and the air traffic controllers and says: 'It is not a question of believing or not believing. We can only give technical information. There are several hypotheses. Technically, I would tell you gentlemen that we have no explanation.' He promises a full dossier within thirty days. It never appears.

timeline.label: Brazilian Air Defence Command records solid, intelligent objects
timeline.text: Brigadier José Pessoa Cavalcanti de Albuquerque signs a CONFIDENCIAL Relatório de Ocorrências concluding that 'the phenomena are solid and reflect in a certain manner intelligence, by the capacity to follow and to maintain distance from observers as well as to fly in formation, not necessarily crewed'. It stays classified for twenty-three years.

timeline.label: GAO tells Congress a carve-out contractor lost control of its documents
timeline.text: GAO testifies to the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations that Lockheed reported 1,460 discrepancies in a 40,000-item special-access inventory, 11 of them still unresolved. In the same statement it explains that since 1965 special access programs have been excluded from Defense Investigative Service supervision, and that this is why they are called carve-out contracts.

timeline.label: Cash-Landrum dismissed
timeline.text: Judge Ross N. Sterling enters an Order of Dismissal under Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 12(b)(1), 12(b)(6) and 56 on the United States' motion. The only US UFO personal-injury case to reach federal court ends without trial.

timeline.label: Japan Air Lines flight 1628 incident over Alaska
timeline.text: A Japan Air Lines 747 crossing Alaskan airspace reported an object accompanying it. The FAA investigated and generated a file that survives at the National Archives in Record Group 237, archival identifier 733667, running to over 1,500 pages including crew statements, air traffic control transcripts and radar data.
timeline.source: The Black Vault document archive, 'Japanese Airlines JAL 1628 UFO Encounter, November 17, 1986', https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/ufo-case-japanese-airlines-jal1628-november-17-1986/

timeline.label: FAA interviews Captain Terauchi
timeline.text: A 19-page transcript of the FAA's interview with Capt. Terauchi, dated 2 January 1987, is itemised in the National Archives file, alongside interviews with First Officer Tamefugi on 5 January and Flight Engineer Tsukuba on 15 January 1987. Klass reports that in this interview Terauchi 'admitted that this was the third time he had reported sighting a UFO'.
timeline.source: The Black Vault document archive, 'Japanese Airlines JAL 1628 UFO Encounter, November 17, 1986', https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/ufo-case-japanese-airlines-jal1628-november-17-1986/

timeline.label: FAA Alaskan Region press release concludes against a second aircraft
timeline.text: The FAA Alaskan Region issued a press release stating that agency experts at the Technical Center in Atlantic City 'determined that a second radar target near the JAL flight... was not another aircraft but was... an uncorrelated primary and beacon [radar transponder] target return', and concluding: 'The FAA has completed its investigation of JAL flight 1628, and does not intend to pursue it any further.'
timeline.source: Philip J. Klass, Skeptics UFO Newsletter (SUN) #68, Summer 2001, 'Dr. Greer's Disclosure Conference Reveals His New Strategy'; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/2022/09/26195512/SUN-68-Summer-2001.pdf

timeline.label: MJ-12 documents released publicly
timeline.text: Moore, Shandera and Friedman publish the material. NARA's subsequent searches produce nothing but a single problematic memorandum in Record Group 341.

timeline.label: End of Fouche's Strategic Air Command liaison post at Kelly AFB; active service concludes
timeline.text: The Meritorious Service Medal citation with oak leaf cluster reads 'as the Strategic Air Command Liaison Officer, San Antonio Air Logistics Center, Kelly Air Force Base, Texas, from 17 July 1983 to 31 August 1987', and closes 'The singularly distinctive accomplishments of Sergeant Fouche culminate a distinguished career in the service of his country.' The certificate is signed by John T. Chain, Jr., General, USAF, Commander in Chief.
timeline.source: Decoration citation in https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf

timeline.label: 10 U.S.C. 119 enacted — and the waiver with it
timeline.text: Pub. L. 100-180, div. A, title XI, sec. 1132(a)(1), 101 Stat. 1151 adds section 119 to title 10. Subsection (e) -- the waiver that lets the Secretary of Defense strip content from the SAP reports and deliver it only to the chairman and ranking minority member of each defense committee -- is present in the original enactment and has never been amended. Sec. 1132(b)-(c) required the first reports to cover all EXISTING SAPs and five prior fiscal years of budget history.

timeline.label: Congress first requires DoD to report special access programs
timeline.text: President Reagan signs Public Law 100-180. Section 1132(a)(1) adds section 119 to title 10, creating for the first time a statutory duty to tell the defense committees that a special access program exists. Every alleged legacy activity from the 1940s to this date ran under no SAP reporting obligation at all. The same section creates the subsection (e) waiver in the same breath.

timeline.label: John Lear's statement is dated, eighteen months before Lazar reaches KLAS
timeline.text: A statement by John Lear dated 29 December 1987, originally a physical letter to the Borderland Sciences Research Foundation and preserved in the BSRA/BSRF holdings at the Archives for the Unexplained, circulated on the ParaNet bulletin board in early 1988. It precedes Lazar's KLAS appearance by roughly eighteen months and set the frame the later account fitted into. Only the archive item record was opened; the statement's text was not rendered and no content from it is asserted.
timeline.source: John Lear's Dec. 29, 1987 Statement, Internet Archive item, https://archive.org/details/john-lear-statement-1987

timeline.label: Lear develops his Dulce hypothesis, sourced to 'Ann West'
timeline.text: Hayakawa's chronology dates Lear's Dulce hypothesis to 1988 and names his source as a woman called Ann West, the same name Levesque later gives as the raw material of the two original Dulce Base articles.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 29 August 2016, https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2016/08/29/enigmatic-personalities-behind-the-initial-dulce-underground-base-rumors/comment-page-1/

timeline.label: Bennewitz hospitalised
timeline.text: After eight years of fabricated material fed to him through AFOSI channels, Paul Bennewitz is hospitalised for psychiatric care and withdraws from the field.

timeline.label: Christic Institute sanctioned
timeline.text: Judge James Lawrence King dismisses Avirgan v. Hull and orders Daniel Sheehan's Christic Institute to pay $955,000 in fees and $79,500 in costs under Rule 11, criticising reliance on witnesses who were dead, unwilling, or one person removed from the facts. Recorded because the same evidentiary pattern recurs in the UAP context and hostile reviewers will reach for this first.

timeline.label: Air show at Norton AFB; SR-71A 61-7962 flies and departs
timeline.text: A private photographic collection of Blackbird aircraft carries a section headed 'Norton Air Force Base Airshow, November 12, 1988', with captions including 'SR-71A 61-7962 at Norton AFB on November 12, 1988' and 'The crew of SR-71A 61-7962 shake hands before departing the November 12, 1988 Norton Air Force Base airshow'. This is the only opened record that dates the air show independently of the ARV account.
timeline.source: air-and-space.com, Lockheed A-12 / YF-12 / SR-71 Blackbirds collection, https://www.air-and-space.com/Lockheed%20A-12%20YF-12%20SR-71%20Blackbirds.htm

timeline.label: CLAIMED ONLY: a classified exhibit in the Big Hangar with three saucer-shaped craft
timeline.text: The load-bearing claim of the whole thread, and it rests on one second-hand chain. McCandlish's December 2000 testimony gives the date and the day: Sorensen 'told me how he had seen these three flying saucers in this hangar at Norton Air Force Base on November 12, 1988 - it was a Saturday.' The 1990 primary document, taken from the claimed eyewitness himself, places it only 'in early Nov. 88'. No record of any exhibit was opened.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document section 3.8.5, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt ; Scott interview notes transcript p 1, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: Lazar's claimed employment at S-4 begins
timeline.text: In his 1991 narration Lazar says that 'between December of 88 and April of 89' he worked at 'a facility at an area known as S4 on the Nellis Air Force range in central Nevada', and that 'I was hired in December of 1988 to replace one of these men'. This row records the claim and its date, not any employment.
timeline.source: The Lazar Tape, Tri-Dot Productions, 1991, captions at 1:54 and 34:44, https://archive.org/details/antigravity

timeline.label: Robert Jacobs publishes his own account of the Big Sur filming
timeline.text: Bob Jacobs, Ph.D., 'Deliberate Deception: The Big Sur UFO Filming', MUFON UFO Journal No. 249, January 1989. He gives his post as Officer-in-Charge of Photo-optical Instrumentation in the 1369th Photographic Squadron at Vandenberg AFB from May 1963 to May 1966, and dates the event, uncertainly, to 2, 3 or 15 September 1964. TWELVE YEARS BEFORE THE DISCLOSURE PROJECT, AND THE ANCHOR THE BOARD SHOULD USE FOR THIS WITNESS.
timeline.source: Bob Jacobs, Ph.D., 'Deliberate Deception: The Big Sur UFO Filming', MUFON UFO Journal No. 249, January 1989, reprinted by NICAP, http://www.nicap.org/reports/bigsur2.htm

timeline.label: Status Report V
timeline.text: 'Is the Coverup Lid Lifting?' surveys Roswell, Aztec, Kingman, El Yunque and Brown County, Ohio, and argues that confirming a single retrieval would compel eventual sharing of alien propulsion and materials technology.

timeline.label: George Knapp begins interviewing Lazar
timeline.text: Tom Mahood's timeline records that Knapp began conducting initial interviews with Lazar in March 1989 'for safekeeping purposes'. No 1989-dated artefact was opened and this row is Tier 3 evidence carried on a Tier C node.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood, 'The Robert Lazar Timeline', https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/the-lazar-timeline/

timeline.label: First Wednesday desert viewing in Tikaboo Valley
timeline.text: Lazar, his wife, Gene Huff and John Lear watched lights in Tikaboo Valley. Mahood's timeline records that only Lear saw an elliptical shape through a telescope. Huff's own synopsis of 12 March 1995 gives the same date.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood's timeline and Gene Huff's synopsis, https://www.dreamlandresort.com/area51/lazar/synopsis.htm

timeline.label: Third viewing ends with the group detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff
timeline.text: On the third Wednesday viewing the group, which included Lazar, Gene Huff and John Lear, was discovered by guards and detained by the Lincoln County Sheriff. Both the claimants' own accounts and the principal sceptical account agree this happened; they disagree about what the group was watching. Tom Mahood's counter-explanation is that the whole alien-craft narrative began as a cover story after this detention.
timeline.source: Gene Huff's synopsis, 12 March 1995, and Tom Mahood's timeline and 2018 retrospective, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/looking-at-the-bob-lazar-story-from-the-perspective-of-2018/

timeline.label: KLAS-TV airs the silhouetted interviews under the pseudonym 'Dennis'
timeline.text: TIER 3 DATE, CARRIED HONESTLY. Tom Mahood's timeline records that in May 1989 Lazar's silhouetted interviews with George Knapp aired on KLAS-TV using the pseudonym 'Dennis'. NO 1989-DATED ARTEFACT WAS OPENED BY THIS BOARD, and KLAS's own retrospectives returned HTTP 403 three times on 18 September 2026.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood, 'The Robert Lazar Timeline', https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/the-lazar-timeline/

timeline.label: Lazar goes on television in Las Vegas
timeline.text: George Knapp broadcasts the Robert Lazar interviews on KLAS-TV, creating the public reverse-engineering narrative attached to Area 51 and S-4. No primary record has ever corroborated it.

timeline.label: Cooper's paper is dated; it names Four Corners reservations and never says Dulce
timeline.text: 'The Secret Government', dated on its own first page and delivered at the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas on 2 July 1989, carries the frame that 'These alien bases would be constructed under Indian reservations in the Four Corners area of Utah, Colorado, New Mexico and Arizona'. The string 'Dulce' occurs ZERO times in its forty-nine pages, which were extracted and searched in full. Cooper grades the paper himself: 'this chapter must be termed a hypothesis'.
timeline.source: Milton William Cooper, 'The Secret Government', 23 May 1989 updated 21 November 1990, https://robscholtemuseum.nl/wp-content/uploads/2016/01/The-Secret-Government.pdf

timeline.label: Moore's AFOSI admission
timeline.text: At the MUFON symposium in Las Vegas, William L. Moore states publicly that he had cooperated with Air Force Office of Special Investigations personnel from about 1980 and had knowingly passed disinformation to Paul Bennewitz.

timeline.label: Moore admits the AFOSI collaboration
timeline.text: At the MUFON symposium Bill Moore tells the UFO community that he worked with Air Force counterintelligence and knowingly passed disinformation to Bennewitz in exchange for access.

timeline.label: Moore admits the Bennewitz deception
timeline.text: William Moore states publicly that he attempted to push Bennewitz toward a breakdown by feeding him false information. Bennewitz had been hospitalised in August 1988; he dies 23 June 2003.

timeline.label: Knapp airs Lazar
timeline.text: George Knapp's KLAS-TV broadcast reveals Bob Lazar's identity and his S-4 claims, putting Area 51 into global consciousness and establishing the template of the insider-plus-local-reporter disclosure.

timeline.label: Knapp broadcasts the S-4 reverse-engineering claim
timeline.text: George Knapp reports Bob Lazar's account of working on recovered craft at S-4 near Groom Lake, employed through EG&G. The modern contractor-custody narrative starts here.

timeline.label: KLAS-TV identifies and interviews Lazar under his own name
timeline.text: TIER 3 DATE, CARRIED HONESTLY. Mahood's timeline gives 10 November 1989; some accounts give 11 November. This is the broadcast that put Area 51 into worldwide public consciousness and no artefact of it was opened by this board. The only contemporaneous documentary confirmation opened is the Las Vegas Review-Journal of 19 June 1990 recording that Lazar 'was the focal point for much of KLAS-TV, Channel 8 reporter George Knapp's award winning series'.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood's timeline; and Las Vegas Review-Journal, 19 June 1990, p 8B, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/lv-review-journal-6-19-1990/

timeline.label: The Belgian Air Force scrambles F-16s during the Belgian wave
timeline.text: The National Archives' guide to the MoD UFO files opened in August 2009 states that the files 'reveal how in March 1990 the Belgian Air Force scrambled F-16 fighters to intercept UFOs reported by police officers and others', and places a four-page account by General Wilfried de Brouwer, Chief of Operations, Belgian Air Staff, in DEFE 24/1960, confirming that the F-16 pilots obtained radar lock-ons but could not explain the phenomena. Malcolm Rifkind later told Lord Hill-Norton that the MoD was not informed at the time.
timeline.source: The National Archives, Highlights Guide to the MoD UFO files opened 17 August 2009, https://cdn.nationalarchives.gov.uk/documents/aug-2009-highlights-guide.pdf

timeline.label: Lazar arrested for pandering in Las Vegas
timeline.text: Mahood's timeline records the arrest on 5 June 1990. The offence, per the police account printed in the Review-Journal a fortnight later, was recruiting a prostitute, operating her business from an apartment complex, maintaining computer records of customers and their licence plate numbers, and taking at least half her earnings.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood's timeline; and Las Vegas Review-Journal, 19 June 1990, p 8B

timeline.label: Guilty plea to felony pandering
timeline.text: Lazar pleaded guilty to felony pandering in District Court. The Las Vegas Review-Journal reported it the next day under the headline 'Source in Channel 8's UFO series pleads guilty to pandering charge', by Warren Bates, page 8B, noting the exposure as 'one to six years, with a possible fine of $5,000'.
timeline.source: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 19 June 1990, p 8B, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/lv-review-journal-6-19-1990/

timeline.label: Pre-Sentence Report records the Pacifica, MIT and Caltech credential list
timeline.text: THE SPINE OF THE CREDENTIAL QUESTION. Lazar's Pre-Sentence Report of 27 July 1990 lists his own reported education: '1978, Bachelor of Science Degree in Physics and Electronic Technology, Pacifica University'; '1982, Masters of Science in Physics, MIT'; '1985, Masters of Science in Electronic Technology, Cal Tech'. Because this is a court document rather than a television statement, the credential question is Tier 1 evidence and not gossip. No institution has confirmed any of the three. Gene Huff's rebuttal of 15 May 1995, that the probation officer misread two Pacifica correspondence courses, is carried beside it and is not adopted.
timeline.source: Pre-Sentence Report, Clark County, Nevada, 27 July 1990, quoted by Tom Mahood, https://www.dreamlandresort.com/area51/lazar/hf-acad.htm

timeline.label: Scott's handwritten sheet headed 'Mark - 8/13/90'
timeline.text: One of the handwritten sheets on Aviation Week & Space Technology letterhead in the 31 page scan is headed, circled, 'Mark - 8/13/90'. It is the earliest dated page in the document.
timeline.source: Scott interview notes, pages 1 to 2 of the scan, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: Sentenced by Judge Jack Lehman to probation, community service and psychotherapy
timeline.text: District Judge Jack Lehman sentenced Lazar to probation rather than prison, with 150 hours of community service, an order to 'stay away from brothels and undergo psychotherapy', and a year of psychotherapy, saying he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'. The same report describes Lazar's claim as of that date as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas', which is a different named place from the one the claim later settled on.
timeline.source: Las Vegas Review-Journal, 21 August 1990, p 2C, by Warren Bates, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/lv-review-journal-8-21-1990/

timeline.label: Chief Financial Officers Act; FASAB created
timeline.text: The CFO Act imposes audited financial statements on major federal agencies. In the same month the Secretary of the Treasury, the Director of OMB and the Comptroller General create the Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board to set federal accounting standards. The Department of Defense will not attempt a full-scope audit for twenty-seven years.

timeline.label: YEAR INFERRED: Aviation Week prints McCandlish's paintings of two aircraft
timeline.text: The 1990 interview notes state 'Brad is the source of artwork done by Mark McCandlish and featured in AVWK's Oct. 1 issue.' The year is 1990 only by the document's own December 1990 dating, and the issue itself was NOT OPENED. It is the highest-value gap on this lead.
timeline.source: Scott interview notes transcript p 1, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: Scott interviews 'Brad' for one hour in his Pasadena office, on two tapes
timeline.text: William B. Scott, senior engineering editor of Aviation Week & Space Technology, interviewed the claimed eyewitness for one paid hour: 'He agreed to a one-hr. session in his Pasadena office, pointedly telling me that he gets $200/hr. for his time, and one hr. was all he could give me.' Internal markers show two tapes.
timeline.source: Scott interview notes transcript pp 1 and 5, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: Handwritten addendum: 'As of 12/10/90 - additional info from Brad'
timeline.text: Page 16 of the transcript carries a handwritten addendum in the same hand, followed by notes on a diamond-shaped aircraft slowing to subsonic speeds to dispense weapons. The interview was followed up before the notes were compiled.
timeline.source: Scott interview notes transcript p 16, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: The 16 page transcript is compiled: 'COMPILED 12-11-90; SCOTT/AVWK LANCASTER'
timeline.text: The typed transcript is hand-numbered 1 to 16 and headed 'NOTES FROM INTERVIEW ON 12-3-90 WITH BRAD' and 'COMPILED 12-11-90; SCOTT/AVWK LANCASTER'. Nothing in the 31 pages is a published article; Aviation Week printed the artwork, not the interview.
timeline.source: Scott interview notes transcript p 1, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf

timeline.label: The Lazar Tape fixes the whole claim in datable form
timeline.text: Tri-Dot Productions publishes 'The Lazar Tape and Excerpts from the Government Bible', forty minutes, created by Gene Huff and Bob Lazar. It is the strongest artefact in the cluster and the one opened by this board: its English auto-generated captions, 1,046 segments to 38:39, were read in full on 18 September 2026. Every element-115 claim, every S-4 description and the Teller anecdote carry timestamps in it.
timeline.source: Internet Archive item 'antigravity', https://archive.org/details/antigravity ; captions via YouTube video kc10m6HFbDE

timeline.label: Air Force contractor reports no detectable propulsive force in high vacuum
timeline.text: Robert L. Talley, 'Twenty First Century Propulsion Concept', PL-TR-91-3009, final report for February 1989 to July 1990 on contract FO4611-89-C-0023, Phillips Laboratory, Air Force Systems Command, Edwards AFB. Quoted in NASA/CR-2004-213312: 'Direct experimental results show that under high vacuum conditions... no detectable propulsive force was electrostatically induced by applying a static potential difference... between test device electrodes.' THE TALLEY REPORT ITSELF HAS NOT BEEN OPENED BY THIS BOARD.
timeline.source: NASA/CR-2004-213312, quoting Talley PL-TR-91-3009, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040171929/downloads/20040171929.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: UFO Crash at Roswell
timeline.text: Randle and Schmitt publish the book that drives Roswell into congressional attention. Haut, described as 'not a witness' in 1980, now appears as a witness, though not to the debris.

timeline.label: Senate Appropriations opens the first contractor inquiry
timeline.text: Richard D'Amato, staffer to Senate Democratic Leader Robert C. Byrd, is tasked to inquire into the New Mexico crash allegations. He visits the Nevada facility and reports back that nothing merits further Senate investigation.

timeline.label: The 30-day pre-initiation bar takes effect
timeline.text: 10 U.S.C. 119(f) -- 'A special access program may not be initiated until (1) the defense committees are notified of the program; and (2) a period of 30 days elapses' -- was added by Pub. L. 101-510 sec. 1482(a)(2) and took effect 1 October 1991 per sec. 1482(d). Before that date no statutory waiting period applied. Subsection (f) is not among the subsections that (e)(1) permits the Secretary to waive.

timeline.label: The Plains of San Agustin Controversy
timeline.text: Mark Rodeghier of CUFOS and Fred Whiting of the Fund for UFO Research publish an investigation concluding against Gerald Anderson, the only claimed first-hand witness to the second 1947 crash site. The field audits its own star witness and publishes against interest.

timeline.label: Yamato-1 becomes the world's first superconducting MHD-propelled ship
timeline.text: Trial runs of the Ship and Ocean Foundation's experimental vessel, begun as a committee in 1985 under the chairmanship of Yohei Sasakawa and laid down in 1989. THE CONTROL CASE FOR THE WHOLE STRAND: the mechanism the ARV literature offers as evidence of recovered technology was built in public by a civil maritime foundation and reported at an international conference two years later.
timeline.source: OSTI record and abstract, Sasakawa, Takezawa, Sugawara and Kyotani, World Congress on Superconductivity vol. 1, https://www.osti.gov/biblio/135352 , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: NRO's existence declassified
timeline.text: After 31 years the Deputy Secretary of Defense authorises acknowledgement that the National Reconnaissance Office exists. The precedent cuts both ways: it proves concealment at scale is possible, and it proves it eventually ends.

timeline.label: The project engineer answers Jacobs in print
timeline.text: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Vol. 17, No. 2, Winter 1993, pages 180 to 186. He identifies himself as the project engineer, confirms that Jacobs was named on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron, publishes team photographs, fixes the date and launch, explains the imagery as decoy and chaff deployment, and states that Jacobs was not authorised to view the film.
timeline.source: Kingston A. George, 'The Big Sur UFO: An Identified Flying Object', Skeptical Inquirer, Vol. 17, No. 2, Winter 1993, pages 180 to 186; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/1993/01/22165151/p77.pdf

timeline.label: The project engineer answers Jacobs and confirms his unit, role and debriefing
timeline.text: Kingston A. George, Skeptical Inquirer Vol. 17, Winter 1993, pp 180-187, identifies himself as the project engineer, writes that 'Bob was named the on-site commander by the 1369th Photo Squadron and managed the logistics of the operation at the Big Sur location', publishes two group photographs and captions Jacobs into both, names Major Florenz Mansmann and CWO Guy Spooner, dates the event to 22 September 1964 on an Atlas launch nicknamed Buzzing Bee, concedes Jacobs's point about lasers, and disputes only what was on the film.
timeline.source: Kingston A. George, Skeptical Inquirer Vol. 17, Winter 1993, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/1993/01/22165151/p77.pdf

timeline.label: Rockefeller Initiative begins
timeline.text: Laurance Rockefeller begins funding a coordinated campaign to obtain presidential declassification of US government UFO holdings.

timeline.label: O'Donnell says nothing to the Senate investigator
timeline.text: Knapp arranges a meeting between Al O'Donnell of EG&G and D'Amato with the blessing of EG&G co-founder Herbert Grier. O'Donnell, who had privately described a recovered saucer and a live being, tells the investigator nothing.

timeline.label: The Rich remark
timeline.text: Ben Rich is reported to have told a UCLA alumni audience that the means to travel among the stars already exist but are locked inside black projects. No recording or transcript has ever been produced.

timeline.label: E.O. 12829 creates the National Industrial Security Program
timeline.text: 58 FR 3479. Section 101: 'There is established a National Industrial Security Program. The purpose of this program is to safeguard classified information that may be released or has been released to current, prospective, or former contractors, licensees, or grantees.' The Secretary of Defense as Executive Agent issues the NISPOM; the DCSA carve-out is a carve-out from this program.

sources.name: E.O. 12829, 58 FR 3479 (reproduced in notes to 50 U.S.C. 3161, Cornell LII)

timeline.label: Executive Order 12829 creates the National Industrial Security Program
timeline.text: The order directs the Secretary of Defense to issue and maintain the NISP Operating Manual and designates the Defense Security Service as the DoD Cognizant Security Office - creating the inspection function that a carve-out would later switch off.

timeline.label: More than thirty sightings over central England in six hours, then a rocket re-entry
timeline.text: The MoD's UFO desk had the RAF replay radar tapes and 'found nothing unusual had been detected'; the Assistant Chief of the Air Staff was nonetheless briefed 'that there was evidence a UFO had evaded UK defences'. The same official guide then records that 'It soon emerged that the majority of sightings were caused by the Russian rocket that launched the Cosmos 2238 satellite, re-entering the earths atmosphere.' Both halves are in one paragraph of one guide.
timeline.source: The National Archives, Highlights Guide to the MoD UFO files opened 17 August 2009, https://cdn.nationalarchives.gov.uk/documents/aug-2009-highlights-guide.pdf

timeline.label: Haut's sworn affidavit
timeline.text: Walter Haut signs an affidavit stating that Col. Blanchard saw the material, that there is no chance Blanchard would have mistaken it for a weather balloon and none that Marcel would have been mistaken.

timeline.label: The government-wide SAP statute -- with DoD, NNSA and the IC written out of it
timeline.text: Sec. 1152 of the FY1994 NDAA, Pub. L. 103-160, 107 Stat. 1758, now 50 U.S.C. 3348. Subsection (g)(2)(B) excludes the Department of Defense, the National Nuclear Security Administration, and every element of the Intelligence Community from the definition of 'covered department or agency'. Its waiver at (e)(2) keeps the audience at the full oversight committees rather than reducing it to chairs and ranking members.

timeline.label: The government-wide SAP statute and the only statutory definition
timeline.text: Section 1152 of the FY1994 NDAA, Public Law 103-160, imposes the same reporting regime on every federal agency that runs a SAP other than DoD, the nuclear weapons complex and the intelligence community, and supplies the only statutory definition of 'special access program' in the United States Code, now at 50 U.S.C. 3348(g)(3).

timeline.label: Baltimore Sun reports the Testors SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart on sale
timeline.text: 'Testor Corp. released the SR-75 Penetrator and XR-7 Thunderdart, the latest in a series of highly speculative military miniature models', designed by 'John Andrews, an aviation historian in San Diego who designed the new models, as well as the F-19'. The Air Force spokeswoman Capt. Mary Dillon is quoted: 'We're not saying no comment, we're saying such a plane does not exist.' Fouche's presentation of August 1998 presents the same SR-75 Penetrator designation and the same mothership architecture as inside knowledge.
timeline.source: Baltimore Sun, https://www.baltimoresun.com/1993/12/25/for-latest-spy-plane-look-under-your-tree-2/

timeline.label: Alcubierre publishes the warp-drive metric, and states that exotic matter will be needed
timeline.text: Classical and Quantum Gravity 11-5, L73-L77. Its abstract closes: 'just as it happens with wormholes, exotic matter will be needed in order to generate a distortion of spacetime like the one discussed here.' The body states that the metric 'violates all three energy conditions' and that the energy density seen by Eulerian observers 'is everywhere negative'. The word 'device' appears zero times in the paper.
timeline.source: Miguel Alcubierre, 'The warp drive: hyper-fast travel within general relativity', read from the author's arXiv posting, https://arxiv.org/abs/gr-qc/0009013 , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Rep. Schiff directs GAO to search the records
timeline.text: After DoD refers his Roswell inquiry to the National Archives rather than answering it, Representative Steven Schiff orders a government-wide GAO records audit.

timeline.label: The 1994 SAP restructuring
timeline.text: Gerb argues the Special Access Program enterprise was restructured in 1994 to gatekeep US government access and vest permanent control of the portfolio in a quasi-industry and government control group - the moment, on this account, at which the government ceased to be the controlling party in its own programme.

timeline.label: Groom Lake contractors sue
timeline.text: Kasza v. Browner and Frost v. Perry allege exposure to hazardous waste burned in open pits. Judge Philip Pro rejects the state secrets claim; the suits are dismissed for lack of evidence and the Ninth Circuit affirms.

timeline.label: The Deputy Secretary of Defense stands up the SAPOC, sixteen years before the directive the board cites
timeline.text: 'On January 5th, 1994, the Deputy Secretary of Defense (DEPSECDEF) significantly enhanced changes in the DoD Special Access Program (SAP) management and control structures. ... The plan standardized and formalized the SAP approval, termination, revalidation and restructuring process through the Special Access Program Oversight Committee (SAPOC). A Senior Review Group (SRG) was established to support the SAPOC principals.' The Joint Security Commission called the committee a 'recent formation' on 28 February 1994. The board's sapoc node dated the committee to DoD Directive 5205.07 of 1 July 2010; the 2010 issuance re-established a body that had run since 1994.
timeline.source: Deputy Secretary of Defense, Special Access Program Oversight Committee, Information Bulletin, November 1994, as transcribed at https://sgp.fas.org/othergov/sapoc.html

timeline.label: Status Report VII
timeline.text: 'Search for Proof in a Hall of Mirrors', Stringfield's last, opens with Walter Scott's 'I say the tale as 'twas told to me' and acknowledges the Fund for UFO Research, MUFON, CUFOS and the Mid-Ohio Research Associates. He dies ten months later.

timeline.label: The Navy codifies the NCIS title, and it is not 1992
timeline.text: A Department of the Navy final rule amends 32 CFR 701.5(e)(2)(iii)(B) by removing 'Commander, Naval Investigative Service Command' and adding in its place 'Director, Naval Criminal Investigative Service'. A Navy document published eight days earlier still lists the old title among the officers it designates. This is the earliest federal record of the new name reached by this pass; the commonly cited 1992 redesignation date is supported by nothing opened.
timeline.source: Federal Register Doc 94-13966, Availability of Department of the Navy Records and Publication of Department of the Navy Documents Affecting the Public, 9 June 1994, https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/1994/06/09/94-13966/availability-of-department-of-the-navy-records-and-publication-of-department-of-the-navy-documents

timeline.label: Air Force report to GAO
timeline.text: Col. Richard L. Weaver, Director of Security and Special Program Oversight in the Office of the Secretary of the Air Force, and 1st Lt. James McAndrew deliver the report concluding the debris was Project Mogul. It also records that the Secretary released former airmen and contract scientists from nondisclosure obligations in writing.

timeline.label: Air Force abandons the weather balloon story
timeline.text: Under pressure from Rep. Steven Schiff the Air Force concedes the 1947 statement was false and attributes the debris to the then-classified Project MOGUL.

timeline.label: NIDS founded
timeline.text: Robert Bigelow founds the National Institute for Discovery Science in Las Vegas, assembling the staff and methodology later inherited by BAASS.

timeline.label: 'The Best Available Evidence' distributed
timeline.text: Marie Galbraith's Rockefeller-funded briefing document goes to legislators, senior officials and heads of state. No policy response follows.

timeline.label: STARGATE declassified and terminated
timeline.text: CIA releases roughly 12,000 pages of the remote-viewing programme record and the effort is closed - the one case where a compartmented programme in a ridiculed domain was fully documented after the fact.

timeline.label: The President exempts a place that officially does not exist
timeline.text: Clinton issues a determination exempting 'the Air Force's operating location near Groom Lake, Nevada' from environmental disclosure law - the only formal recognition to that date that Groom Lake is more than part of the Nellis complex. It is reissued annually.

timeline.label: STAR GATE is terminated
timeline.text: CIA's AIR evaluation finds remote viewing information 'vague and ambiguous' and unusable for actionable intelligence. The roughly $20 million programme ends; the records are published to CREST in January 2017.

timeline.label: Schneider supplies the specification: seven levels, 2.5 miles, a 1979 firefight
timeline.text: At Post Falls, Idaho he said he had been 'involved in building an addition to the deep underground military base at Dulce', that 'It goes down seven levels and over 2.5 miles deep', and that in a cavern there he shot two aliens and about seventy people were killed. The hosting page's own introduction gives a different casualty figure, sixty-six. He was not part of the initial rumours and arrived about fifteen years after they began.
timeline.source: Transcript of Phil Schneider's May 1995 Post Falls, Idaho lecture, https://www.difoet.dk/www.raven1.net/mcf/underground-bases.htm

timeline.label: GAO finds the records destroyed
timeline.text: GAO reports that RAAF outgoing messages (Oct 1946 - Dec 1949) and administrative records (Mar 1945 - Dec 1949) were destroyed, and that the disposition form does not record who destroyed them, when, or under what authority.

timeline.label: GAO: Roswell records destroyed, authority unknown
timeline.text: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 finds RAAF administrative records (Mar 1945-Dec 1949) and outgoing messages (Oct 1946-Dec 1949) destroyed, with the disposition form recording neither who destroyed them nor under what authority.

timeline.label: GAO reports Roswell message traffic destroyed
timeline.text: GAO/NSIAD-95-187, produced at Rep. Steven Schiff's request, finds that Roswell Army Air Field outgoing messages for March 1945 to December 1949 were destroyed with no destruction certificate located to authorise it.

timeline.label: GAO finds the Roswell records destroyed
timeline.text: GAO/NSIAD-95-187 reports that RAAF outgoing messages from October 1946 to December 1949 were destroyed with no disposition authority located. No agency has ever rebutted it.

timeline.label: Clintons visit Rockefeller's JY Ranch
timeline.text: The President and First Lady visit Laurance Rockefeller in Jackson, Wyoming - documented in Clinton Library FOIA collection 2006-0546-F, and the occasion on which Rockefeller is reported to have pressed the disclosure case directly.

timeline.label: First presidential Groom Lake exemption published
timeline.text: A Presidential Determination exempting 'the Air Force's Operating Location Near Groom Lake, Nevada' from federal environmental disclosure requirements appears in the Federal Register. It is repeated annually thereafter.

timeline.label: Petition to withdraw the 1990 guilty plea is refused
timeline.text: Lazar petitioned to withdraw the plea, citing post-traumatic stress, hidden federal records and inadequate legal representation. The District Attorney opposed, arguing 'that Lazar's new claims were irrelevant to his admitted and documented criminal activity'. The judge denied the petition and the conviction stands.
timeline.source: Douglas Dean Johnson, 31 January 2021, https://douglasjohnson.ghost.io/bob-lazar-and-his-nevada-felony-conviction/

timeline.label: Salas goes on the record and locates Meiwald himself
timeline.text: Robert Salas went public with the Oscar Flight account in a 1996 interview with the Great Falls Tribune, and in the summer of that year located his former missile commander Frederick Meiwald, who wrote to him about the incident on 1 October 1996. Robert Hastings separately states he tape-recorded a telephone conversation with Meiwald in August 1996. Salas approaching a newspaper himself is a different provenance from the witnesses who reach the public only through an interviewer.
timeline.source: Robert Hastings, 'The Echo and Oscar Flight Incidents', https://www.ufohastings.com/articles/the-echo-and-oscar-flight-incidents

timeline.label: NASA establishes the Breakthrough Propulsion Physics Project
timeline.text: From its own summary document: 'This emerging science, combined with the realization that rockets are fundamentally inadequate for interstellar exploration, led NASA to establish the "Breakthrough Propulsion Physics (BPP)" Project in 1996.' Three grand challenges: propellantless propulsion, hyper-fast travel, and breakthrough spacecraft power.
timeline.source: NASA/TM-2004-213082, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040070788/downloads/20040070788.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Bigelow buys the Utah ranch
timeline.text: Bigelow purchases the Uintah Basin property later known as Skinwalker Ranch and begins instrumented NIDS study under Colm Kelleher.

timeline.label: Bigelow buys Skinwalker Ranch
timeline.text: The 480-acre Sherman property in Uintah County, Utah is purchased with a condition that the sellers keep quiet about what they had witnessed; a research team and surveillance equipment move in.

timeline.label: Knapp joins NIDS
timeline.text: Knapp works with Robert Bigelow's National Institute of Discovery Science alongside Colm Kelleher; this period produces the Skinwalker Ranch material and the Reid-Bigelow introduction that leads to AAWSAP.

timeline.label: Dark Skies airs
timeline.text: Bryce Zabel creates and showruns Dark Skies, a prime-time dramatisation of a Majestic-12-style control group - a dateable marker of how long the control-group narrative has been in mass circulation.

timeline.label: Bechtel Nevada takes the Nevada Test Site contract
timeline.text: Bechtel Nevada becomes DOE management and operating contractor for the Nevada Test Site, running the Remote Sensing Laboratory and Special Technologies Laboratory under Atomic Energy Act authorities outside the DoD SAP regime.

timeline.label: Carnegie tests the Howe samples
timeline.text: Linda Moulton Howe says the bismuth/magnesium-zinc laminate was tested by Carnegie Science's Department of Terrestrial Magnetism, the first documented laboratory in that chain of custody.

timeline.label: Schneider dies in Clackamas County, Oregon; the record is thin and contested
timeline.text: His memorial record gives death on 11 January 1996 in Clackamas County, Oregon, cremated. The date in circulation, tied to the discovery of the body, is 17 January 1996. NO DEATH CERTIFICATE, MEDICAL EXAMINER'S REPORT OR POLICE REPORT WAS OPENED, and neither the suicide ruling nor the contest to it is carried as a claim anywhere in this file.
timeline.source: Find a Grave memorial 146890828, https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/146890828/phil-schneider

timeline.label: The Varginha encounter
timeline.text: Three young women in Varginha, Minas Gerais report a crouching creature with red eyes and three fingers; a week earlier an ultralight pilot reported a cylindrical craft coming down outside the town. Rumours of military recovery and of an American removal follow. A 2010 Brazilian military inquiry attributes the sighting to a mentally disabled man and routine vehicle movements.

timeline.label: TACIT BLUE placed on public museum display
timeline.text: 'The aircraft was placed on display at the museum in May 1996.' A real compartmented aircraft programme of the Groom Lake era ends in a public exhibition hall with a published fact sheet and a cockpit plaque naming its five pilots.
timeline.source: U.S. Air Force Fact Sheet 'NORTHROP TACIT BLUE', https://nsarchive2.gwu.edu/NSAEBB/NSAEBB443/docs/area51_58.PDF

timeline.label: Physicist David L. Morgan publishes the physics critique
timeline.text: Dr David L. Morgan, a particle physicist, publishes 'A Physicist's Critique', revised April 2001. Three objections: that the strong nuclear force 'has NOTHING TO DO WITH GRAVITY'; that the nuclear force 'extends out to about the same distance away from a nucleus NO MATTER HOW MASSIVE THE NUCLEUS IS'; and, crucially without needing any model of gravity, that if the antimatter must be made on board then 'your system produces NO NET ENERGY AT ALL!!'
timeline.source: Dr David L. Morgan, 'A Physicist's Critique', https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/bluefire-main/bluefire/the-bob-lazar-corner/a-physicists-critique/

timeline.label: First intelligence budget disclosure in fifty years
timeline.text: Following FOIA litigation brought by the Federation of American Scientists with Steven Aftergood as plaintiff, assisted by Kate Martin of the Center for National Security Studies, the Director of Central Intelligence declassifies the total intelligence budget: $26.6 billion for FY1997. It is the first such disclosure since the CIA was created.

timeline.label: The Roswell Report: Case Closed
timeline.text: James McAndrew publishes the bodies report through HQ USAF and the GPO. Section 2.1 works the 427th AAFBU Squadron 'M' morning reports and National Personnel Records Center holdings to show Glenn Dennis's 'Naomi Maria Selff' never existed, and identifies 1st Lt. Eileen M. Fanton as matching every other particular.

timeline.label: CIA admits official deception
timeline.text: CIA's Studies in Intelligence publishes Gerald Haines's history, stating that reconnaissance secrecy 'led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public' and that mention of CIA sponsorship of the Robertson Panel was forbidden.

timeline.label: CIA publishes the U-2 cover-story admission
timeline.text: Gerald Haines' Studies in Intelligence history states that Blue Book investigators knowingly attributed U-2 sightings to ice crystals and temperature inversions and that 'this led the Air Force to make misleading and deceptive statements to the public.'

timeline.label: CIA publishes its own UFO history
timeline.text: Gerald K. Haines' 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-1990' appears in Studies in Intelligence, acknowledging the Office of Scientific Intelligence effort, the Robertson Panel and the later attribution of sightings to U-2 and OXCART overflights.

timeline.label: CIA concedes the false explanations
timeline.text: CIA historian Gerald K. Haines publishes 'CIA's Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947-90' in Studies in Intelligence, recording that U-2 and OXCART flights accounted for over half of late-1950s and 1960s reports and that Air Force investigators knowingly gave false explanations to the public. A documented admission of deliberate deception, from the deceiving agency.

timeline.label: Wilson's alleged SAP inquiry begins
timeline.text: Per the Davis notes, Joint Staff J-2 Vice Admiral Thomas Wilson - prompted by the Disclosure Project's Washington briefings - begins trying to locate a special access programme holding recovered non-human material.

timeline.label: 'The Roswell Report: Case Closed'
timeline.text: The Air Force attributes reported bodies to anthropomorphic test dummies dropped in parachute tests conducted principally between 1953 and 1959.

timeline.label: DoD FOIA case 97-F-1677 released
timeline.text: The Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense releases both the Halt memo and the November 1975 Malmstrom overflight records to The Black Vault in a single case.

timeline.label: CEFAA created in Chile
timeline.text: Gonzalo Miranda Aguirre, Director of Chile's Dirección General de Aeronáutica Civil, creates the Comité de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos after a sighting wave over Arica and the expressed interest of the former Air Force Commander-in-Chief. Ricardo Bermúdez takes the directorship and holds it until 2016.

timeline.label: Stanton Friedman publishes 'The Bob Lazar Fraud'
timeline.text: Friedman, a nuclear physicist who spent his career arguing that UFOs are real craft, publishes the credential investigation, updated January 2011. He located the professor Lazar named as a Caltech instructor: 'I located Dr. Duxler. He's a Pierce Junior College physics prof, and never taught at Caltech.' He records the directory page's own scope statement and describes the W-2 as totalling 'under $1000.00'. The heaviest denial in the cluster comes from a proponent, not a debunker.
timeline.source: Stanton T. Friedman, 'The Bob Lazar Fraud', https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-bob-lazar-fraud-2/

timeline.label: Alien Rapture: The Chosen published by Galde Press
timeline.text: First edition, Lakeville, Minnesota, Galde Press, 1998, xii and 275 pages, 23 cm, ISBN 1880090503, by Edgar Rothschild Fouche and Brad Steiger. The Library of Congress record gives only the year; no primary record for the month was opened. No copy of the text was opened, so how the TR-3B appears inside it is unestablished.
timeline.source: Library of Congress catalogue record LCCN 98002961, http://lx2.loc.gov:210/lcdb ; Open Library work record, https://openlibrary.org/works/OL1803180W.json

timeline.label: Second and last DCI disclosure, then nine years of silence
timeline.text: The DCI discloses $26.7 billion for FY1998 and then stops. No intelligence budget figure is published again until 2007, and then only because Congress compels it by statute.

timeline.label: The Air Force concedes the site exists
timeline.text: Forty-three years after establishment, the USAF acknowledges the existence of the operating location at Groom Lake - without describing anything done there.

timeline.label: Ninth Circuit dismisses the Groom Lake workers' suit
timeline.text: Kasza v. Browner, 133 F.3d 1159, sustains dismissal on state secrets and statutory exemption grounds. The Supreme Court denies certiorari at 525 U.S. 967. The facility's contents remain legally unspeakable.

timeline.label: The 7th Annual International UFO Congress Convention runs at Laughlin, and Fouche is not on its programme
timeline.text: A contemporaneous page for the '7th Annual International UFO Congress Convention Film Festival & EBE Awards' gives the dates 'February 1 thru 7, 1998' and the venue 'Gold River Resort, Laughlin, Nevada', and lists 24 speakers by name. Edgar Fouche is not among them. His own transcript is dated August 1998 and his own text says he spoke at Laughlin 'in August', which the Congress's separate summer sessions make consistent rather than contradictory, but no contemporaneous record placing him on any podium in 1998 was opened.
timeline.source: 1998 International UFO Congress main page, https://padrak.com/ufo/IUFOC_1998.html

timeline.label: THE LIBRARY OF CONGRESS CATALOGUES ALIEN RAPTURE AS SCIENCE FICTION
timeline.text: Library of Congress record LCCN 98002961, recordContentSource DLC, recordCreationDate 980204, carries the gsafd genre element 'Science fiction.', the subject heading 'Alien abduction - Fiction', the classification PS3556.O779 A79 1998, which is American literature, individual authors, 1961 onward, and the Dewey number 813/.54, American fiction. The cataloguing predates both the book's publication and the August presentation.
timeline.source: Library of Congress catalogue, SRU query bath.isbn=1880090503, MODS record, http://lx2.loc.gov:210/lcdb

timeline.label: THE ANCHOR: the presentation transcript that originates the TR-3B
timeline.text: A 62 page slide-cued speaking script headed 'Presentation to IUFOR by / Edgar Rothshild Fouche / Copyright Aug. 1998 / Fouche Media Associates'. Slide 5 names the book it was given to promote. Slides 69 to 72 give the TR-3B its designation and code name Astra, attribute it to 'the Top Secret, Aurora Program with SDI and black budget monies', name the NRO, NSA and CIA as funders and taskers, name Sandia and Livermore as developers of the propulsion, specify a mercury-based plasma 'at a temperature of 150 degrees Kelvin', and give the operational craft two different sizes two slides apart, 600 feet at slide 69 and 300 feet at slide 70.
timeline.source: Presentation to IUFOR by Edgar Rothshild Fouche, https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouche%20-%201998%20Presentation%20to%20IUFOC.pdf

timeline.label: Bigelow's first NIDS interview
timeline.text: Bigelow tells the Deseret News that anomalous aerial activity and animal deaths have continued around the ranch and that 'we wouldn't be there just for the weather,' while declining to discuss specifics.

timeline.label: The Defense Threat Reduction Agency is established, heir to AFSWP
timeline.text: DTRA is established in the Department of Defense as a combat support agency by DoD Directive 5105.62 of 30 September 1998, consolidating the Defense Special Weapons Agency, the On-Site Inspection Agency, the Defense Technology Security Administration and OSD arms control elements. Its own history states the line: 'The nation's oldest defense agency thus lives on; MED to AFSWP to DAS A to DNA to DSWA to DTRA.' The Atomic Energy Commission's own records are a separate National Archives group, RG 326, not RG 374.
timeline.source: Records of the Defense Threat Reduction Agency, Record Group 374, sec. 374.1, Guide to Federal Records in the National Archives, https://www.archives.gov/research/guide-fed-records/groups/374.html

timeline.label: COMETA publishes 'Les OVNI et la Défense'
timeline.text: A committee of French retired general officers, weapons engineers, an admiral and a national police chief, almost all IHEDN auditors, concludes that the physical reality of unknown flying objects is 'almost certain', that 'a single hypothesis sufficiently takes into account the facts ... the hypothesis of extraterrestrial visitors', and recommends that France 'initiate diplomatic demarches to the United States ... to urge the superpower to collaborate and, if necessary, exert useful pressure'.

timeline.label: NNSA gets its own SAP statute with the DoD-style waiver
timeline.text: Sec. 3236 of Pub. L. 106-65, 113 Stat. 962, creates 50 U.S.C. 2426. The waiver mirrors 10 U.S.C. 119(e): case-by-case adverse-national-security determination by the Administrator, after which the information goes jointly to the chairman and ranking minority member of each congressional defense committee.

sources.name: 50 U.S.C. 2426 (Cornell LII)

timeline.label: NNSA gets a SAP statute with a broader waiver than DoD's
timeline.text: Section 3236 of the FY2000 NDAA, Public Law 106-65, creates 50 U.S.C. 2426. Its subsection (e)(1) lets the NNSA Administrator waive not only the reports but the 30-day report-and-wait itself - the most permissive SAP provision in the Code, governing the agency that holds Restricted Data and runs Los Alamos, Sandia and Livermore.

timeline.label: A B-52 co-pilot approaches CUFOS on his own initiative
timeline.text: Capt. Bradford Runyon, co-pilot of JAG-31 on 24 October 1968, contacted the Center for UFO Studies in 2000 and completed a CUFOS questionnaire. The modern investigation of the Minot case begins there. A witness approached a research body; a research body did not recruit a witness. It is the control case against which the Malmstrom and Ellsworth provenance chains should be read.
timeline.source: Minot B-52 UFO case archive, https://minotb52ufo.com/doc.php

timeline.label: Project Condign reports
timeline.text: The UK Defence Intelligence Staff completes 'Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in the UK Air Defence Region' as Scientific & Technical Memorandum 55/2/00. Its key recommendation is that DI55 should no longer monitor UAP reports; its paragraph on 'Related Military Applications' is withheld under the defence exemption; its chapter on other countries denies any US or Canadian collaboration 'of any sort' and then redacts four lines.

timeline.label: NNSA established by Congress
timeline.text: The nuclear weapons complex is placed under a semi-autonomous agency inside DOE, consolidating the most capable custodial architecture in the government outside the DoD SAP system.

timeline.label: Lt Col John Williams's Disclosure Project testimony on a compartmented facility at Norton
timeline.text: Printed in the same document as McCandlish's. Williams says he 'was responsible for that base's facilities from 1981-82' and that 'I was never allowed in that area when I was there at Norton Air Force Base'. Greer cross-references the two testimonies to each other in bracketed notes signed 'SG'.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Clifford Stone's testimony recorded for the Disclosure Project
timeline.text: Printed at section 3.8.4 under 'Testimony of Sergeant Clifford Stone, United States Army / September 2000'. The editorial header: 'Stone has seen living and dead extraterrestrials in his official duties on an army team that retrieved crashed ET crafts.'
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Larry Warren's testimony recorded for the Disclosure Project
timeline.text: Printed at section 3.8.4 under 'Testimony of Security Officer Larry Warren, United States Air Force / September 2000'.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: John Callahan's testimony recorded for the Disclosure Project
timeline.text: Printed at section 3.8.2 under 'Testimony of FAA Division Chief John Callahan / October 2000'. TIER 1 FOR THE FACT OF THE TESTIMONY ONLY; the case he describes has its own federal record and his claimed title does not.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Robert Jacobs's testimony recorded for the Disclosure Project
timeline.text: Printed at section 3.8.3 under 'Testimony of Professor Robert Jacobs, Lt. US Air Force / November 2000'. The last and weakest of his three published accounts of the same event.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: McCandlish's Disclosure Project testimony is taken
timeline.text: Printed at section 3.8.5 under the heading 'Testimony of Mr. Mark McCandlish, US Air Force / December 2000'. It is where the claimed craft acquires the names Alien Reproduction Vehicle and Flux Liner in print, where the sizes are given as 24 / 60 / 'about 120 to 130 feet', and where the Frank Carlucci identification is published in his own voice and labelled as his own speculation.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document section 3.8.5, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Klass publishes Stone's service record and the 1987 FAA release
timeline.text: Skeptics UFO Newsletter #68, Summer 2001. It prints Clifford Stone's assignment history obtained from the National Personnel Records Center, quotes the FAA Alaskan Region press release of 5 March 1987 and the air traffic control transcript on JAL 1628, and records that twenty of sixty-nine interviewees spoke at the press conference. Klass declares that he was refused admission to the event.
timeline.source: Philip J. Klass, Skeptics UFO Newsletter (SUN) #68, Summer 2001, 'Dr. Greer's Disclosure Conference Reveals His New Strategy'; PDF downloaded and converted to text in full this session, https://cdn.centerforinquiry.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/29/2022/09/26195512/SUN-68-Summer-2001.pdf

timeline.label: The Disclosure Project Briefing Document is prepared by Greer and Loder
timeline.text: The roughly 500 page compilation prepared by Steven M. Greer MD and Theodore C. Loder III PhD, printing summarised witness testimony including McCandlish's of December 2000. It is the custody point for dozens of this board's witness claims.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Disclosure Project Briefing Document published
timeline.text: 'Written and Compiled by: Steven M. Greer, M.D., Director and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D. / April, 2001', addressed to members of the press, the US government and the US scientific community. Its section 3.8 prints sixty-eight dated witness testimonies across five subsections.
timeline.source: Disclosure Project Briefing Document, April 2001, written and compiled by Steven M. Greer, M.D., and Theodore C. Loder III, Ph.D.; full OCR text read this session, https://archive.org/stream/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument/DisclosureProjectBriefingDocument_djvu.txt

timeline.label: Disclosure Project press conference at the National Press Club
timeline.text: About twenty former government workers spoke, out of sixty-nine whose interviews appear in the accompanying book. ABC News covered it the same day. NO OPENED SOURCE LISTS THE TWENTY; five are placed at the podium by opened sources, namely Callahan, Stone, Filer, Sheehan and Webre.
timeline.source: ABC News, 'Group Calls for Disclosure of UFO Info', 9 May 2001, 2:35 PM, https://abcnews.com/Technology/story?id=98572&page=1

timeline.label: Disclosure Project press conference
timeline.text: Steven Greer presents about twenty former military and government witnesses at the National Press Club and demands congressional hearings with subpoena power. Global coverage; no hearing.

timeline.label: Greer's National Press Club event
timeline.text: Steven Greer stages the Disclosure Project press conference with twenty retired Air Force, FAA and intelligence officers, creating the format every subsequent disclosure event has followed.

timeline.label: FAA tells a FOIA requester the JAL 1628 records will be destroyed in 30 days
timeline.text: Letter of 27 June 2001: 'all documents pertaining to this UFO sighting will be destroyed in 30 days from the date of this letter.' A further request in 2009 was answered with the statement that the records had been destroyed. Over 1,500 pages were later found at the National Archives.
timeline.source: The Black Vault case file, 'The Vault Files: 1986 Alaska JAL Flight 1628', John Greenewald Jr., https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/the-vault-files-1986-alaska-jal-flight-1628/

timeline.label: Cooper is killed during an attempted arrest in Arizona
timeline.text: A sheriff's operation involving seventeen officers, with two deputies in plain clothes, on a 1998 federal warrant for tax evasion and bank fraud and a local warrant for aggravated assault with a deadly weapon. Cooper shot a deputy in the head and 'was killed by multiple shots before he made it inside'. The SPLC report gives 6 November; the date in general circulation is 5 November.
timeline.source: Southern Poverty Law Center, Intelligence Report, Spring 2002, issue 105, https://www.splcenter.org/resources/reports/conspiracy-theorist-slain-police-shootout/

timeline.label: CAUS still litigating against DoD
timeline.text: The Ninth Circuit decides Citizens Against UFO Secrecy, Inc. v. United States Department of Defense - twenty-four years after the organisation was founded.

timeline.label: NASA support for the project ends after six years and sixteen research tasks
timeline.text: 'NASA supported the Breakthrough Propulsion Physics Project from 1996 through 2002... Of 16 incremental research tasks completed by the project and from other sponsors, about a third were found not to be viable, a quarter have clear opportunities for sequels, and the rest remain unresolved.' The circumstances of the closure were not opened and are not asserted.
timeline.source: NASA/TM-2004-213082, abstract, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040070788/downloads/20040070788.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: UFOs and the National Security State vol. I
timeline.text: Richard Dolan publishes 'Chronology of a Cover-Up, 1941-1973', moving the field's argument from witness testimony to the documented architecture of American secrecy.

timeline.label: MITRE takes over JASON administration
timeline.text: The JASON contract passes to MITRE, placing the government's most sensitive standing scientific advisory panel inside the corporation that would be interrogated about UAP records 24 years later.

timeline.label: The Wilson-Davis meeting
timeline.text: Eric Davis takes fifteen pages of handwritten notes recording Admiral Thomas Wilson describing being refused access, on need-to-know grounds, to a SAP holding recovered non-human material in contractor custody.

timeline.label: Alleged Wilson meeting
timeline.text: The date attributed to Eric Davis's meeting with Vice Adm. Thomas R. Wilson recorded in the notes that surfaced in 2019 among Edgar Mitchell's papers, describing a special access programme that refused a former DIA director access.

timeline.label: Podesta calls for declassification
timeline.text: Six days after the Wilson meeting, the former White House Chief of Staff appears at the National Press Club for the Coalition for Freedom of Information and demands the government open its UFO files.

timeline.label: The sealed Haut affidavit
timeline.text: Donald Schmitt composes and emails a further affidavit which Haut signs at the International UFO Museum before his daughter and a notary, embargoed until after his death. It asserts first-hand sight of a craft and bodies, contradicting his 1979, 1989 and 1993 statements.

timeline.label: Vandenberg incursions during NRO launches (2003-2005)
timeline.text: Jeffrey Nuccetelli's testimony describes objects 'like flying buildings' over a space launch range during National Reconnaissance Office missions, each incident witnessed by multiple personnel, documented, investigated and reported up the chain. No Air Force series exists in RG 615 to hold those reports.

timeline.label: Kean's FOIA request
timeline.text: Leslie Kean files with NASA for records on Kecksburg, the 9 December 1965 incident, the Fragology Files 1962-1967, Richard M. Schulherr, Project Moon Dust and Cosmos 96. NASA answers 'no records' on 11 April 2003.

timeline.label: Bennewitz dies; buried at Santa Fe National Cemetery as a Coast Guard seaman
timeline.text: Paul Frederick Bennewitz Jr, born 30 September 1927, died 23 June 2003, Section 12 Site 402, marker inscribed 'S1C US COAST GUARD WORLD WAR II'. The man at the centre of the best-documented domestic disinformation operation in this subject was a Second World War Coast Guard seaman who ran a humidity-instrument company.
timeline.source: Find a Grave memorial 17482201, https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/17482201/paul_frederick-bennewitz

timeline.label: Vandenberg red square
timeline.text: Boeing contractors at Vandenberg AFB report a massive glowing red square hovering silently over two missile defense sites; security guards report a rectangular craft larger than a football field the same night.

timeline.label: A red square over the missile defense sites
timeline.text: Boeing contractors at Vandenberg report a massive glowing red square hovering silently over two missile defense sites; security personnel the same night describe a rectangular craft larger than a football field. A witness a week later is threatened and told to keep quiet.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA filed
timeline.text: Thirty-eight years to the day after Kecksburg, Kean sues NASA in the District of Columbia. The case is assigned to Judge Emmet G. Sullivan.

timeline.label: USS Reagan log pages removed
timeline.text: Multiple USS Ronald Reagan watchstanders observe an orange self-luminous object above the flight deck; a Boatswain's Mate of the Watch is ordered to 'rip it out' of the deck logbook and another witness sees an officer order pages removed.

timeline.label: NIDS closes; ranch retained
timeline.text: Bigelow shuts the institute but keeps Skinwalker Ranch. The cleared cadre remains intact and available.

timeline.label: Element 115 synthesis published in Physical Review C
timeline.text: Oganessian et al., 'Experiments on the synthesis of element 115 in the reaction 243Am(48Ca,xn)291-x115', Physical Review C 69, 021601(R), a Dubna and Lawrence Livermore collaboration. The isotopes are 287 and 288, at cross sections of roughly 1 and 3 picobarn, observed as chains of consecutive alpha decays running to completion within about twenty seconds and about half a second. Nothing about them is stable, machinable or storable.
timeline.source: Physical Review C 69, 021601(R), https://journals.aps.org/prc/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevC.69.021601

timeline.label: GAO reports it cannot vouch for DoD contractor security oversight
