timeline.text: GAO-04-332, 'Industrial Security: DOD Cannot Provide Adequate Assurances That Its Oversight Ensures the Protection of Classified Information', prepared in response to a Senate report accompanying the FY2004 NDAA. DSS monitored 11,000-plus contractor facilities; GAO issued seven recommendations. Facilities under an approved carve-out sit outside the population DSS inspected and therefore outside GAO's audit universe.

timeline.label: GAO audits contractor security and is steered around special access programs
timeline.text: GAO-04-332 finds that DoD 'cannot provide adequate assurances that its oversight ensures the protection of classified information' at more than 11,000 cleared contractor facilities. Footnote 2 records that, by agreement with committee staff, the review 'did not include DSS's oversight of special access programs at contractor facilities.'

timeline.label: NASA publishes the finding that Biefeld-Brown devices are ion wind
timeline.text: NASA/TM-2004-213082, prepared for a NASA/DoD-cosponsored conference in Seattle, 24 to 26 June 2004. Section 3.2.7: 'To date, all rigorous experimental tests indicate that the observed thrust is attributable to ion wind... These "Biefeld-Brown," "Lifter" and "Asymmetrical Capacitor Thrusters" are not viable candidates for breakthrough physics propulsion.' Section 3.3.1 records that 'metric engineering' had emerged at aerospace conferences and that 'The origin of this term is unknown'.
timeline.source: NASA/TM-2004-213082, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040070788/downloads/20040070788.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Final surface remediation completed; 5,562 cubic yards of contaminated soil removed
timeline.text: Thirty-seven years after the detonation the federal government was still hauling contaminated soil off ground twelve miles from Dulce. A permanent monument, a brass plaque in a concrete base, marks the site.
timeline.source: US Department of Energy Office of Legacy Management, 'Gasbuggy, New Mexico, Site' fact sheet, https://www.energy.gov/sites/default/files/2021-08/GasbuggyFactSheet.pdf

timeline.label: NASA contractor report models asymmetrical capacitor thrust as ion drift
timeline.text: NASA/CR-2004-213312. 'In spite of decades of speculation about possible new physical principles being responsible for the thrust produced by ACTs and lifters, we find no evidence to support such a conclusion. On the contrary, we find that their operation is fully explained by a very simple theory that uses only electrostatic forces and the transfer of momentum by multiple collisions.' Its reference list cites both Brown patents and GB 300,311 by number.
timeline.source: NASA/CR-2004-213312, Conclusions, https://ntrs.nasa.gov/api/citations/20040171929/downloads/20040171929.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Princeton tracks descents from 80,000 ft
timeline.text: USS Princeton's upgraded SPY-1B tracks objects descending from above 80,000 feet to 20,000 feet over roughly two weeks before the intercept.

timeline.label: Nimitz Tic Tac intercept
timeline.text: VFA-41 CO David Fravor and Lt. Cmdr. Alex Dietrich intercept a white 46-foot object with no control surfaces about 30 miles off Baja California; a follow-on aircraft records the ATFLIR footage later released as FLIR1.

timeline.label: The Nimitz intercept
timeline.text: Princeton vectors two VFA-41 F/A-18Fs to a contact it has held on Aegis for two weeks. Fravor, Dietrich and their WSOs watch a 46-foot white object for about five minutes; it departs and reappears at the CAP point 60 miles away in under a minute. A follow-on sortie records FLIR1.

timeline.label: Princeton data collection alleged
timeline.text: Princeton crewmen Kevin Day and Gary Voorhis say unidentified personnel came aboard and removed or wiped recording media. No visit log, message or chain-of-custody document has been located.

timeline.label: Reporting terminates at Third Fleet
timeline.text: The Navy range fouler report on the incident records: 'Pilots reported the incident through Intelligence Personnel. Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.'

timeline.label: The Princeton data goes missing
timeline.text: Three Princeton crewmen in different divisions - Day, Voorhis and Turner - describe unidentified personnel coming aboard within roughly 48 hours and removing or ordering wiped the recording media. No FOIA release, visit log or message traffic has ever identified them.

timeline.label: Military Intelligence Program created
timeline.text: The Joint Military Intelligence Program and Tactical Intelligence and Related Activities aggregations are consolidated into the Military Intelligence Program under the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence, formalising the split between DNI-controlled and SECDEF-controlled intelligence money and creating the oversight seam between the intelligence and armed services committees.

timeline.label: Majic Eyes Only
timeline.text: Ryan S. Wood publishes the retrieval literature's first indexed catalogue, with dates, locations, source trails and credibility weightings.

timeline.label: 'Hunt for the Skinwalker' published
timeline.text: Kelleher and Knapp publish the account of the NIDS ranch work; James Lacatski of DIA reads it.

timeline.label: Greg Bishop publishes Project Beta, the principal documented account
timeline.text: Paraview Pocket Books, ISBN 9780743470926, 288 pages, LCCN 2005297375, OCLC 57678877. A participant account at one remove: a writer relying on it states that Bishop had an undisclosed friendship with Bill Moore, one of the two men the book is about.
timeline.source: Open Library bibliographic record, https://openlibrary.org/books/OL7950835M/Project_Beta

timeline.label: NASA's satellite statement
timeline.text: Before the fortieth anniversary NASA states that experts examined metallic fragments from Kecksburg and determined they came from a Soviet satellite, but that the records of those findings were lost in the 1980s. NASA's own later position is that Cosmos 96 could not have been responsible.

timeline.label: FAS wins FOIA suit against the NRO
timeline.text: Aftergood, for FAS, secures release of unclassified National Reconnaissance Office budget records - the only occasion on which any component-level intelligence budget material has been prised loose by litigation.

timeline.label: Northrop-led consortium takes over the Nevada complex
timeline.text: National Security Technologies LLC succeeds Bechtel Nevada as Nevada Test Site management and operating contractor, inheriting the classified support infrastructure adjacent to Groom Lake.

timeline.label: Condign released under FOI
timeline.text: The Ministry of Defence releases the Condign report following a September 2005 Freedom of Information Act request by David Clarke and Gary Anthony. The publication scheme entry names the Directorate of Air Staff as author organisation.

timeline.label: $22M directed into the black budget
timeline.text: Reid, Inouye and Stevens direct roughly $22 million into the classified defense appropriation for DIA aerospace threat work, bypassing the authorizing committees.

timeline.label: FLIR1 leaks without authorization
timeline.text: DoD's 2020 release statement acknowledges the videos circulated publicly following unauthorized disclosures in 2007 and 2017.

timeline.label: Reid initiates AATIP
timeline.text: Senator Harry Reid, prompted by Robert Bigelow, sets in motion the program that becomes AATIP. Funding of roughly $22 million flows from late 2008 through 2011, most of it to Bigelow Aerospace.

timeline.label: DIA contacts Bigelow about Skinwalker
timeline.text: A senior Defense Intelligence Agency official writes to Bigelow about the ranch; Bigelow connects him to Senator Harry Reid. The AAWSAP contract follows in 2008 - the private capability is re-federalised without a new office being created.

timeline.label: Court finds NASA's searches inadequate
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan holds that NASA 'has not yet met its burden of demonstrating that the search for documents was adequate', denies summary judgment in part, and orders the parties to propose search and documentation procedures creating a proper record. NASA had already admitted its first two searches were inadequate.

timeline.label: Lacatski writes to Bigelow
timeline.text: Per 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon', Lacatski writes to Robert Bigelow on DIA letterhead, the act that originates the contract. DIA later reports no records of the letter.

timeline.label: CPSC: United Nuclear, the company, fined $7,500 after pleading guilty to three counts
timeline.text: CORRECTS THE STANDARD FRAMING. It is widely repeated that 'in 2006, Lazar pleaded guilty' to a Federal Hazardous Substances Act violation. The CPSC's own release of 20 July 2007 says the COMPANY pled guilty, to three criminal counts, before U.S. Chief Magistrate Lorenzo F. Garcia: 'United Nuclear Scientific Supplies LLC, of Edgewood, N.M., founded and operated by Robert Lazar, was fined $7,500 and received three years probation.' Robert Lazar and accountant Joy White appear in the separate civil consent decree.
timeline.source: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission, Release 07-249, https://www.cpsc.gov/Newsroom/News-Releases/2007/New-Mexico-Company-Fined-Ordered-To-Stop-Selling-Illegal-Fireworks-Components

timeline.label: Section 601 compels annual NIP disclosure
timeline.text: Section 601 of the Implementing Recommendations of the 9/11 Commission Act, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3306, requires the DNI to disclose the aggregate NIP appropriation within 30 days of each fiscal year's end, subject to a presidential waiver. The FY2007 figure is $43.5 billion. This remains, with the later request-side requirement, the entire statutory transparency regime for the intelligence budget.

timeline.label: Stipulated settlement in part
timeline.text: Judge Sullivan signs the Stipulation of Settlement in Part and orders joint status reports every sixty days. NASA searches under court supervision for the next twenty-two months.

timeline.label: 'Probable ET Generated' proposal to Puthoff
timeline.text: A proposal to analyse 'Probable ET Generated Specific Near-field Electromagnetic Emissions' is addressed to Puthoff and Hathaway - quoted verbatim in the preface of Kit Green's later DIRD, nine months before the AAWSAP contract.

timeline.label: DIA money flows to a private contractor
timeline.text: Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies wins the DIA AAWSAP contract on a special appropriation obtained through Sen. Harry Reid. Government-funded UAP research moves onto private premises.

timeline.label: A public AFIT thesis defines 'fastwalker'
timeline.text: AFIT/GA/ENY/08-M06, distribution unlimited, defines the term in its own words as 'any orbital object seen passing through the field of view of an Earth observing sensor which is suspected of being in orbit'. The words UFO and unidentified appear nowhere in its 112 pages. It names a fastwalker observation database with data from as far back as 1972, and a 1989 predecessor thesis by R. Osedacz.

timeline.label: The National Archives UFO release programme begins
timeline.text: The first of ten tranches of MoD UFO files is published at nationalarchives.gov.uk/ufos with a highlights guide by David Clarke. The programme runs to June 2013 and covers DEFE 24 and DEFE 31.

timeline.label: FY2008 Defense Supplemental Appropriation Act carries Reid/Inouye $10M add directing DIA to assess far-term foreign advanced aerospace threats out to 40 years
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237626/

timeline.label: DIA/Virginia Contracting Activity posts solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211, 'Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program', Total Small Business set-aside, NAICS 541330
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237630/

timeline.label: DIA posts solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211
timeline.text: The DIA Virginia Contracting Activity publicly solicits advanced aerospace weapon system studies across eleven areas out to 2050, naming Dr. James T. Lacatski as Government Project Leader.

timeline.label: DIA buys the physics
timeline.text: The Defense Intelligence Agency issues solicitation HHM402-08-R-0211 for the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program. The resulting contract produces thirty-eight Defense Intelligence Reference Documents on metric engineering, wormholes, antigravity and field effects on human tissue - the tier-1 evidence that a US agency paid to study the physics a recovered craft would require.

timeline.label: AAWSAP awarded
timeline.text: The DIA awards the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications contract to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies; Colm Kelleher serves as deputy administrator.

timeline.label: Solicitation response deadline; DIA receives only one bid, from BAASS
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237615/

timeline.label: Contract HHM402-08-C-0072 signed with Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies LLC
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237615/

timeline.label: AAWSAP awarded to BAASS
timeline.text: DIA awards firm-fixed-price contract HHM402-08-C-0072 to Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies LLC, $10,000,000 base with four option years.

timeline.label: DIA Director meets Senator Reid on the program
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237615/

timeline.label: BAASS submits 12 technical-area program management plans; DIA rates them 'very good to excellent'
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237615/

timeline.label: DIA 'Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Contract Status' briefing
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237613/

timeline.label: First DIA contract status briefing
timeline.text: DIA prepares its first Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications contract status briefing three months after award.

timeline.label: Defense Security Service conducts facility clearance site inspection at BAASS
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237615/

timeline.label: BAASS funds MUFON's Star Team Impact Project
timeline.text: A DIA-contracted firm funds rapid-response investigation by the largest civilian UFO network in the United States, routing case data back to BAASS. The arrangement collapses in 2010.

timeline.label: Stratton reopens the Nimitz case
timeline.text: Fravor testifies that Jay Stratton contacted him in 2009 to investigate the 2004 sighting as part of a DoD program - five years after the Navy declined to investigate it.

timeline.label: The alleged Lockheed material negotiation
timeline.text: Per George Knapp's later sworn testimony, Robert Bigelow and an AAWSAP colleague negotiate with senior Lockheed Martin executives for a quantity of material held at a California facility. AARO separately records an allegation that an organisation possessed off-world material in 2009 and 2010.

timeline.label: DIRD series produced
timeline.text: The FY2009 Defense Intelligence Reference Documents are produced under the DIA Defense Warning Office with James T. Lacatski as programme manager - propulsion physics, exotic materials and human injury pathology commissioned as one set.

timeline.label: DIA talking paper for Reid visit
timeline.text: DIA prepares a talking paper for a Senator Reid visit on AAWSAP contract status — the first of three surviving Reid briefing papers from 2009.

timeline.label: DIA status briefing: 'On Track, On Schedule, and Within Cost'; SCI clearance processing completed for all key BAASS personnel
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237616/

timeline.label: May 2009 Reid briefing
timeline.text: DIA briefs Reid on contract status; the meeting generates the request that produces the October deliverables quality review.

timeline.label: Sen. Reid writes DEPSECDEF Lynn requesting restricted Special Access Protection for the AAITP
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237659/

timeline.label: Reid requests a Restricted SAP
timeline.text: Reid asks Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III for a Restricted Special Access Program with a bigoted access list over methodologies for engineering advanced technologies and contractor involvement.

timeline.label: BAASS delivers 26 detailed research reports — twice the contracted minimum
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237642/

timeline.label: BAASS delivers the 494-page Ten Month Report
timeline.text: The contractor delivers a report integrating exotic physics research with field investigation, a case database, ranch operations and human physiological effects. DIA has never released it.

timeline.label: Reid seeks SAP status
timeline.text: Reid writes to Deputy Secretary of Defense William Lynn III requesting Special Access Program status for AATIP. The request is denied. Elizondo's and Puthoff's names in the memo are originally redacted.

timeline.label: Kean v. NASA dismissed
timeline.text: On the parties' joint motion and NASA's representation that it had met its settlement obligations, the case is dismissed. The only federal finding of an inadequate UFO-related records search stands undisturbed.

timeline.label: Brazil declassifies the 1986 report
timeline.text: The Air Defence Command report of 2 June 1986 is released to the Arquivo Nacional. The Brazilian Air Force begins transferring its whole UAP holding to the National Archives; by 2022 it is the second most consulted collection there, behind only the records of the military dictatorship.

timeline.label: DIA Info Memo U-429-09 reviews deliverables; all reviews positive; five reviews by outside reviewers incl. three Sandia National Laboratories staff
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237617/

timeline.label: DIA finds the deliverables excellent
timeline.text: DIA's Defense Warning Office records that of thirteen reviews of the 26 FY09 reports, including three by Sandia National Laboratories staff, 'all of the reviews were positive, some exceptionally so'.

timeline.label: The conversion is considered
timeline.text: An Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence information memorandum records review of a special access programme request relating to AATIP. This is the documented moment at which a FOIA-visible programme was considered for conversion into an invisible one.

timeline.label: DIA Info Memo U-09-2660: 'DIA cannot find adequate justification to establish a restricted SAP'
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237611/

timeline.label: DIA: insufficient grounds to classify
timeline.text: DIA finds the program cannot be classified — the material is basic scientific research not owned or controlled by the government and no report is sufficiently sensitive to require extra protection.

timeline.label: Clapper recommends against a SAP
timeline.text: USD(I) James R. Clapper Jr. recommends against establishing a Special Access Program in the packet presented to Deputy Secretary Lynn. Nine months later he becomes Director of National Intelligence.

timeline.label: USD(I) recommends against SAP status
timeline.text: James Clapper's recommendation closes out Senator Reid's June 2009 request for restricted special access program status for the DIA advanced aerospace effort. The one documented SAP decision in the modern record goes against concealment.

timeline.label: DEPSECDEF Lynn and DIA meet Sen. Reid at Senate Visitor Center SVC-217, 1645; DIA position is that deliverables do not meet DoD 5200.1-R criteria for a SAP
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237628/

timeline.label: Lynn refuses Reid in person
timeline.text: At 4:45pm in Senate Visitor Center room SVC-217, the Deputy Secretary of Defense tells the Majority Leader the AAWSAP deliverables do not meet DoD 5200.1-R criteria for SAP protection.

timeline.label: The MoD closes the UFO desk
timeline.text: Britain terminates its public UAP reporting channel with effect from December 2009, in the same period in which it was handling the largest volume of sighting reports in thirty years. The National Archives records that the closure 'sparked' a disclosure campaign.

timeline.label: First DIRD publication in the released set: DIA-08-0911-016, 'Aerospace Applications of Programmable Matter'
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237656/

timeline.label: E.O. 13526 fixes who may create a SAP and caps ISOO's access
timeline.text: Sec. 4.3(a) limits SAP creation to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy and Homeland Security, the Attorney General and the DNI, or the principal deputy of each. Sec. 4.3(b)(3) permits an agency head to limit access to a SAP to the Director of ISOO 'and no more than one other employee' or, 'for special access programs that are extraordinarily sensitive and vulnerable, to the Director only.' Sec. 4.3(c): 'Nothing in this order shall supersede any requirement made by or under 10 U.S.C. 119.'

timeline.label: Executive Order 13526 fixes the six officials who may create a SAP
timeline.text: Section 4.3 limits SAP creation to the Secretaries of State, Defense, Energy and Homeland Security, the Attorney General and the DNI, or their principal deputies, requires the number to be kept at an absolute minimum, and affords the ISOO Director access 'consistent with the policies and procedures directed by the President'.

timeline.label: Reid SAP request (2009, denied by DIA) and later KONA BLUE PSAP to DHS (post-2012, rejected by DHS leadership) — two formal attempts to move the effort into special-access channels
timeline.source: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/AARO_Historical_Record_Report_Vol_1_2024.pdf

timeline.label: MIP topline published for the first time
timeline.text: Military Intelligence Program figures are disclosed alongside the NIP for FY2010: $27.0 billion MIP against $53.1 billion NIP, a combined $80.1 billion. No breakdown of either accompanies the figures, then or since.

timeline.label: Brazilian Army inquiry on Varginha
timeline.text: The inquiry concludes the 1996 witnesses encountered Luiz Antonio de Paula, a mentally disabled man, and that the observed military vehicle movements were routine maintenance and Escola de Sargentos das Armas transport. The underlying unit movement logs are not published.

timeline.label: Elizondo assumes AATIP role
timeline.text: On TTSA's account Elizondo takes over AATIP as Director in 2010, running it from OUSD(I). Neill Tipton, his superior in this period, later states he brought no AATIP responsibilities with him.

timeline.label: The transfer is blocked
timeline.text: The divestment never occurs. Elizondo testifies that a memorandum from the Secretary of the Air Force required to complete it never issued; the reported cause is a CIA veto, which AARO records as a former senior CIA official quashing the proposal to remove the material from the corporation.

timeline.label: DIA's own antigravity survey is issued, and it does not mention Thomas Townsend Brown
timeline.text: DIA-08-1003-018, 'Antigravity for Aerospace Applications', ICOD 1 December 2009, 'Acquisition Threat Support', 45 pages as released, attributed on the DIA list of 9 January 2018 to Dr Eric Davis. Word counts over the released PDF: Biefeld 0, electrogravitics 0, ion wind 0, Podkletnov 0, and Brown absent except as three other authors' surnames in the reference list. THIS IS EVIDENCE ABOUT WHAT THE DOCUMENT CONTAINS AND IS NOT A FINDING THAT DIA CONSIDERED AND REJECTED BROWN.
timeline.source: DIA-08-1003-018, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_19-DIRD_Antigravity_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Hathaway's DIRD on maverick inventors is issued, naming Hutchison zero times
timeline.text: DIA-08-1003-017, 'Maverick Inventor Versus Corporate Inventor: Where Will the Next Major Innovations Arise?', ICOD 1 December 2009, 20 pages as released, attributed on the DIA list to Dr George Hathaway of Hathaway Consulting, who is the author of the book 'Mindbending: The Hutchison Files'. Word counts: Hutchison 0, Pharos 0, levitation 0.
timeline.source: DIA-08-1003-017, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_17-DIRD_Maverick_Inventor_Versus_Corporate_Inventor-Where_Will_the_Next_major_Innovations_Arise.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: DIA's warp DIRD is issued, tabulating the requirement at -10^42 J for light speed
timeline.text: DIA-08-1004-001, 'Warp Drive, Dark Energy, and the Manipulation of Extra Dimensions', ICOD 1 December 2009, 34 pages as released. Its Table 3, after the reduction it argues for, gives -1.00 x 10^42 J at light speed and -4.00 x 10^42 J at twice light speed; its Table 2 gives -3.03 x 10^50 J at light speed. Its reference 1 is Alcubierre 1994.
timeline.source: DIA-08-1004-001, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_13-DIRD_Warp_Drive_Dark_energy_and_the_Manipulation_of_Extra_Dimensions.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: DIA-08-1004-004 issued
timeline.text: 'Traversable Wormholes, Stargates, and Negative Energy' is issued with Eric W. Davis of EarthTech International, 11855 Research Blvd, Austin TX, named as author.

timeline.label: DoDD 5205.07 puts acknowledged / unacknowledged / waived into DoD policy
timeline.text: The directive cancels DoDD 5205.07 of 5 January 2006, establishes the SAPOC and DoD SAPCO, defines the three-state taxonomy and the carve-out, restricts waived-SAP access to committee chairs, ranking minority members and staff directors, and provides at para 4.h that 'All waived SAP material submitted to Congress, to include annual reports and other products, shall remain in DoD custody.' Change 2 issued 4 February 2020.

sources.name: DoDD 5205.07 (1 Jul 2010, Chg 2 4 Feb 2020) — Internet Archive capture

timeline.label: DoD Directive 5205.07 defines acknowledged, unacknowledged and waived
timeline.text: The directive establishes the SAPOC and DoD SAPCO and puts the three-state taxonomy into DoD policy in terms, together with the rule that committee members get access to DoD SAPs 'except for waived programs' and that waived material submitted to Congress 'shall remain in DoD custody'.

timeline.label: Contract modification P00001 to HHM402-08-C-0072 (FY10 option, $12M add in FY2010 Defense Appropriations Act)
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237652/

timeline.label: Seven USAF veterans speak at the National Press Club
timeline.text: Robert Hastings convened Dwynne Arneson, Bruce Fenstermacher, Charles Halt, Robert Jamison, Patrick McDonough, Jerry Nelson and Robert Salas at the National Press Club. Six are named on his own page as having executed affidavits. For five of the seven this is their first appearance in the public record. Walter Figel declined to sign an affidavit and did not appear.
timeline.source: Robert Hastings, 'The UFOs-Nukes Connection Press Conference', https://ufohastings.com/articles/the-ufos-nukes-connection-press-conference

timeline.label: UFO-Nukes Connection press conference
timeline.text: Robert Hastings convenes seven named USAF veterans at the National Press Club. CNN streams it live. Signed affidavits from Salas, Halt, McDonough, Jamison, Arneson, Fenstermacher and Nelson are on file and published in facsimile. Anonymous testimony becomes on-the-record testimony.

timeline.label: DIA's MHD DIRD is issued, and it is about hypersonic aerodynamics
timeline.text: DIA-08-1011-006, 'MHD Air Breathing Propulsion and Power for Aerospace Applications', ICOD 20 July 2010, 'Defense Futures', 33 pages as released, attributed on the DIA list to Dr S Macheret of Lockheed Martin. Its Summary reports 'significant difficulties... weight, complexity, higher power' and that the Ajax energy bypass concept 'has been shown to be meaningless below at least Mach 12'. Word counts: UFO 0, antigravity 0, scalar 0, zero point 0.
timeline.source: DIA-08-1011-006, https://documents2.theblackvault.com/documents/dia/AAWSAP-DIRDs/DIRD_33-DIRD_MHD_Air_Breathing_Propulsion_and_Power_for_Aerospace_Applications.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: DIA proposes moving AATIP out
timeline.text: A DIA info memo to USD(AT&L) says the reports were of limited value to DIA but could merit other organisations, and that the project could be transitioned to a better-suited component.

timeline.label: DIA withholds the BAASS contract
timeline.text: DIA withholds the AAWSAP contract in full in response to a FOIA request; it will not release it for another eleven years.

timeline.label: KONA BLUE proposed at DHS
timeline.text: A successor special access program to house UAP recovery and reverse-engineering work is proposed to the Department of Homeland Security and subsequently rejected by DHS leadership.

timeline.label: Alleged 2011 restriction on historical briefings
timeline.text: UAP Gerb alleges a legacy program briefing restriction initiated in 2011 to cease historical briefings on program incumbents - i.e. a policy act specifically designed to prevent newly cleared personnel from learning the programme's own history. If real, it is documentable as a memorandum or classification guide change.

timeline.label: KONA BLUE proposed to DHS
timeline.text: AAWSAP's advocates propose a prospective special access program at DHS to restart the work and reverse-engineer any recovered craft they hoped to acquire. DHS rejects it. AARO notes it was never reported to Congress because it never met the SAP threshold.

timeline.label: DHS Under Secretary for S&T establishes KONA BLUE as a prospective SAP
timeline.text: On the government's own account, a DHS component head creates a prospective special access program that supporters intended to use to reverse-engineer recovered craft and exploit non-human biologics. Senators Lieberman and Reid ask that it be established.

timeline.label: Last DIRD publication in the released set: DIA-08-1102-007, 'Quantum Tomography of Negative Energy States in the Vacuum'
timeline.source: https://www.dia.mil/FOIA/FOIA-Electronic-Reading-Room/FileId/237632/

timeline.label: First publication of the NIP budget request
timeline.text: Under section 364 of the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2010, the aggregate NIP budget request is published for the first time, in February 2011. Two numbers a year is now the settled floor and ceiling of public knowledge.

timeline.label: DHS Deputy Secretary terminates KONA BLUE
timeline.text: Approximately six months after it is established, the Deputy Secretary disapproves the prospective program. Neither the establishing nor the terminating official is named in the released paper.

timeline.label: The most-reproduced black triangle photograph is confessed as a hoax on Belgian television
timeline.text: Robert Sheaffer records that on 26 July 2011 the Belgian broadcaster RTL carried the photographer's confession about the Petit-Rechain image of the 1989-90 Belgian wave: 'The UFO of Petit-Rechain is not a spaceship from a distant galaxy but a panel of painted styrofoam with three spots affixed', and, from the maker, 'One has managed to fool the whole world with a silly model made of styrofoam.' Fouche's 1998 presentation had attached his craft to 'the country of Belgium' at slide 6. This does not touch the eyewitness reports and it decides nothing about Fouche; it records that the visual corpus the claim borrows plausibility from has a confessed hoax at its centre.
timeline.source: Robert Sheaffer, 'Bad UFOs', https://badufos.blogspot.com/2011/07/classic-ufo-photo-from-belgian-wave.html

timeline.label: CAPCO Register v5.1 gives SAPs their own marking category
timeline.text: Volume 5 Edition 1 of the IC Authorized Classification and Control Markings Register moves the Special Access Required marking into a dedicated Special Access Program Markings category with the indicator 'SAR-'. Its title page records that certain markings were removed for classification and 'compiled in separate classified addenda'.

timeline.label: DIA ends AAWSAP; follow-on program KONA BLUE proposed to DHS and rejected
timeline.source: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/AARO_Historical_Record_Report_Vol_1_2024.pdf

timeline.label: AAWSAP/AATIP terminated
timeline.text: DoD's official history states the program was 'terminated in 2012 upon the completion of its deliverables due to DIA and DoD concerns about the project'. Daniel Inouye dies the same year.

timeline.label: AATIP funding ends
timeline.text: The Department's position is that AATIP terminated in 2012. Elizondo's position is that only government funding ceased and the effort continued to his 2017 departure.

timeline.label: Puthoff's negative result
timeline.text: A letter from Puthoff reports that testing of the Howe samples produced no proof of alien origin and no 'interesting/anomalous outcome', with one test outstanding for want of equipment.

timeline.label: Betty J. Sapp is sworn in as Director of the National Reconnaissance Office
timeline.text: The Congressional Research Service's intelligence-community leadership roster records 'Director of the National Reconnaissance Office (D/NRO) Betty J. Sapp (sworn in July 6, 2012)', with the appointment authority at 50 U.S.C. 3041(b)(2)(B) and 50 U.S.C. 3602(a)(2), and gives Christopher Scolese as nominated on 7 February 2019 in the same row. This is the NRO's first named officer on this board.
timeline.source: CRS, U.S. Intelligence Community (IC): Appointment Dates and Appointment Legal Provisions for Selected IC Leadership, IF10538 version 6, 19 March 2019, Table 1, https://www.congress.gov/crs_external_products/IF/PDF/IF10538/IF10538.6.pdf

timeline.label: DoDI 5205.11 issued — SAP management, administration and oversight
timeline.text: The instruction reissued on 12 September 2024 records that it 'Reissues and cancels DoD Instruction 5205.11, February 6, 2013, as amended', and also 'incorporates and cancels' the Deputy Secretary of Defense Memorandum, 'Integrated Joint Special Technical Operations (IJSTO) Policy', 5 April 2021.

timeline.label: DoDI 5205.11 publishes the carve-out request procedure and a worked example
timeline.text: The instruction sets the prospective SAP timeline ending 'NLT P+210 - End of 30-day period without Congressional decision', requires a carve-out justification in the approval package, and reproduces a sample action memo to the Deputy Secretary recommending that a fictional unacknowledged SAP be approved and that 'The Defense Security Service will be carved out from its normal industrial security oversight responsibilities.'

timeline.label: US release date given by IMDb for the Zero Point documentary
timeline.text: IMDb tt6111304 gives a US release date of 2 June 2013 for 'Zero Point: The Story of Mark McCandlish and the Flux Liner', a 1h 32m documentary with James Allen credited as director and writer. IMDb is user-maintained and the film itself was not opened. The UAP Gerb episode description calls it the '2014 Zero Point Documentary'.
timeline.source: IMDb tt6111304, https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6111304/, opened 18 September 2026

timeline.label: Mirage Men premieres at Sheffield Doc/Fest, built on the Doty admission
timeline.text: Directed by John Lundberg with Roland Denning and Kypros Kyprianou, based on Mark Pilkington's 2010 book, produced by a company named Perception Management Productions. The film centres on Doty's dealings with Bennewitz and Linda Moulton Howe. THE FILM WAS NOT WATCHED by this session and nothing he says in it is quoted.
timeline.source: archive.org item for Mirage Men (2013), https://archive.org/details/mirage-men-2013

timeline.label: The CIA names Area 51
timeline.text: Answering a 2005 FOIA request by Jeffrey Richelson of the National Security Archive, the CIA releases the U-2 and OXCART history and acknowledges specific activity at the site - fifty-eight years after establishment.

timeline.label: The only public view inside the black budget
timeline.text: The Washington Post publishes excerpts from the 'National Intelligence Program Summary for FY2013', classified TS/SI/TK/NOFORN, from the Snowden material. For the same year the officially disclosed figure was a single aggregate: $52.7 billion requested, $49.0 billion after sequestration. Thirteen years later this remains the only occasion on which the interior of the intelligence budget has been seen outside the cleared community.

timeline.label: The CIA's U-2 and OXCART history, declassified, acknowledges Groom Lake
timeline.text: The National Security Archive posts Electronic Briefing Book 443, edited by Jeffrey T. Richelson, on the CIA history 'The Central Intelligence Agency and Overhead Reconnaissance: The U-2 and OXCART Programs, 1954-1974' by Gregory Pedlow and Donald E. Welzenbach, declassified that summer. This is the documented half of the hub's geography and it is a statement about Groom Lake, NOT about Papoose Lake.
timeline.source: National Security Archive EBB 443, https://nsarchive.gwu.edu/node/3324

timeline.label: Skeptoid 391: 'there's nothing there at all'
timeline.text: Brian Dunning: 'It's trivial to study Google Earth images of Archuleta Mesa and see that there's nothing there at all, certainly nothing like Schneider's elaborate descriptions.' Classified fictional. The episode's own reference list for Dulce is a single blog post, which bounds how much weight it can carry.
timeline.source: Brian Dunning, Skeptoid 391, 3 December 2013, https://skeptoid.com/episodes/4391

timeline.label: VFA-11 encounters begin
timeline.text: After the fleet's APG-79 AESA radar upgrade, Ryan Graves's squadron begins witnessing UAP 'on a regular basis' off Virginia Beach during USS Theodore Roosevelt workups.

timeline.label: A dated report of the Doty admission, which quotes him nowhere
timeline.text: Alejandro Rojas reports that Doty says he was tasked with hoaxing documents and feeding false information while an AFOSI special agent at Kirtland, that he was ordered to make Bennewitz believe in an impending alien invasion, and that he entered Bennewitz's house and office under orders. The piece paraphrases throughout and contains no direct quotation from him; the Air Force 'refuses to comment'.
timeline.source: Alejandro Rojas, HuffPost Weird News, 13 May 2014, https://www.huffpost.com/entry/exair-force-law-enforceme_b_5312650

timeline.label: The fifteen page military documents compilation is printed to PDF
timeline.text: The PDF opened carries producer 'PDF-XChange 4.0.195.0' and creation date D:20140615084520+01'00'. It is a print of an HTML page on checktheevidence.co.uk, 15 pages with 23 embedded images and a caption text layer in mixed voice. It contains no discharge certificate, no DD Form 214, no clearance record, no contract and no programme document.
timeline.source: PDF metadata and contents read from https://www.checktheevidence.com/pdf/Edgar%20Fouches%20Military%20Documents.pdf

timeline.label: David Hilton alleges Fouche faked one or more of his own military documents
timeline.text: Andrew Johnson records that Hilton made the allegation in a video dated 26 June 2014 and concluded that Fouche could not be trusted. The video itself was not opened; the allegation reaches this record only through Johnson's description of it.
timeline.source: Andrew Johnson, checktheevidence.com, https://www.checktheevidence.com/wordpress/2015/01/13/edgar-fouche-documents-released-in-foia-show-the-same-type-of-record-as-he-provided-himself/

timeline.label: Hilton posts the FOIA return on Fouche's military records
timeline.text: Andrew Johnson records that Hilton filed a Freedom of Information Act request for Fouche's military records and posted the return on 25 September 2014, and reads it as corroborating what Fouche had already said: Lackland AFB 1967, Keesler and Cannon 1968, Nellis June 1976 to 16 July 1979, Kadena 5 September 1979 to 4 March 1982, and decorations including the Vietnam Service Medal and three Meritorious Service Medals. THE FOIA RETURN ITSELF WAS NOT OPENED by this research.
timeline.source: Andrew Johnson, http://www.checktheevidence.co.uk/articles/David%20Hilton%20FOIA%20on%20ed%20Fouche.htm

timeline.label: Chilean Navy helicopter FLIR case
timeline.text: A Chilean Navy helicopter films an object in daylight on infrared during a coastal patrol. Two radar stations cannot see it although they can see the helicopters; air traffic control confirms no authorised aircraft in the area. CEFAA analyses the case for two years.

timeline.label: W-72 near-midair
timeline.text: Two F/A-18Fs 100 feet apart take evasive action around a dark gray cube inside a clear sphere holding station against the wind at the entry point of Warning Area W-72. The squadron files a safety report and receives no acknowledgement.

timeline.label: GIMBAL and GO FAST recorded
timeline.text: Two ATFLIR recordings are made in the Atlantic operating areas; both are formally released by DoD five years later as authentic and unidentified.

timeline.label: Fleet Forces safety message recalled
timeline.text: A US Fleet Forces Command 'URGENT SAFETY OF FLIGHT ISSUE' email carrying GO FAST and citing 'multiple near-midair collisions' is sent to all subordinate commanders and deleted from every recipient's account the next day.

timeline.label: Invention original date recorded for the Inertial Mass Reduction Device
timeline.text: The NAVAIR invention-disclosure briefing for Navy Case PAX 205 records the invention original date as 06/03/2015 and states that the concept is theoretical with no prototype in existence.

timeline.label: DoDM 5205.07 Volume 1 states exactly what a carve-out removes
timeline.text: Enclosure 2 para 2: unless a carve-out is approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary of Defense, DSS/DCSA performs SAP security inspections at cleared contractor locations, authorizes contractor SAP information systems, and coordinates CI threat and incident cross-sharing. A carve-out removes all three. Volume 1 also incorporates and cancels the DoD Overprint to the NISPOM Supplement, and confines fraud/waste/abuse reporting to SAP channels.

sources.name: DoDM 5205.07 Vol 1 (2015/2018) — Internet Archive capture

timeline.label: DoD SAP Security Manual Volume 1 issued
timeline.text: DoDM 5205.07-V1 states what a carve-out removes - contractor SAP security inspections, information system authorisation and counterintelligence cross-sharing - and defines carve-out in its glossary as a provision approved by the Secretary or Deputy Secretary that relieves DSS of its NISP obligation.

timeline.label: Application 14/807,943 filed for the Electromagnetic Field Generator
timeline.text: The first of the five Pais filings, assigned to the United States as represented by the Secretary of the Navy. It is the device NAWCAD would later test.
timeline.source: Google Patents record for US 10,135,366 B2, https://patents.google.com/patent/US10135366B2/en , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: DoD FMR Volume 3 Chapter 6 reissued
timeline.text: The Department's reprogramming regulation sets the four action types and the congressional approval thresholds - $10 million for military personnel, $15 million for operation and maintenance, $20 million or 20 percent for procurement, $10 million or 20 percent for RDT&E - and preserves Below-Threshold Reprogramming, which requires no approval and no notification at all.

timeline.label: A researcher publishes Callahan's self-supplied OMB Form 171
timeline.text: Paul Dean publishes an OMB Form 171 showing 'Division Mgr. Investigations/Evaluations', 'FAA ATS-1 Washington Headquarters', 'Oct. 1986 to present', stating that the originals were provided by Callahan himself in 2015. In part one of the same series Dean had reported his own negative finding: the public record showed a 'Quality Control Branch Manager' of the 'Quality Assurance Staff'.
timeline.source: Paul Dean, 'John Callahan & The JAL-1628 UFO Encounter; FAA Credentials Finally Confirmed, pt2', The UFO Chronicles, https://www.theufochronicles.com/2015/10/john-callahan-jal-1628-ufo-encounter_4.html

timeline.label: ICD 906 signed, governing IC Controlled Access Programs
timeline.text: The current ICD 906 states at B.2: 'This ICD supersedes ICD 906, Controlled Access Programs, signed 17 October 2015.' The 2015 text is preserved in an Internet Archive capture of dni.gov.

sources.name: ICD 906 (current) — Internet Archive capture of dni.gov

timeline.label: ICD 906 signed, governing Controlled Access Programs
timeline.text: The DNI's directive establishes the IC's counterpart to the DoD SAP regime, defines CAPs as control systems with compartments and sub-compartments, permits unacknowledged CAPs on DNI or PDDNI approval, and creates the CAP Oversight Committee and Senior Review Group. This version was later superseded by a reissue released in December 2024.

timeline.label: NRO declassifies almost the entire DORIAN collection
timeline.text: The NRO's Center for the Study of National Reconnaissance held a panel at the National Museum of the United States Air Force on the occasion of the NRO declassifying almost its entire collection of records on the Dorian program: over 850 documents with some 22,000 pages and 280 photographs. Line-by-line review had taken over a year, and the collection was posted on the NRO public web page the day after the panel.
timeline.source: Spies in Space: Reflections on National Reconnaissance and the Manned Orbiting Laboratory, NRO CSNR, May 2019, foreword, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/GOVPUB-D-PURL-gpo123652/pdf/GOVPUB-D-PURL-gpo123652.pdf

timeline.label: THE CONFESSION: 'TEC (Thomas Edwin Castello) is a creation. A MYTH'
timeline.text: Tal Levesque, who wrote as Jason Bishop III and authored the two original Dulce Base articles, told Adam Gorightly by email that Castello was his own invention, described composing the articles from an account by a woman he names as Ann West mixed with his own research, and described mailing a hundred large envelope packets of supporting material to authors and lecturers 'who then mixed it into their talks, articles and books'. The single most important dated item in this cluster, and the board's cleanest worked example of manufactured corroboration.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 2 April 2024, reproducing the November 2015 Levesque email as published in Adam Gorightly, 'Saucers, Spooks and Kooks', https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2024/04/02/startling-final-confession-made-in-2015-by-the-enigmatic-tal-levesque-originator-of-the-entire-dulce-base-myth/

timeline.label: IUPAC assigns discovery priority for element 115
timeline.text: Priority went to 'the Dubna-Livermore-Oak Ridge collaborations', on the basis of work 'starting in 2010, and subsequently confirmed in 2012 and 2013'. A precision point usually got wrong in both directions: the priority statement rests on the 2010 to 2013 work, not on the 2003 experiment. The Joint Working Party report is Karol, Barber, Sherrill, Vardaci and Yamazaki, Pure and Applied Chemistry 88 (2016) 155.
timeline.source: IUPAC, 30 December 2015, https://iupac.org/discovery-and-assignment-of-elements-with-atomic-numbers-113-115-117-and-118/

timeline.label: 'Exemplary' performance evaluation
timeline.text: Elizondo's annual evaluation rates him exemplary; his supervisor writes that it 'cannot be overstated the importance of Mr. Elizondo's portfolio to national security' and credits him with neutralising six insider threats.

timeline.label: DeLonge names Wright-Patterson and McCasland to Podesta in writing
timeline.text: Under the subject line 'General McCasland', Tom DeLonge writes to John Podesta: 'When Roswell crashed, they shipped it to the laboratory at Wright Patterson Air Force Base. General McCasland was in charge of that exact laboratory up to a couple years ago.' The same day's calendar thread for a DeLonge/Podesta meeting runs between Podesta and an address signing 'Neil McC', copied to DeLonge, a Clinton campaign address and Rob Weiss of Lockheed Martin. Neither Prometheus nor Linda Moulton Howe appears anywhere in the release.
timeline.source: WikiLeaks, The Podesta Emails, email id 3099, released 10 October 2016, https://wikileaks.org/podesta-emails/emailid/3099

timeline.label: Peter Merlin's four-part analysis of Fouche is published
timeline.text: Quoted verbatim between (QUOTE) and (UNQUOTE) markers on Norio Hayakawa's blog: that the SAC letter is unclassified and carries no classification markings, control number or copy-of count and that 'REPLY TO: DARPA' is probably a five-letter office code; that the photograph Fouche captioned 'Have Blue' is 'the first YF-117A SENIOR TREND prototype'; that 'No such person as Steve Stenson was ever commander of AFFTC'; and that the KGB passport and badges are fakes 'widely available at many Army-Navy surplus stores'.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 'Edgar Fouche's TR-3B is most likely a hoax', https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2016/03/19/edgar-fouches-tr-3b-is-most-likely-a-hoax/

timeline.label: Greenewald traces the Dulce photograph to the film The 6th Day
timeline.text: The photograph of bodies in a chamber, circulated for years as Castello's leaked proof, is a frame from the 2000 feature film: it 'is, in fact, a verifiable hoax', and 'You can see that the position of the bodies, inside the chamber, are a match.' In the same case file: 'There is no evidence that I have found, that shows that Thomas Costello even exists.'
timeline.source: The Black Vault case file, John Greenewald, 1 April 2016, https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/leaked-underground-dulce-base-alien-photo-thomas-costello/

timeline.label: Navy files the inertial mass reduction craft application
timeline.text: Application 15/141270, 'Craft using an inertial mass reduction device', filed with the United States as represented by the Secretary of the Navy as assignee.

timeline.label: Application 15/141,270 filed: 'Craft using an inertial mass reduction device'
timeline.text: Assignee on the granted patent: 'The United States of America as represented by the Secretary of the Navy, Washington, DC (US)'. Attorney of record: 'Mark O Glut; NAWCAD'. Prior publication US 2017/0313446 A1 of 2 November 2017.
timeline.source: US Patent 10,144,532 B2, printed front page, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/de/4c/43/62c585ccc936cc/US10144532.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Pais craft application referred for third-level security review
timeline.text: USPTO events record the inertial mass reduction craft application referred to Level 2 (LARS) and then by L&R for third-level security review, the screening that decides whether a filing receives a secrecy order. It cleared.

timeline.label: DODIG-2016-113: $6.5 trillion in unsupported year-end adjustments
timeline.text: The DoD Inspector General finds that the Army Comptroller's office and DFAS Indianapolis 'did not adequately support $2.8 trillion in third quarter journal voucher (JV) adjustments and $6.5 trillion in yearend JV adjustments made to AGF data during FY 2015 financial statement compilation'. Footnote 2 states the amounts are not cumulative. The report will become the load-bearing citation of the entire missing-money literature, usually misquoted.

timeline.label: DoD asks FASAB for a classified-reporting standard
timeline.text: Two months after the Army adjustments report, the Department of Defense identifies to the Federal Accounting Standards Advisory Board the need for a standard reconciling generally accepted accounting principles with classification obligations under Executive Order 13526. That request becomes SFFAS 56.

timeline.label: Hayakawa, working the question since 1988: 'it does not seem to exist'
timeline.text: The same post supplies the dated chronology of the cluster's originators used throughout this file: Bennewitz from about 1979, Myrna Hansen in 1980, Tom Adams in the early 1980s, John Lear in 1988 from 'Ann West', and Phil Schneider only in 1995.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 29 August 2016, https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2016/08/29/enigmatic-personalities-behind-the-initial-dulce-underground-base-rumors/comment-page-1/

timeline.label: NAWCAD begins testing the High Energy Electromagnetic Field Generator
timeline.text: Timothy Boulay, Communications Director at NAWCAD, on the record: 'The High Energy Electromagnetic Field Generator testing occurred from October 2016 through September 2019.' The $508,000 spent corresponds closely to the two $250,000 lines the PAX 205 invention-disclosure briefing proposed.
timeline.source: Brett Tingley, The War Zone, quoting Timothy Boulay of NAWCAD, https://www.twz.com/39012/the-navy-finally-speaks-up-about-its-bizarre-ufo-patent-experiments , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Element 115 formally named moscovium
timeline.text: The name moscovium, symbol Mc, was formally approved on 28 November 2016 and announced on 30 November 2016, proposed by the discoverers at Dubna, Oak Ridge, Vanderbilt and Lawrence Livermore, in recognition of the Moscow region. This event is regularly presented as vindicating the Lazar claim. It does not: his claim requires a STABLE isotope that can be machined and stored, and no such isotope exists.
timeline.source: IUPAC, 30 November 2016, https://iupac.org/iupac-announces-the-names-of-the-elements-113-115-117-and-118/

timeline.label: Chile releases the Navy footage
timeline.text: CEFAA publishes the Chilean Navy infrared video without an explanation - the first release of state military sensor footage of an unresolved object by a Latin American government, three years before the US Department of Defense authorised release of the three Navy videos.

timeline.label: Edgar Albert Fouche dies, aged 69; buried Coffey Cemetery, Mason County, Texas
timeline.text: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, created 18 June 2017 and citing an obituary from Mason Funeral Home, gives the death date and age and the burial at Coffey Cemetery, Streeter, Mason County, Texas, with the inscription 'Saved by the blood of Jesus Christ'. A death date of 6 May 2018 at age 82 also circulates and is wrong on both counts; no opened record supports it.
timeline.source: Find a Grave memorial 180498305, https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/180498305/edgar-albert-fouch%C3%A9

timeline.label: Bigelow on 60 Minutes
timeline.text: Robert Bigelow tells CBS he is 'absolutely convinced' of an extraterrestrial presence on Earth, seven months before the program he was paid to run becomes public.

timeline.label: Peter Robbins repudiates his co-author after twenty-nine years
timeline.text: Robbins publishes a statement alleging that Larry Warren fabricated a photograph with John Lennon, altered a USAF Form 490 whose ophthalmic notation is attributed to a physician Robbins found to be an orthopaedic surgeon, produced an in-processing sheet with mismatched signatures, and attributed testimonial letters to two named airmen that were never sent. He accepts as authentic Warren's January 1981 letter to his mother.
timeline.source: Peter Robbins, statement regarding Larry Warren, posted 13 June 2017 and updated 20 June 2017, hosted on Sacha Christie's blog, http://sacha-christie-infomaniachousewife.blogspot.com/2017/06/peter-robbins-statement-regarding-larry.html

timeline.label: FBI searches United Nuclear Scientific in a Michigan homicide investigation
timeline.text: A two-page Laingsburg, Michigan police report records an 'Agency Assist' supporting an FBI search of United Nuclear Scientific in aid of 'a homicide investigation out of Houghton, MI involving poison', and records that Lazar consented to the search. The underlying case is the thallium death of Janel Sturzl, 31, on 22 December 2015. Lazar is not recorded as a suspect. The report was obtained by Tim McMillan under a local open-records request.
timeline.source: Laingsburg Police Department report, published by The Black Vault, https://www.theblackvault.com/casefiles/documents-on-2017-bob-lazar-united-nuclear-raid-laingsburg-police-department/

timeline.label: DD Form 1910 submitted
timeline.text: Elizondo, as Director of the National Programs Special Management Staff, submits a clearance request for three .mpg files — GoFast, Gimbal and FLIR — for research and analysis only, expressly 'not for publication'.

timeline.label: DD Form 1910 approved
timeline.text: The clearance request is approved. Forty-one days later Elizondo resigns; six weeks after that the files appear in the New York Times.

timeline.label: Skidmore and Fitts publish the unsupported-adjustment compilation
timeline.text: Mark Skidmore of Michigan State University and Catherine Austin Fitts publish a summary report compiling unsupported journal voucher adjustments reported in public OIG and GAO documents for FY1998-FY2015: roughly $21 trillion at DoD and $350 billion at HUD. The authors state that the public reports 'only provide summary information; thus it is impossible for us to conduct a detailed assessment of the nature of these unsupported adjustments and errors'.

timeline.label: Elizondo drafts AATIP transition memo for Tipton
timeline.text: Emails later released under FOIA show Elizondo drafting a memorandum to help Neill Tipton 'assume the new responsibilities for AATIP' — five years after the Department says the program ended.

timeline.label: Resignation letter #1
timeline.text: 'Effective 4 October 2017, I humbly submit my resignation as Director, National Programs Special Management Staff... I respectfully request I receive a deferred retirement.' Hand-delivered.

timeline.label: Resignation memorandum to the Secretary
timeline.text: A memorandum saluted 'Mr. Secretary' protesting that 'certain individuals in the Department remain staunchly opposed to further research on what could be tactical threats,' and asking the Secretary to 'ask the hard questions'.

timeline.label: To The Stars Academy launches
timeline.text: DeLonge, Puthoff, Semivan, Justice, Elizondo and Mellon appear on one masthead, with a Regulation A+ offering targeting $50 million and divisions for Science, Aerospace and Entertainment.

timeline.label: To The Stars Academy formed
timeline.text: Puthoff co-founds TTSA with Tom DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Steve Justice, creating a public-company vehicle for materials acquisition and analysis.

timeline.label: Publisher suspends distribution of Left at East Gate
timeline.text: Cosimo, Inc.: 'Cosimo is announcing that it is suspending the distribution of the book, Left at East Gate, by Larry Warren and Peter Robbins', because 'some of the experiences described in this book may be inaccurate or embellished'.
timeline.source: Cosimo, Inc., publisher's announcement, 'Announcement: Left at East Gate', http://cosimoblog.blogspot.com/2017/10/announcement-left-at-east-gate.html

timeline.label: First Kotlikoff-Skidmore Forbes column
timeline.text: 'Has Our Government Spent $21 Trillion of Our Money without Telling Us?' puts the aggregate in front of a financial-markets readership. Two further columns follow in July 2018 and January 2019, the second asking directly whether the concealment is intentional.

timeline.label: FASAB issues the exposure draft for SFFAS 56
timeline.text: The exposure draft of what becomes SFFAS 56 is issued on 14 December 2017 with comments requested by 16 March 2018. FASAB receives seventeen responses from preparers, auditors and professional associations. Seventeen comment letters is the entirety of the public deliberation on a standard authorising modified public financial reporting across the federal government.

timeline.label: NAVAIR's chief technology officer writes to the patent examiner
timeline.text: The Chief Technology Officer of the Naval Aviation Enterprise wrote directly to examiner Philip Bonzell about application 15/141,270, agreeing that the claimed mode of movement was 'beyond the state of the possible, at least at present', describing a funded NAWCAD test programme already a year old, and arguing that the Navy should hold the patent because 'China is already investing significantly in this area'.

timeline.label: New York Times reveals the program
timeline.text: The Times names the program, the $22 million, Harry Reid and Bigelow Aerospace, and quotes Luis Elizondo as the official who ran it.

timeline.label: FLIR1 published by the New York Times
timeline.text: The Nimitz footage enters public circulation and reopens the entire subject.

timeline.label: New York Times breaks AATIP
timeline.text: Cooper, Blumenthal and Kean publish 'Glowing Auras and Black Money', naming AATIP, its $22 million, Harry Reid, Bigelow Aerospace and Luis Elizondo, with two of the three videos.

timeline.label: Pentagon acknowledges the program
timeline.text: Spokesman Thomas Crosson confirms AATIP existed and was shut down in 2012 because 'there were other, higher priority issues that merit' the funding. This is acknowledgement, not denial.

timeline.label: NYT reveals AATIP
timeline.text: Leslie Kean, Ralph Blumenthal and Helene Cooper publish the New York Times story revealing $22.5M in DoD spending on the Advanced Aerospace Threat Identification Program - the article that makes the modern disclosure era possible.

timeline.label: 'Glowing Auras and Black Money'
timeline.text: Cooper, Blumenthal and Kean reveal AATIP, the $22 million appropriation, Elizondo's resignation and the Navy videos. No new physical evidence; decisive institutional standing. Every subsequent official act follows from this date.

timeline.label: FOIA 18-F-0324 filed
timeline.text: John Greenewald files the FOIA request that will eventually produce the resignation letters and the Garry Reid memoranda. The Department takes until August 2022 to release eight pages.

timeline.label: Garry Reid memorandum to the Secretary
timeline.text: Reid answers six questions from the Secretary's office, asserts Elizondo 'aggrandized his role' and had 'no job responsibilities related to the AATIP', questions the second letter's 'uncertain provenance', and records an AFOSI inquiry.

timeline.label: Mahood's retrospective: nothing at Papoose Lake, S-4 is a Tonopah radar facility
timeline.text: Tom Mahood publishes his mature assessment: there is 'nothing at Papoose Lake', S-4 refers to a radar facility at the Tonopah Test Range, and the alien-craft narrative began as a cover story after the April 1989 detention. It concedes in the same document that Lazar is 'amazingly believable' and that Mahood initially found the story plausible. T.D. Barnes reaches the same radar-site conclusion by an unrelated route in 2026.
timeline.source: Tom Mahood, https://otherhand.org/home-page/area-51-and-other-strange-places/looking-at-the-bob-lazar-story-from-the-perspective-of-2018/

timeline.label: DIA sends SASC the list of 38 products
timeline.text: Brian L. Jenkins, DIA Chief of Records Management, writes to Senators McCain and Reed enclosing all 38 product titles — the authorizing committee's first formal notification about a ten-year program.

timeline.label: Mellon's Washington Post op-ed
timeline.text: 'The military keeps encountering UFOs. Why doesn't the Pentagon care?' — a former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence taking the question to the op-ed page.

timeline.label: The only rejection the electromagnetic field generator ever drew
timeline.text: USPTO mailed the single non-final rejection in application 14/807943. A telephone interview followed on 10 July and the applicant responded on 19 July. Enablement was never raised in this case.

timeline.label: Navy appeals the rejection of the inertial mass reduction craft patent
timeline.text: After a final rejection on 27 March 2018, the Department of the Navy filed a Notice of Appeal, then an Appeal Brief on 21 August 2018 accompanied by a Rule 131/132 affidavit. The examiner allowed the application on 31 October 2018 before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board ruled.

timeline.label: Examiner: the physics is sound, the claims are still not enabled
timeline.text: The Advisory Action on application 15/141,270 recorded that the examiner agreed 'the math and physics are sound in this application' while holding the claims not enabled, and asked the applicant to demonstrate the effect. The application was allowed three months later without any demonstration appearing in the file.

timeline.label: ADAM partners with EarthTech
timeline.text: TTSA's SEC filings record the launch of materials research relevant to Space-Time Metric Engineering in partnership with Harold Puthoff's EarthTech International.

timeline.label: Electromagnetic field generator allowed on prior art, not on enablement
timeline.text: The Notice of Allowability for application 14/807943 allowed claims 1-12 because 'the prior art fails to show' the claimed generator. The craft application, which incorporates this generator by reference, was under appeal at that moment for being impossible.

timeline.label: SFFAS 56 effective date
timeline.text: The standard takes effect for reporting periods beginning after 30 September 2018 - the first period following the Department of Defense's first full-scope financial statement audit.

timeline.label: SFFAS 56 'Classified Activities' issued
timeline.text: FASAB issues the standard permitting an entity to present amounts associated with one financial statement line item in another 'but not presenting narrative explaining the modification', to omit disclosures that would reveal classified information, and to move a component reporting entity from one consolidation to another. Paragraph 12 requires entities to disclose that such modifications are permitted while expressly forbidding them to disclose that they applied the Statement.

timeline.label: Karl Wolfe dies
timeline.text: Karl R. Wolfe, 19 April 1944 to 10 October 2018, per his funeral home obituary at Lansing, New York. The obituary does not mention US Air Force service, an employer, an education or a career, which is the whole of the independent record on him.
timeline.source: Obituary of Karl R. Wolfe, Lansing Funeral Home, Lansing, New York, https://www.lansingfuneralhome.com/obituaries/karl-wolfe

timeline.label: TTSA's $37.4 million deficit reported
timeline.text: Vice reports SEC filings showing a $37.4 million accumulated deficit, $129,000 cash on hand, roughly $1 million raised against a $50 million target, and a going-concern warning.

timeline.label: First full-scope DoD audit: disclaimer of opinion
timeline.text: David L. Norquist, Under Secretary of Defense (Comptroller) and Chief Financial Officer, writes in the FY2018 Agency Financial Report: 'In FY 2018, the Department underwent its first full-scope financial statement audit. As anticipated, our independent auditor, the Department of Defense Office of Inspector General, issued a Disclaimer of Opinion as the result of the audit.' It will be the first of eight.

timeline.label: Bob Lazar: Area 51 and Flying Saucers released digitally in the United States
timeline.text: Jeremy Corbell's 97-minute documentary, narrated by Mickey Rourke, featuring Lazar, George Knapp and Joy White. Letterboxd lists United States digital release on 1 November 2018, United Kingdom physical on 4 December 2018 and United States physical on 8 December 2018. The widely cited '4 December 2018' is the UK physical date; IMDb returned HTTP 403 and no distributor record was opened.
timeline.source: Letterboxd record, https://letterboxd.com/film/bob-lazar-area-51-and-flying-saucers/

timeline.label: Former PDDNI Donald Kerr elected MITRE board chairman
timeline.text: MITRE's trustees elect a former director of Los Alamos and of the National Reconnaissance Office as chairman, and former House Intelligence Committee chairman Mike Rogers as vice chairman.

timeline.label: US 10,144,532 granted
timeline.text: The inertial mass reduction craft patent issued to the Secretary of the Navy. Reporting states the application had first been rejected and was granted after the Naval Aviation Enterprise chief technology officer asserted operability to the USPTO and cited Chinese development of comparable technology.

timeline.label: US 10,144,532 granted, with Philip J Bonzell named as primary examiner
timeline.text: The printed front page gives 'Primary Examiner - Philip J Bonzell', the same person the board's existing Tier 1 claim names as the addressee of the Sheehy letter of 15 December 2017. 4 claims, 1 drawing sheet, term extended 153 days under 35 U.S.C. 154(b). A PATENT IS TIER 1 FOR WHAT IT CLAIMS AND NEVER FOR WHETHER THE THING WORKS.
timeline.source: US Patent 10,144,532 B2, printed front page, https://patentimages.storage.googleapis.com/de/4c/43/62c585ccc936cc/US10144532.pdf , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: House Oversight and Senate HSGAC written into the SAP reporting statute
timeline.text: Sec. 103 of Pub. L. 115-390 amends 50 U.S.C. 3348 to substitute 'the congressional oversight committees' for 'Congress' throughout subsections (a)-(e), replaces 'appropriate oversight committees' in (f)(1), and adds the (g)(1) definition naming the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs and the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform alongside leadership and jurisdictional committees.

timeline.label: House Oversight named a statutory recipient of SAP reports
timeline.text: Section 103 of Public Law 115-390 amends 50 U.S.C. 3348 to substitute 'the congressional oversight committees' for 'Congress' throughout and defines that term to include the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform and the Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.

timeline.label: Grusch joins UAPTF; tasked to inventory SAPs
timeline.text: As NRO's representative to the UAP Task Force, Grusch is asked by the Task Force Director to identify all special access programs and controlled access programs needed to satisfy the Task Force's congressionally mandated mission. He is, in his sworn words, cleared to literally all relevant compartments.

timeline.label: Read-on request denied
timeline.text: Grusch testifies he was informed in the course of official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program and was denied the additional read-ons when he requested them. No official account has ever explained the denial or its authority.

timeline.label: A private company signs a federal exploitation agreement over claimed exotic material
timeline.text: To The Stars Academy executes CRADA 19-15, 'Novel & Emerging Technology Exploitation,' with the US Army CCDC Ground Vehicle Systems Center. It is filed with the SEC the following year, making it the only fully documented private-custody chain in the file.

timeline.label: The 38 DIRD titles enter the public record
timeline.text: Nick Pope publishes the DIA transmittal letter; researchers begin extracting the individual reports through FOIA, eventually obtaining 37 of 38.

timeline.label: DIA releases the 38-title list
timeline.text: DIA responds to Steven Aftergood's FOIA request with the list of 38 AATIP research titles funded 2007-2012 at approximately $22 million, previously provided to Congress in January 2018.

timeline.label: Elizondo's evaluation published
timeline.text: Keith Kloor publishes the 'exemplary' rating and the supervisor's language on the importance of Elizondo's portfolio in Issues in Science and Technology.

timeline.label: Wilson-Davis notes surface
timeline.text: The fifteen pages enter public circulation. Davis confirms the notes are his; Wilson denies the meeting and its substance. No agency has attempted to reconcile the two.

timeline.label: Pentagon moves to kill JASON
timeline.text: OUSD(R&E) confirms it is ending the JASON contract managed by MITRE. Two weeks later NNSA posts a notice of intent to award a short-term sole source contract to MITRE, and the panel survives.

timeline.label: Tipton originates the denial formula
timeline.text: Internal email: Elizondo 'had no assigned responsibilities for this program.' A colleague warns the Department risks 'contradicting previous statements'; the chain closes with 'we will have to keep our messages in synch.'

timeline.label: Friedman dies
timeline.text: Stanton Friedman dies of a heart attack at Toronto Pearson Airport returning from a lecture. He had donated his research files to the Provincial Archives of New Brunswick in the months before his death.

timeline.label: The five observables reach print
timeline.text: The earliest dated publication of the five as a set located for this board, attributing them to Luis Elizondo from his AATIP work. The Navy's PAX 205 briefing, which itemises four of them as design goals, predates it by four years.

timeline.label: Pentagon confirms AATIP studied UAP
timeline.text: Christopher Sherwood tells the New York Post that AATIP 'did pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena'.

timeline.label: 'Unidentified' premieres on History
timeline.text: The TTSA-produced series presents Elizondo as having run AATIP for eight years, prompting The Intercept to test the Department's position.

timeline.label: 'No responsibilities with regard to the AATIP program'
timeline.text: Christopher Sherwood's statement to The Intercept becomes the Department's fixed position on Elizondo and remains so for the next seven years.

timeline.label: Elizondo writes to DoD Public Affairs
timeline.text: His 'final effort to avoid seeing this unfortunate situation escalate', with attached substantiating documents the Department did not release.

timeline.label: Pentagon authenticates Reid's letter, denies its meaning
timeline.text: Susan Gough confirms the 2009 SAP request is genuine while restating that Elizondo 'had no assigned responsibilities for AATIP while he was in OUSD(I)'.

timeline.label: Gough authenticates the Reid memo and reaffirms the denial
timeline.text: 'It makes no change to previous statements. Mr. Elizondo had no assigned responsibilities for AATIP while he was in OUSD(I).' She adds that DIA administered AATIP and Elizondo was never assigned to DIA.

timeline.label: US 10,322,827 granted
timeline.text: The high frequency gravitational wave generator patent issued to the Secretary of the Navy.

timeline.label: USS Kidd first sights drones
timeline.text: USS Kidd spots UAVs around 2200; USS Rafael Peralta and USS John Finn also report activity, with a white light hovering over Peralta's flight deck for over 90 minutes at 16 knots in low visibility.

timeline.label: 'Multiple UAVs around ship'
timeline.text: USS Kidd's deck log records the phrase at 2120; USS Russell reports objects changing elevation and direction; the cruise ship Carnival Imagination reports five or six drones. The event runs nearly three hours.

timeline.label: TTSA announces metamaterials acquisition
timeline.text: The ADAM Research Project announces possession of material reportedly from an advanced aerospace vehicle of unknown origin; Steve Justice says its structure and composition match no known military or commercial application.

timeline.label: ADAM Research Project announced
timeline.text: TTSA announces acquisition of 'potentially exotic materials'; COO Steve Justice concedes they came from sources 'with varying levels of chain-of-custody documentation'.

timeline.label: Further swarm events
timeline.text: Additional incidents are logged on 25 and 30 July 2019. The Navy, Coast Guard and FBI investigate and the matter reaches the Chief of Naval Operations without any attribution being made.

timeline.label: DD Form 1910 released via FOIA
timeline.text: The unredacted form is published, identifying Elizondo by name and OUSD(I) title as the officer who cleared the three video files in August 2017.

timeline.label: NAWCAD concludes testing: the Pais Effect could not be proven
timeline.text: Timothy Boulay, Communications Director at NAWCAD: 'When NAWCAD concluded testing in September 2019, the "Pais Effect" could not be proven.' Three years, $508,000, of which $462,000 was salaries. The sponsor tested its own patent and reported the negative result.
timeline.source: Brett Tingley, The War Zone, quoting Timothy Boulay of NAWCAD, https://www.twz.com/39012/the-navy-finally-speaks-up-about-its-bizarre-ufo-patent-experiments , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Navy designates the objects UAP
timeline.text: Joseph Gradisher: 'The Navy designates the objects contained in these videos as unidentified aerial phenomena' — while stating the Navy never released them and that no DOPSR record of an unrestricted-release request exists.

timeline.label: Entropy kinematics paper
timeline.text: Knuth, Powell and Reali publish 'Estimating Flight Characteristics of Anomalous Unidentified Aerial Vehicles' - the first quantitative UAP performance analysis in a peer-reviewed physics journal.

timeline.label: $35,000 SEC filing
timeline.text: Vice reports TTSA's SEC filing recording $35,000 paid for six pieces of bismuth/magnesium-zinc metal and a piece of aluminium previously held by Linda Moulton Howe.

timeline.label: TTSA-Army CRADA signed
timeline.text: Jeffery Langhout for the Army GVSC and Kari DeLonge for TTSA sign a five-year cooperative research agreement covering inertial mass reduction, metamaterials, quantum communications, beamed energy propulsion and active camouflage.

timeline.label: The Army signs for the material
timeline.text: GVSC Director Jeffery Langhout signs a CRADA with To The Stars Academy at Detroit Arsenal covering inertial mass reduction and metamaterial waveguides. The text is released 18 October; all twenty-nine emails of correspondence are later withheld in full.

timeline.label: CRADA announced publicly
timeline.text: Dr. Joseph Cannon of Army Futures Command calls TTSA 'an exciting, non-traditional source for novel materials'. The Army releases the agreement text the next day.

timeline.label: US Army CRADA signed
timeline.text: TTSA enters a five-year cooperative research and development agreement with the US Army Combat Capabilities Development Command covering inertial mass reduction, metamaterials, quantum physics and beamed energy propulsion.

timeline.label: Davis briefs SASC staff
timeline.text: Eric Davis gives a classified briefing on retrievals of unexplained objects to staff members of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

timeline.label: Davis briefs SSCI members
timeline.text: Two days later Davis briefs members of the Senate Intelligence Committee on the same subject.

timeline.label: Gough reverses: 'Neither AATIP nor AAWSAP were UAP related'
timeline.text: The Department repudiates its own May 2019 acknowledgement, saying Sherwood was repeating an earlier spokesperson who 'is no longer with my organization', and that AATIP 'did not pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena'.

timeline.label: Kit Green DIRD released
timeline.text: Popular Mechanics publishes Green's AAWSAP medical study, revealing the Institute for Advanced Studies at Austin imprint, the November 2007 Puthoff/Hathaway proposal and the human-injury reverse-engineering hypothesis.

timeline.label: Army withholds all CRADA correspondence
timeline.text: CCDC FOIA Officer Joy L. Linton locates 29 emails totalling 100 pages of TTSA-Army correspondence and denies all of them under exemptions (b)(4) and (b)(5).

timeline.label: Davis briefs a DoD agency
