timeline.text: Davis gives a classified briefing to a Defense Department agency about retrievals from 'off-world vehicles not made on this earth'. The agency has never been identified.

timeline.label: Papoose Lake photographed from the air on a legal overflight: nothing there
timeline.text: Tyler Rogoway of The War Zone publishes aerial images taken on a pilot's authorised flight directly over Papoose Lake: 'nothing appears to be there, just as satellite images show. There isn't even an access road and, as you can see, the lakebed is flooded, which is a fairly common occurrence.'
timeline.source: Tyler Rogoway, The War Zone, https://www.twz.com/32951/pilots-rare-trip-around-area-51-includes-pics-of-range-targets-drone-bases-ufo-legends

timeline.label: DoD releases the three Navy videos
timeline.text: The Department authorizes release of FLIR1, GIMBAL and GO FAST, stating 'The aerial phenomena observed in the videos remain characterized as unidentified.'

timeline.label: DoD authorises release of the three videos
timeline.text: The Department releases FLIR1, Gimbal and GoFast officially, calls their earlier appearance the product of 'unauthorized releases in 2007 and 2017', and states the phenomena 'remain characterized as unidentified'.

timeline.label: The Department releases FLIR1
timeline.text: DoD authorises release of the three Navy videos, stating the phenomena 'remain characterized as unidentified' - the government authenticating the artefact and declining to explain it.

timeline.label: The Pentagon authenticates the imagery
timeline.text: The Department of Defense formally releases FLIR1, GIMBAL and GOFAST, confirming the videos are genuine while stating the phenomena in them remain unidentified. The government thereby authenticates the evidence and declines to explain it - the exact posture the disclosure movement has been arguing against ever since.

timeline.label: 'The truth... is that I ran the program'
timeline.text: Elizondo writes to Susan Gough noting she corrected the AATIP/UAP statement but never the statement about him. The letter sits in the Department's own FOIA reading room.

timeline.label: 'We couldn't make it ourselves'
timeline.text: The New York Times publishes Davis's account of his briefings and his statement about the analysed material, alongside Harry Reid's call for information on retrieved craft to come out.

timeline.label: UAP Task Force approved
timeline.text: Deputy Secretary of Defense David Norquist approves the UAP Task Force under the Department of the Navy with OUSD(I&S) cognizance. The Navy announces it on 14 August.

timeline.label: UAP Task Force established under Navy lead
timeline.text: The Deputy Secretary of Defense formalises the government's UAP effort under USD(I&S) cognisance with the Department of the Navy leading, placing it in ONI's institutional orbit and out of the hands of offices with acquisition equity.

timeline.label: Elizondo, Mellon and Justice leave TTSA
timeline.text: The three government-side principals depart; the aerospace and materials work winds down and the entity later renames itself To The Stars Inc.

timeline.label: The NISPOM is published as a federal rule
timeline.text: 32 CFR Part 117 published at 85 FR 83312, 21 December 2020, with the carve-out written into 117.6(b): 'The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07.'

sources.name: 32 CFR Part 117 (eCFR); Source: 85 FR 83312, Dec. 21, 2020

timeline.label: An IC controlled access program is expanded to include reverse engineering
timeline.text: AARO confirms that one intelligence community CAP was 'unnecessarily expanded in 2021 to include a UAP reverse-engineering mission' without evidence or mission need, and was later disestablished.

timeline.label: The Navy says so publicly, through a named spokesman
timeline.text: Brett Tingley, 'The Navy Finally Speaks Up About Its Bizarre "UFO Patent" Experiments', The War Zone, updated 1 February 2021. This is the citation that replaces the board's previous encyclopedia sourcing for the same fact: a named NAWCAD official quoted by a named reporter, giving the window, the sum, the salary share and the result.
timeline.source: Brett Tingley, The War Zone, https://www.twz.com/39012/the-navy-finally-speaks-up-about-its-bizarre-ufo-patent-experiments , opened 2026-09-19

timeline.label: Gorightly publishes the confession in Saucers, Spooks and Kooks
timeline.text: Daily Grail Publishing, ISBN 978-0994617682. The book was NOT opened by this session; the confession was read as reproduced by Hayakawa quoting it, which is why every dependent claim is capped at Tier 2 and why opening the book is this cluster's highest-value upgrade.
timeline.source: Norio Hayakawa, 23 April 2021 and 2 April 2024, https://noriohayakawa.wordpress.com/2021/04/23/thomas-e-castello-never-existed-admitted-the-late-tal-levesque-originator-of-the-dulce-base-myths/

timeline.label: Clifford Stone dies at Roswell
timeline.text: Kevin Randle: 'Clifford E. Stone, known for his relentless pursuit of UFO documentation through his use of FOIA died on February 10, in Roswell, New Mexico.' Randle sets out in the same post the discrepancies between Stone's account and his service record.
timeline.source: Kevin D. Randle, 'Cliff Stone Has Died', A Different Perspective, https://kevinrandle.blogspot.com/2021/02/cliff-stone-has-died.html

timeline.label: 32 CFR Part 117 takes effect; the carve-out becomes regulation
timeline.text: With the NISPOM's conversion from DoD 5220.22-M into a codified rule, the DCSA carve-out ceased to be an internal departmental arrangement and became a provision of the Code of Federal Regulations, citing DoDD 5205.07 by URL.

sources.name: 32 CFR 117.6 (eCFR)

timeline.label: The NISPOM becomes federal regulation at 32 CFR Part 117
timeline.text: The carve-out provision moves from a DoD manual into the Code of Federal Regulations at 117.6(b)(3): the Director, DCSA 'will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision'.

timeline.label: McCandlish declared deceased at 1946 Trumpet Drive, Redding, California
timeline.text: Shasta County Sheriff-Coroner case C21-0324, Verdict of Death (without jury): 'In the matter of the death of Mark Edward McCandlish, a 68 year old male ... he was declared deceased on the 13th day of April 2021.' Cause of death 'Gunshot wound of head'; other significant conditions 'None'.
timeline.source: Shasta County Sheriff-Coroner, Verdict of Death, case C21-0324, https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UNSHXesvWduXFduto_Cqh4LDOCG4gIkX/view

timeline.label: External examination at 0713 by Dan Purtzer MD; no internal examination performed
timeline.text: The Report of External Examination, dated 04/19/21 at 0713, gives the cause of death as 'central nervous system damage caused by self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head', records an entrance wound '1 cm above the right ear' whose edges 'have powder burns' and an exit wound above the left ear, and states on page 2: 'Due to the obvious cause of death, internal examination is not performed.'
timeline.source: Shasta County Sheriff-Coroner, Report of External Examination, case C21-0324, https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UNSHXesvWduXFduto_Cqh4LDOCG4gIkX/view

timeline.label: Elizondo files DoD IG complaint
timeline.text: Alleging 'malicious activities, coordinated disinformation, professional misconduct, whistleblower reprisal and explicit threats', naming Garry Reid, Susan Gough and Neill Tipton.

timeline.label: 60 Minutes brings the aviators forward
timeline.text: Fravor, Dietrich, Graves, Mellon and Elizondo appear on CBS; Dietrich gives her first public account: 'I never wanted to be on national TV, no offense.'

timeline.label: 60 Minutes segment
timeline.text: Elizondo, Mellon and Navy aviators appear in a CBS 60 Minutes report on UAP in restricted U.S. airspace, weeks before the ODNI preliminary assessment.

timeline.label: Doty's 321-page New Mexico State Police personnel file released
timeline.text: Obtained by John Greenewald under the New Mexico Inspection of Public Records Act, NMSA 14-2-1 et seq., and released by the New Mexico Department of Public Safety with redactions. His Air Force service dates, rank progression and separation are inside the PDF, which was not opened by this session.
timeline.source: The Black Vault, 20 May 2021, https://www.theblackvault.com/documentarchive/richard-doty-personnel-file-new-mexico-state-police/

timeline.label: Doty personnel file published
timeline.text: A 321-page New Mexico State Police personnel file for Richard Doty is released under state public-records law - documentation federal FOIA never produced.

timeline.label: Gough's partial re-reversal
timeline.text: The Department concedes the AATIP contract 'allowed for research drawn from a wide variety of sources, including reports of UAPs' while insisting UAP examination 'was not the purpose of AATIP'. The denial of Elizondo's role does not move.

timeline.label: Nolan says he was approached
timeline.text: Nolan tells KQED that representatives of the government and an aerospace corporation asked him to assess medical harm from 'supposed interactions with an anomalous craft'.

timeline.label: Nine transients on a 1950 plate
timeline.text: Villarroel and colleagues report nine simultaneously occurring transients on a single Palomar plate from 12 April 1950 in Scientific Reports.

timeline.label: Verdict of Death signed by Chief Deputy Coroner Logan Stonehouse; manner of death Suicide
timeline.text: The verdict gives manner of death as Suicide and records that 'Phillip Wacker, Deputy Coroner, conducted the investigation and established the identity of the decedent. A postmortem examination was conducted by Dr. Dan Purtzer, M.D., Pathologist.' The postmortem it rests on is an external examination that expressly declined an internal one.
timeline.source: Shasta County Sheriff-Coroner, Verdict of Death, case C21-0324, https://drive.google.com/file/d/1UNSHXesvWduXFduto_Cqh4LDOCG4gIkX/view

timeline.event: ODNI delivers Preliminary Assessment: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena - 144 USG reports, one resolved (a deflating balloon)

timeline.label: ODNI preliminary assessment: 144 reports
timeline.text: 144 reports from USG sources spanning November 2004 to March 2021; only one resolved with high confidence; 18 incidents in 21 reports showed unusual movement; aviators face 'disparagement' for reporting.

timeline.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment
timeline.text: ODNI delivers the 9-page Preliminary Assessment to Congress: 144 incidents, one explained, and the data-limitation formula that every AARO annual report will reuse through FY2025.

timeline.label: ODNI Preliminary Assessment published
timeline.text: Nine pages, 144 reports, 80 with multiple sensors, five explanatory categories - and a contributor list naming NRO, NGA, NSA, DIA, Navy/ONI, DARPA, FAA and NOAA. The list is the most useful part of the document.

timeline.label: First disclosure to the DoD Inspector General
timeline.text: Grusch provides classified information to the DoD IG regarding the improper withholding and concealment of UAP-related material from Congress, ten months before the ICIG filing.

timeline.label: Galileo Project founded
timeline.text: Avi Loeb founds the Galileo Project four weeks after the ODNI preliminary assessment, on the premise that unclassified instrumentation is the way past a classified impasse.

timeline.label: 'Skinwalkers at the Pentagon' published
timeline.text: The DIA program manager, the contractor's deputy administrator and the reporter who broke the story publish a DOPSR-cleared insider account including Lacatski's claim of entering a craft of unknown origin.

timeline.label: CEFAA becomes SEFAA
timeline.text: By Resolución Exenta N° 04/3/0113/1385 the Chilean office is moved in the DGAC organisation chart to the Subdepartamento Comunicacional and renamed the Sección de Estudios de Fenómenos Aéreos Anómalos.

timeline.label: Grusch becomes NGA co-lead for UAP analysis
timeline.text: Joins NGA as a GS-15 Senior GEOINT Capabilities Requirements Officer and becomes the agency's co-lead for UAP and trans-medium object analysis, reporting to the UAPTF and later to AARO. Reviewing overhead collection of such events is one of his primary tasks.

timeline.label: AOIMSG stood up
timeline.text: Deputy Secretary Hicks directs establishment of the Airborne Object Identification and Management Synchronization Group, a coordinating layer with no independent authority, overseen by AOIMEXEC.

timeline.label: FY2022 NDAA signed; UAP office written into statute
timeline.text: Public Law 117-81 is approved. Section 1683, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373, requires DoD and ODNI to stand up a standing UAP office within 180 days, designate line organizations able to 'rapidly respond to, and conduct field investigations of' UAP incidents, and run a science plan aimed at performance 'that exceed the known state of the art in science or technology' and at providing 'the foundation for potential future investments to replicate any such advanced characteristics and performance.'

sources.name: Public Law 117-81, National Defense Authorization Act for FY2022 (full text, GPO)

timeline.label: Sec. 1683 enacted
timeline.text: The FY2022 NDAA is signed as P.L. 117-81. Section 1683, Gillibrand's provision, orders a permanent UAP office stood up within 180 days and is codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373.

timeline.label: FY2022 NDAA enacted
timeline.text: P.L. 117-81 creates the statutory requirement for a permanent UAP office and the reporting regime that becomes 50 U.S.C. 3373.

timeline.label: Harry Reid dies
timeline.text: The senator who created the funded lineage and was refused the SAP he asked for dies in Henderson, Nevada.

timeline.label: The statutory annual DoD SAP report to Congress lapses
timeline.text: Per the 'Termination of Reporting Requirements' note carried with 10 U.S.C. 119 in the U.S. Code: the provisions of subsecs. (a) and (b) requiring submittal of an annual report to Congress terminated effective 31 December 2021 under sec. 1061 of Pub. L. 114-328. The annual SAP census and the annual new-SAP notice are the two pieces that lapsed; the (c), (d) and (f) notices did not.

timeline.label: Americans for Safe Aerospace founded
timeline.text: Ryan Graves builds the aircrew reporting channel the Navy did not provide; by July 2023 it has nearly 5,000 members and is working with more than 30 UAP witnesses.

timeline.label: AARO contracts Oak Ridge to test the magnesium specimen
timeline.text: The Pentagon's UAP office sends its one publicly acknowledged material sample to a laboratory operated by UT-Battelle - a partnership including the same Battelle Memorial Institute that analysed the Air Force's UFO data in the 1950s.

timeline.label: First peer-reviewed UAP materials analysis
timeline.text: Nolan, Vallee, Jiang and Lemke publish the SIMS and MIBI analysis of the Council Bluffs mass in Progress in Aerospace Sciences: no isotopic anomaly, but metals mixed incompletely by an industrial process of unknown origin.

timeline.label: DIA cannot find the Utah ranch report
timeline.text: DIA tells a FOIA requester it can locate no report matching 'Utah Ranch Investigation: August 2009-February 2010' as described by the program's own manager.

timeline.label: IAA FY2022 sec. 413 compels immediate handover of UAP data
timeline.text: Public Law 117-103 is approved, carrying the Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2022 as Division X. Section 413 (50 U.S.C. 3373a) requires the DNI and SecDef jointly to make every IC element and DoD component with UAP data 'make such data available immediately' to the UAP Task Force and NASIC, with classified quarterly reports to the intelligence and armed services committees.

sources.name: Public Law 117-103, Consolidated Appropriations Act 2022 (incl. Div. X, Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2022) (full text, GPO)

timeline.label: Congress creates a no-waiver oversight regime for IC controlled access programs
timeline.text: Sec. 504 of the FY2022 Intelligence Authorization Act (Pub. L. 117-103, div. X, 136 Stat. 986) adds sec. 501A to the National Security Act, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3091a: semiannual DNI briefings on every CAP in effect, a bar on establishing any CAP, compartment or subcompartment before notifying the intelligence and appropriations committees and the four congressional leaders, and annual reports listing every active and terminated compartment and subcompartment. There is no waiver provision.

timeline.label: Congress creates a statutory oversight regime for IC Controlled Access Programs
timeline.text: Section 504 of the FY2022 Intelligence Authorization Act, Public Law 117-103, adds section 501A to the National Security Act: semiannual briefings on every CAP, a prohibition on establishing a CAP or compartment before notification, and annual reports listing every active and terminated compartment with a DNI certification for each.

timeline.label: John Lear dies
timeline.text: The Museum of Flight Archives authority record states: 'John Lear died on March 29, 2022.' He was born 3 December 1942, the son of William Powell Lear and Moya Olsen Lear, and his materials sit within the William P. and Moya Olsen Lear Family Collection.
timeline.source: The Museum of Flight Archives, https://archives.museumofflight.org/agents/people/4962

timeline.label: Garry Reid removed
timeline.text: Reid is removed as Director for Defense Intelligence after DoD IG investigations substantiate ethics violations, 65 instances of official business on personal email, and unwelcome physical contact with subordinates.

timeline.label: Classified conversation with Sean Kirkpatrick
timeline.text: Three months before Kirkpatrick takes over AARO, Grusch briefs him in a classified setting and passes him concerns. Grusch later testifies he was happy to give counsel on where to look; Kirkpatrick did not follow up.

timeline.label: Grusch files the ICIG urgent-concern complaint
timeline.text: Charles McCullough III, himself a former Intelligence Community Inspector General, files a Disclosure of Urgent Concern(s) and Complaint of Reprisal with the ICIG on behalf of David Grusch, covering information Grusch had gathered from 2019.

timeline.label: Congress asks DoD about the Wilson-Davis memo
timeline.text: At the House Intelligence subcommittee UAP hearing, Ronald Moultrie and Scott Bray are asked directly about the Wilson-Davis memo and the Malmstrom missile events and state they are unaware of them.

timeline.label: First open congressional UAP hearing in over fifty years
timeline.text: The House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, Subcommittee on Counterterrorism, Counterintelligence, and Counterproliferation met at 9:00 a.m. in Room HVC-210 with Rep. Andre Carson presiding, taking testimony from Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security Ronald S. Moultrie and Deputy Director of Naval Intelligence Scott W. Bray. Carson opened by saying the subcommittee would 'bring that organization out of the shadows', referring to AOIMSG.
timeline.source: HHRG-117-IG05-Transcript-20220517, https://www.congress.gov/117/meeting/house/114761/documents/HHRG-117-IG05-Transcript-20220517.pdf , 2022-05-17

timeline.label: NASA commissions its panel
timeline.text: NASA commissions the sixteen-member UAP Independent Study Team under David Spergel - with access to unclassified data only.

timeline.label: PPD-19 urgent-concern complaint filed with the ICIG
timeline.text: Charles McCullough III, the first Inspector General of the Intelligence Community, files Grusch's urgent-concern complaint with the office he once ran.

timeline.label: ICIG finds the complaint credible and urgent
timeline.text: The Intelligence Community Inspector General determines the complaint credible and urgent - the statutory finding that obliges transmission to the congressional intelligence committees.

timeline.label: ICIG finds the complaint credible and urgent
timeline.text: The statutory determination that obliges transmission to the congressional intelligence committees. It has never been withdrawn, and no executive-branch document reconciles it with AARO's later findings.

timeline.label: AARO established
timeline.text: Hicks signs the memorandum creating AARO, disestablishing AOIMSG, and ordering the Navy to disestablish the UAPTF and transfer its data and materials. Announced 20 July.

timeline.event: AARO established as the UAPTF's successor entity, per the ODNI 2022 Annual Report

timeline.label: FOIA 18-F-0324 released
timeline.text: Four years and eight months after the request, DoD releases the two resignation letters and the two Garry Reid memoranda — eight pages.

timeline.label: DIA finally releases the AAWSAP contract
timeline.text: Fourteen years after award and eleven years after withholding it, DIA releases contract HHM402-08-C-0072 under FOIA-00349-2018, with all government personnel names redacted.

timeline.event: Pub. L. 117-263 enacted; Sec. 6802 rewrites 50 U.S.C. 3373, setting a 540-day Historical Record Report deadline (15 June 2024) and a four-year annual-report requirement

timeline.label: FY2023 NDAA creates AARO and the whistleblower channel
timeline.text: Public Law 117-263 is approved. Section 1673 (50 U.S.C. 3373b) creates a secure authorized-reporting mechanism covering federal and contractor activity involving 'material retrieval, material analysis, reverse engineering', voids nondisclosure agreements as against authorized disclosures, overrides EO 13526 and Atomic Energy Act chapter 18 restrictions, and bans reprisal including clearance revocation. Division F sec. 6802 rewrites 50 U.S.C. 3373 to establish the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office and inserts the statutory definitions of 'unidentified anomalous phenomena' and 'transmedium objects or devices'.

sources.name: Public Law 117-263, James M. Inhofe National Defense Authorization Act for FY2023 (incl. Div. F, Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2023) (full text, GPO)

timeline.label: AARO named; Historical Record Report ordered
timeline.text: P.L. 117-263 carries IAA FY2023 Sec. 6802, restating Sec. 1683 to name the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office, and Sec. 1673, creating the authorized reporting channel that voids nondisclosure agreements.

timeline.label: FY2023 NDAA UAP whistleblower protections enacted
timeline.text: The FY2023 National Defense Authorization Act includes provisions permitting authorized UAP disclosures without retaliation regardless of prior nondisclosure agreements. The Debrief reports Grusch helped draft the language.

timeline.label: AARO codified in statute
timeline.text: The FY2023 NDAA (P.L. 117-263) codifies AARO and its public reporting mandate at 50 U.S.C. 3373, including the annual report deadline AARO later misses.

timeline.label: US 10,135,366 expires for non-payment of maintenance fees
timeline.text: The first of the two granted Pais patents lapsed for non-payment of the first maintenance fee, five weeks before the inertial mass reduction patent did the same. USPTO had mailed a maintenance fee reminder on 11 July 2022.

timeline.label: US 10,144,532 expires for non-payment of maintenance fees
timeline.text: Four years after fighting an appeal to obtain the grant, the Navy did not pay the first maintenance fee on the inertial mass reduction craft patent. USPTO records it as expired under 37 CFR 1.362, placing the invention in the public domain.

timeline.event: ODNI 2022 Annual Report on UAP finalised (PDF creation date); catalogue reaches 510 reports as of 30 Aug 2022

timeline.label: The Navy's own report on the Tic Tac surfaces
timeline.text: 72 range fouler reports posted to the Navy FOIA reading room include the 14 November 2004 incident: a 46-foot object with no nacelles, pylons or wings, and the disposition line 'Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.'

timeline.label: 72 range fouler reports released
timeline.text: The Navy releases 72 previously Secret//FVEY range fouler reports covering 2004-2021, including the Nimitz report describing a 46-foot object with no nacelles, pylons or wings.

timeline.label: DoD IG interviews Elizondo
timeline.text: A 103-page transcript of the Inspector General's interview of Elizondo is later released under FOIA, along with 126 pages of DoD IG UAP emails in February 2024.

timeline.label: Alaska object destroyed
timeline.text: US fighters destroy an object at 40,000 feet described as the size of a small car, cylindrical and silver-grey with no apparent propulsion, over Prudhoe Bay. It is tracked as UAP #20.

timeline.label: Yukon object destroyed
timeline.text: An F-22 destroys a small cylindrical object at 40,000 feet over the Yukon; the Canadian Privy Council records it as UAP #23, unverified as to function, propulsion or national affiliation.

timeline.label: Lake Huron object destroyed
timeline.text: Two F-16CMs of the 148th Fighter Wing destroy an object at roughly 20,000 feet with an AIM-9X. A pilot reports 'I can't tell if it's metallic or what, but I can see like lines coming down below it.'

timeline.label: Galileo Project overview published
timeline.text: Loeb and Laukien publish the project's architecture in the Journal of Astronomical Instrumentation, alongside Cloete et al.'s detection and tracking platform - methods published before observations.

timeline.label: Charette Secret memo to Trudeau
timeline.text: The Clerk of the Privy Council records that exploitation of UAP #20 is incomplete and that UAP #23's function and propulsion are unknown.

timeline.label: USS Jackson records four objects
timeline.text: At about 1915 PST in Warning Area W-291, USS Jackson's CIC records four self-luminous tic-tac objects, one emerging from the ocean, on a Star SAFIRE EO/IR system with intact position and time metadata.

timeline.label: USS Jackson: a light rising from the waterline
timeline.text: At about 1915 PST in W-291 off Southern California, Senior Chief Alexandro Wiggins observes a self-luminous object emerge from the ocean, join three others, and depart with near-instantaneous acceleration. CIC records it on the ship's Star SAFIRE and reports to the Tactical Action Officer.

timeline.label: Sixteen senators demand full AARO funding
timeline.text: Gillibrand and Rubio lead fourteen colleagues insisting AARO receive the amount in the classified attachment, arguing the office offers 'increased transparency to the American people.'

timeline.label: The EG&G account published as Congress reopens the question
timeline.text: Liberation Times publishes George Knapp's account of Al O'Donnell describing a recovered saucer and a live being, together with D'Amato's public statement and his reported private view that a private-company cover-up was 'entirely feasible.'

timeline.label: Public call to audit Lockheed Martin's special access programs
timeline.text: Jeremy Corbell challenges the Senate Appropriations Committee to audit Lockheed Martin SAPs; Elizondo responds that the inquiry should extend to several other aerospace companies that have likely played a key historical role.

timeline.label: DoD clears Grusch's statements for open publication
timeline.text: DOPSR approves his first submission on 4 April and his second on 6 April 2023. Internal reviewer correspondence in the FOIA release shows the sensitive-areas references were raised and judged not a problem.

timeline.label: Grusch leaves federal service
timeline.text: He departs NGA and the government to pursue accountability through public disclosure, his information cutoff date for anything he can attest to from inside.

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick testifies to SASC on AARO
timeline.text: The Senate Armed Services Subcommittee on Emerging Threats and Capabilities holds an open hearing on 'The Mission, Activities, Oversight, and Budget of the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office' with AARO Director Sean Kirkpatrick as sole witness, following a closed session the same day. Printed as S. Hrg. 118-648 (CHRG-118shrg60390).

sources.name: CHRG-118shrg60390 (S. Hrg. 118-648), 'The Mission, Activities, Oversight, and Budget of the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office', SASC Subcommittee on Emerging Threats and Capabilities

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick testifies to the Senate
timeline.text: The only open Senate hearing on AARO under its first director. Kirkpatrick reports 650+ cases and no credible evidence of extraterrestrial activity. Published as S.Hrg. 118-648.

timeline.label: IM1 Pacific expedition
timeline.text: The Galileo Project drags a magnetic sled across the seabed off Papua New Guinea, recovering several hundred sub-millimetre spherules from the CNEOS 2014-01-08 site.

timeline.label: Grusch allegations published
timeline.text: The Debrief publishes David Grusch's crash-retrieval allegations; Tim Burchett begins publicly demanding a House hearing.

timeline.label: The Debrief publishes the Grusch allegations
timeline.text: Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal report that the US has retrieved intact and partially intact craft of non-human origin, with on-record corroboration from Karl Nell, Christopher Mellon and a serving NASIC officer using the name Jonathan Grey.

timeline.label: Grusch story published by The Debrief
timeline.text: Kean and Blumenthal publish David Grusch's claim that the US operates a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse-engineering programme. The New York Times, which ran their 2017 scoop, does not run it; The Debrief does.

timeline.label: Coulthart broadcasts Grusch
timeline.text: Ross Coulthart's NewsNation interviews convert the ICIG complaint from a written allegation into a broadcast event, giving it a face and a national audience.

timeline.label: The paper of record declines the Grusch story
timeline.text: Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal, whose 2017 AATIP scoop the New York Times published, take the David Grusch story to The Debrief instead. The story did not fail verification; it failed placement. The change of venue is an artefact of institutional appetite and belongs in the concealment record, not the journalism record.

timeline.label: Grusch names the mechanism on the record
timeline.text: In The Debrief, Leslie Kean and Ralph Blumenthal quote Grusch: 'Individuals on these UAP programs approached me in my official capacity and disclosed their concerns regarding a multitude of wrongdoings, such as illegal contracting against the Federal Acquisition Regulations and other criminality and the suppression of information across a qualified industrial base and academia.' Procurement fraud, not merely secrecy, is the accusation.

timeline.label: Department denies Grusch's claims
timeline.text: OSD Public Affairs, through Susan Gough, states AARO has not discovered verifiable information substantiating claims of a programme possessing or reverse-engineering extraterrestrial materials - a statement bounded by AARO's discoveries, not the Department's knowledge.

timeline.label: The MoD file covering the Calvine period is signed closed until 2076
timeline.text: DEFE 24/1940, 'UFO reports', 1 August 1990 to 31 January 1991, former reference D/Sec(AS)12/2 Part J, carries closure code 84 under the criterion 'Personal information where the applicant is a 3rd party', a Freedom of Information Act exemption instrument signed on 7 June 2023, and a record opening date of 1 January 2076. The closure is the series norm rather than a singling out: the neighbouring files open between 2072 and 2077 on the same basis. A redacted digital copy, DEFE 24/1940/1, has been open since 20 October 2008 and would not download from this environment.
timeline.source: The National Archives Discovery catalogue record for DEFE 24/1940, https://discovery.nationalarchives.gov.uk/API/records/v1/details/C11483085

timeline.label: Pentagon issues the standing denial
timeline.text: Susan Gough: AARO has not discovered any verifiable information to substantiate claims that any programs regarding the possession or reverse-engineering of extraterrestrial materials have existed in the past or exist currently. The sentence bounds itself to what one office has discovered.

timeline.label: First television interview with Ross Coulthart
timeline.text: Grusch says the recoveries are non-human origin technical vehicles, that we are definitely not alone, that sometimes you encounter dead pilots, and that a sophisticated disinformation campaign targets the public.

timeline.label: Senate Intelligence Committee votes to compel a contractor inventory
timeline.text: S. 2103 Sec. 1104, reported unanimously, would require any current or former federal contractor holding government-derived UAP material to notify the DNI within 60 days and produce 'a comprehensive list of all non-earth origin or exotic unidentified anomalous phenomena material,' with immunity for compliance.

timeline.label: S. 2226 introduced
timeline.text: Chairman Jack Reed introduces the FY2024 NDAA, the vehicle that will carry both UAP regimes.

timeline.label: Schumer submits the UAP Disclosure Act as S.Amdt. 797
timeline.text: 'SA 797. Mr. SCHUMER (for himself, Mr. Rounds, Mr. Rubio, Mrs. Gillibrand, Mr. Young, and Mr. Heinrich) submitted an amendment intended to be proposed by him to the bill S. 2226 ... which was ordered to lie on the table.' The text is the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act of 2023, including the exercise of eminent domain over recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence, and a nine-member Senate-confirmed Records Review Board.

sources.name: Congressional Record, 13 July 2023, Text of Senate Amendment 797 (CREC-2023-07-13-pt1-PgS2953)
congress.gov, S.Amdt.797 to S.2226 overview (Wayback capture 2024-12-18)

timeline.label: S.Amdt. 797 filed
timeline.text: Schumer submits the UAP Disclosure Act of 2023 with Rounds, Rubio, Gillibrand, Young and Heinrich; the text prints at 169 Cong. Rec. S2953-S2959. Warner files S.Amdt. 666, the IAA carrying the contractor turn-in, the same day.

timeline.label: Michael Herrera's account enters the public record on a dated recording
timeline.text: 'Michael Herrera - US Marine Encounters UFO Black Ops Human Trafficking Operation | SRS #66 (Part 1)' premiered on the Shawn Ryan Show, runtime 1:26:50. The artefact is dated and openable; the account within it is a man's own statement and nothing more.
timeline.source: Shawn Ryan Show #66 part 1, YouTube video id 3zm4nh3S66I, 2023-07-17

timeline.label: Hearing noticed
timeline.text: The Oversight National Security subcommittee announces a UAP hearing with Graves, Grusch and Fravor as witnesses.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies to House Oversight under oath
timeline.text: The House Oversight Subcommittee on National Security, the Border, and Foreign Affairs hears Ryan Graves, David Grusch and Cdr. David Fravor (Ret.) in room 2154 Rayburn. Grusch testifies that he 'was informed in the course of my official duties of a multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program to which I was denied access', and, asked whether recovered biologics were human or nonhuman, answers 'Nonhuman'. Printed as Serial No. 118-53 (CHRG-118hhrg53022).

sources.name: CHRG-118hhrg53022, printed hearing transcript, 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', Serial No. 118-53
Official hearing transcript PDF, HHRG-118-GO06-Transcript-20230726.pdf (docs.house.gov)

timeline.label: Aviators testify to House Oversight
timeline.text: Fravor and Graves testify alongside David Grusch. Fravor's statement: 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.'

timeline.label: The founding hearing
timeline.text: Grothman gavels in the first modern House UAP hearing in 2154 Rayburn and waives Burchett, Luna, Gaetz, Burlison, Ocasio-Cortez and Ogles onto the subcommittee.

timeline.label: SCIF access denied before the hearing
timeline.text: Burchett opens by disclosing that members were denied a classified SCIF briefing with Grusch before the hearing 'due to the amount of hoops that we had to jump through to grant temporary clearance.'

timeline.label: Non-human biologics, under oath
timeline.text: Answering Mace, Grusch testifies that biologics came with some recoveries and that they were assessed non-human by people with direct knowledge still on the program.

timeline.label: Gaetz: the Eglin radar sequence
timeline.text: Gaetz describes being initially refused images, radar and full crew access at Eglin AFB, obtaining a photograph and one crew member after a discussion about how authorities flow, and asks that the radar material be subpoenaed. It never was.

timeline.label: Ogles names the Holman Rule
timeline.text: Ogles volunteers to initiate the Holman Rule against any personnel, program or agency that denies Congress access to Grusch in a SCIF. No such amendment has been offered.

timeline.label: AOC finds the notification loophole
timeline.text: Ocasio-Cortez identifies that there are no statutory definitions or requirements for congressional notification and asks whether notification means a phone call to a chairman or 'an email to, hypothetically, a dead email box.'

timeline.label: House Oversight hearing
timeline.text: Grusch testifies under oath, thirteen days after the amendment premised on his allegations is filed.

timeline.label: Sworn testimony before House Oversight
timeline.text: Grusch testifies to a multi-decade crash retrieval and reverse engineering program, over 40 witnesses interviewed across four years, nonhuman biologics recovered with craft, personal knowledge of people harmed, and funding by misappropriation and contractor IR&D. Members state they were denied a SCIF.

timeline.label: House Oversight UAP hearing
timeline.text: George Knapp attends; the hearing establishes the congressional venue that Shellenberger will use sixteen months later.

timeline.label: Grusch names IR&D under oath
timeline.text: Asked how unreported programs are funded, Grusch answers 'misappropriation of funds and self-fund,' then identifies IR&D as the channel, and tells the committee that contractors have no obligation to report UAP encounters.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies under oath
timeline.text: House Oversight hearing at which Grusch testifies that the UAP Task Force Director tasked him to inventory relevant SAPs and that the read-ons were refused.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies as the NRO's former representative to the UAP Task Force
timeline.text: The House Oversight Committee takes sworn testimony in 2154 Rayburn. Grusch's official witness title places the National Reconnaissance Office inside the chain of custody of the modern allegation.

timeline.label: Grusch testifies under oath to House Oversight
timeline.text: At 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Implications on National Security, Public Safety, and Government Transparency', Grusch testifies alongside Ryan Graves and David Fravor. His written statement describes a 'multi-decade UAP crash retrieval and reverse engineering program' to which he was denied access and refers to 'Non-Human Reverse Engineering Programs'. It contains no funding detail; that he reserved for classified session.

timeline.label: Grusch, Fravor and Graves testify
timeline.text: The first congressional hearing at which a former intelligence officer testifies under oath to a multi-decade crash retrieval programme. No contractor is called and no document production is compelled.

timeline.label: Three witnesses under oath
timeline.text: David Grusch, David Fravor and Ryan Graves testify under oath before the House Oversight Committee. Grusch describes a multi-decade retrieval and reverse-engineering programme reported to him by individuals he named to the Intelligence Community Inspector General; Fravor and Graves describe what they personally observed with sensor corroboration.

timeline.label: Senate passes S. 2226 carrying the full UAP Disclosure Act
timeline.text: S. 2226 as engrossed in the Senate contains DIVISION G--UNIDENTIFIED ANOMALOUS PHENOMENA DISCLOSURE, secs. 9001-9015, in full: the Records Collection, the Review Board, the eminent-domain provision, the 25-year disclosure deadline, and the appropriations authorization.

sources.name: S. 2226, 118th Congress, Engrossed in Senate (BILLS-118s2226es) - contains DIVISION G, UAP Disclosure Act of 2023, secs. 9001-9015

timeline.label: Senate passes both regimes
timeline.text: S. 2226 passes the Senate carrying Division G, Secs. 9001-9015 including the eminent domain command, and Division M Sec. 1102, the contractor turn-in with immunity.

timeline.label: AARO director calls the hearing insulting
timeline.text: Kirkpatrick posts, in a statement the Pentagon authenticates, that the hearing was insulting to DoD and IC officers and that the central source of the allegations has refused to speak with AARO.

timeline.label: Senate passes eminent domain over privately held recovered technology
timeline.text: Division I of the Senate-passed NDAA includes Sec. 9010: 'The Federal Government shall exercise eminent domain over any and all recovered technologies of unknown origin and biological evidence of non-human intelligence that may be controlled by private persons or entities.'

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick calls the hearing 'insulting'
timeline.text: The sitting AARO director posts publicly that the congressional UAP hearing was insulting to the workforce; the White House distances itself from the remarks.

timeline.label: Turner disparages the testimony
timeline.text: The HPSCI chairman says the striking thing about the hearing was that 'repeatedly over and over again, the whistleblowers had to say, actually, I don't have any knowledge.'

timeline.label: Hicks takes direct oversight of AARO
timeline.text: Days after Grusch testifies, the Deputy Secretary pulls AARO out of the USD(I&S) chain; its director now reports directly to her.

timeline.label: Grusch's psychiatric-detention records published
timeline.text: Ken Klippenstein publishes Loudoun County police records of Grusch's 2014 and 2018 emergency custody episodes, obtained under Virginia FOIA, two weeks after the sworn testimony. Members of Congress later describe the leak as a discrediting operation.

timeline.event: DoD OIG issues classified report DODIG-2023-109, finding DoD has no overarching UAP policy

timeline.label: DoD IG completes DODIG-2023-109
timeline.text: The Inspector General finds no department-wide UAP policy and component-level stovepipes, and cannot confirm that UAP threats have been identified and addressed. The full report stays classified.

timeline.label: Sol Foundation founded
timeline.text: Garry Nolan and Peter Skafish co-found The Sol Foundation, the first institution to treat UAP simultaneously as a materials, governance and public-understanding problem.

timeline.label: DoD IG issues DODIG-2023-109
timeline.text: The Inspector General finds no comprehensive DoD approach to UAP, combatant commanders largely excluded, and no requirement that components report UAP incidents to AARO.

timeline.label: DODIG-2023-109 issued and classified
timeline.text: The DoD Inspector General completes the only formal evaluation of the Department's UAP conduct three weeks after Grusch testifies. The report is classified; only an unclassified summary is released.

timeline.label: UAP Caucus founded
timeline.text: Burchett launches the bipartisan Congressional UAP Caucus and leads a caucus letter to the Intelligence Community Inspector General about UAP retrieval programs.

timeline.label: aaro.mil launched
timeline.text: AARO launches its public website, initially without the mandated reporting mechanism; the secure reporting portal for USG employees and contractors follows in October 2023.

timeline.event: NASA releases the UAP Independent Study Team final report

timeline.label: NASA report released; director unnamed
timeline.text: The UAP Independent Study Team report finds analysis 'hampered by poor sensor calibration, the lack of multiple measurements, the lack of sensor metadata.' NASA announces a Director of UAP Research and declines to name him at the briefing.

timeline.label: NASA panel reports and dissolves
timeline.text: The UAP Independent Study Team delivers its report - no evidence of extraterrestrial origin, data quality is the binding constraint - and dissolves the same day. It had never been given the classified holdings.

timeline.label: NASA publishes the Independent Study Team report
timeline.text: Spergel's 16-member panel concedes that 'much of the data collected by military sensors or intelligence satellites are classified' and Nicola Fox announces a NASA Director of UAP Research.

timeline.label: First select committee push dies
timeline.text: Burchett's effort to create a House select committee on UAP collapses when Speaker Kevin McCarthy loses the speakership.

timeline.event: FY2023 Consolidated Annual Report on UAP released - 291 reports, 290 of them airborne

timeline.label: AARO FY2023 annual report
timeline.text: First statutory annual report: 291 new reports, 801 total holdings. It contains no finding of any kind on extraterrestrial technology.

timeline.label: FY2023 annual report
timeline.text: AARO's first statutory annual report: 291 new reports, cumulative holdings 801, no explicit extraterrestrial denial - that formula appears only from FY2024.

timeline.label: Sue Gordon elected MITRE board vice chair
timeline.text: A former Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence becomes vice chair of MITRE's governing board, three months after David Grusch's House Oversight testimony.

timeline.label: Grusch does not appear for the AARO interview
timeline.text: Having agreed on 10 November to meet, Grusch does not attend the Arlington appointment. AARO's memorandum for record makes this the centerpiece of its impeachment; the same document shows five prior months of approaches routed through intermediaries.

timeline.label: Inaugural Sol Foundation conference
timeline.text: Two days at Stanford, sponsored by the Nolan Laboratory and Stanford School of Medicine, with Eric Davis, Tim Gallaudet, Avi Loeb, Leslie Kean, Christopher Mellon, Karl Nell, Hal Puthoff and Jacques Vallee speaking. The movement acquires an academic address.

timeline.label: Turner and Rogers named
timeline.text: Reporting identifies Turner and Rogers as leading the effort to eliminate or alter the Act, with McConnell and Speaker Johnson supporting; Sheehan states Turner demanded the eminent domain provision and the subpoena power be struck.

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick leaves AARO for Oak Ridge
timeline.text: AARO's founding director departs government and becomes Chief Technology Officer for Defense and Intelligence Programs at the Battelle-operated laboratory that had performed AARO's materials analysis.

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick departs AARO
timeline.text: Announced 7 November, effective 1 December. He joins Oak Ridge National Laboratory as CTO for Defense and Intelligence Programs the same month. Tim Phillips becomes Acting Director.

timeline.label: Langley incursions begin
timeline.text: The Air Force confirms Joint Base Langley-Eustis 'first observed UAS activities the evening of December 6' and experienced multiple incursions through the month. F-16 CAPs, NASA WB-57F orbits and FBI coordination follow.

timeline.label: Senate accepts the gutting in silence
timeline.text: The Senate's final consideration of the FY2024 NDAA produces no transcribed remarks containing the word 'anomalous'; no member objects aloud to the removal of the division the chamber had passed.

timeline.label: FY2024 NDAA enacted with the Review Board and eminent domain stripped
timeline.text: Public Law 118-31 is approved. Only secs. 9004-9006 of the Senate's Division G survive, renumbered as secs. 1841-1843 in Division A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C. The enacted text contains no Review Board and no eminent-domain provision. Postponement decisions revert to 'the original classification authority' holding the record, and Senior Agency Officials may unilaterally withdraw records from the Collection on notice to Congress. Sec. 1687 and IAA sec. 7343 impose conditional funding limits on unreported UAP special-access activity.

sources.name: Public Law 118-31, National Defense Authorization Act for FY2024 (full text, GPO)
S. 2226, 118th Congress, Engrossed in Senate (BILLS-118s2226es) - contains DIVISION G, UAP Disclosure Act of 2023, secs. 9001-9015

timeline.label: Money is cut off for unreported UAP special-access activity
timeline.text: Pub. L. 118-31 sec. 1687 (Secretary of Defense; this Act's funds) and div. G sec. 7343 (DNI; that division's funds) bar obligation or expenditure for any activity involving unidentified anomalous phenomena 'protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitation' unless details are provided to a committee list wider than the 10 U.S.C. 119(g) defense committees, plus the four congressional leaders. Both sections also disallow UAP-related independent research and development as an indirect contract expense unless disclosed.

sources.name: Public Law 118-31 (FY2024 NDAA incl. FY2024 IAA) — full text, GPO

timeline.label: The stripping is enacted
timeline.text: P.L. 118-31 is signed. Fifteen sections become three. The Review Board, the eminent domain clause, the Controlled Disclosure Campaign Plan, the $20,000,000 authorization, the contractor turn-in and the immunity grant are all gone. Sec. 7343 is left referring to an instruction it no longer identifies.

timeline.label: Eminent domain and the contractor inventory are stripped; the IR&D clause survives
timeline.text: Public Law 118-31 is enacted without the Review Board, the eminent domain provision or the SSCI contractor disclosure regime. It retains the records collection at Secs. 1841-1843 and the funding limitations at Secs. 1687 and 7343, including the IR&D restriction citing DoDI 3204.01 by change date.

timeline.label: FY2024 NDAA creates the UAP Records Collection
timeline.text: Sections 1841-1843 of P.L. 118-31 mandate a UAP Records Collection at the National Archives - without the review board, subpoena power or contractor reach in the original UAP Disclosure Act.

timeline.label: Sections 1841-1843 of Public Law 118-31 enacted
timeline.text: The UAP Disclosure Act is cut down in conference: the National Archives collection survives, the review board with subpoena power and the eminent domain provision over recovered technologies do not.

timeline.label: Congress bars UAP-related IR&D as an allowable indirect cost
timeline.text: Section 1687 of the FY2024 NDAA bars funds for UAP activity under special or restricted access limitation absent disclosure to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership, and provides that 'independent research and development funding relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena shall not be allowable as indirect expenses'. Section 7343 of the Intelligence Authorization Act enacts the same bar through the Director of National Intelligence. Congress has named the mechanism.

timeline.label: Congress cuts off money for unreported UAP special access activity
timeline.text: Sections 1687 and 7343 of Public Law 118-31 bar the obligation of funds for any UAP activity 'protected under any form of special access or restricted access limitations' unless the Secretary of Defense and the Director of National Intelligence respectively provide details to the defense and intelligence committees and congressional leadership, and make UAP-related independent research and development unallowable as an indirect expense.

timeline.label: The Review Board is stripped in conference
timeline.text: P.L. 118-31 is enacted with Subtitle C - a UAP Records Collection at NARA, an agency duty to transmit, and grounds for postponement. The independent Review Board and the eminent domain provision over recovered technologies, both passed by the Senate as Division I of H.R. 2670, are removed in conference where no recorded vote attaches.

timeline.label: AARO memorandum on Grusch interview attempts
timeline.text: AARO documents eight approaches to Grusch between June and November 2023 and concludes he had no intention of providing information. Later released as FOIA 24-F-0266.

timeline.label: Garcia files the reporting bill
timeline.text: Ranking Member Robert Garcia introduces H.R. 6967, the Safe Airspace for Americans Act, with Republican subcommittee chairman Glenn Grothman.

timeline.label: The ICIG briefing produces nothing
timeline.text: Inspector General Thomas Monheim briefs about sixteen House members for ninety minutes. Krishnamoorthi did not get the answers he hoped for; Burchett calls it 'more of the same' and a 4/10; Ogles says he asked specific questions and got no specific answers.

timeline.label: ICIG briefs House Oversight members in closed session
timeline.text: Members emerge saying they learned nothing new about UAP transparency from the Inspector General of the Intelligence Community.

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick publishes the circular-reporting thesis
timeline.text: In Scientific American the departing AARO director attributes the allegations to inadvertent disclosures of legitimate programs or unsupported belief, seven weeks before his agency's report advances the same frame.

timeline.label: Kirkpatrick op-ed in Scientific American
timeline.text: Seven weeks after leaving office and seven weeks before his report is published, Kirkpatrick calls the disclosure record circular reporting from a small group of interconnected believers and calls the whistleblowers suspect.

timeline.event: DoD OIG publishes the unclassified summary of DODIG-2023-109

timeline.label: IG summary released
timeline.text: The unclassified summary of DODIG-2023-109 is published; the findings are structural and the full report remains withheld.

timeline.label: DoD IG unclassified summary published
timeline.text: The public summary of DODIG-2023-109 lands, documenting that DoD does not require components to report UAP incidents to its own authoritative UAP office.

timeline.label: The Inspector General reports, mostly classified
timeline.text: The DoD Inspector General releases an unclassified summary of DODIG-2023-109, its evaluation of the Department's actions regarding UAP. The evaluation was initiated on personnel complaints; the public receives the summary.

timeline.label: IM1 spherules classified
timeline.text: Loeb et al. publish the recovery and classification of the Pacific spherules in Research Notes of the AAS, claiming a distinct extrasolar composition.

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Volume I
timeline.text: AARO reaffirms the MOGUL attribution and finds 'no empirical evidence' for reverse-engineering claims, without addressing the 1995 records-destruction finding or the JANAP channel.

timeline.label: AARO answers on the record
timeline.text: AARO publishes Volume I of its historical record report, concluding it found no empirical evidence that the US government or private companies have reverse-engineered extraterrestrial technology. The report is catalogued here in full: its scope, its access and its methodology are the parts a hostile audit turns on.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes the Battelle investigation
timeline.text: UAP Gerb's first corporate investigation, published with a full primary-document citation list including Project Stork, Special Report No. 14 and the Defense.gov Moultrie roundtable transcript. The method that will define the domain is established.

timeline.label: Seismic signal attributed to a truck
timeline.text: Fernando et al. publish in Geophysical Journal International that the seismic signal used to localise the IM1 search was consistent with truck traffic, not an impact - the search may have been in the wrong place.

timeline.label: McConnell retires after 37 years
timeline.text: Kirk McConnell leaves Capitol Hill after 37 years on defence and intelligence, including the Senate Armed Services Committee and both intelligence committees, and joins the UAP nonprofit sector.

timeline.event: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I cleared for open publication by DOPSR
AARO releases Historical Record Report Volume I - discloses KONA BLUE and an IC CAP 'unnecessarily expanded in 2021' to add a UAP reverse-engineering mission

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Report Vol. I published, confirming $22M FY2008/FY2010 appropriations at Reid's direction and AAWSAP=AATIP
timeline.source: https://www.aaro.mil/Portals/136/PDFs/AARO_Historical_Record_Report_Vol_1_2024.pdf

timeline.label: AARO publishes the official history
timeline.text: DoD confirms the $22M, the Reid direction, the contractor's UFO research 'with the support of the DIA program manager' and the ranch investigation — then closes the file and names no one.

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Volume 1
timeline.text: AARO's report treats 2009 as the standup year for AAWSAP and AATIP and states it found 'no evidence for the USG reverse-engineering narrative provided by interviewees'.

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I released
timeline.text: The formal DoD rebuttal: alleged reverse-engineering programs do not exist, are misidentified authentic programs, or were disestablished, and none of AARO's interviewees had firsthand knowledge. It identifies KONA BLUE, never engages Karl Nell by name, and never addresses the ICIG determination.

timeline.label: AARO Volume I published - and omits the era
timeline.text: AARO's historical record report names dozens of programmes but contains no mention of Kirtland, AFOSI, Bennewitz, Doty, MOON DUST, BLUE FLY, MJ-12, AQUARIUS, Rendlesham, Wilson or the 1975 nuclear-base overflights.

timeline.label: AARO publishes the corporate denials without naming a company
timeline.text: The Historical Record Report states that executives and chief technology officers of the named companies met AARO's Director and denied on the record ever having recovered, possessed or reverse-engineered extraterrestrial technology. No company is identified and no inspection is described.

timeline.label: Historical Record Report Volume I
timeline.text: AARO publishes its 63-page history under DOPSR-2024-0263, finding no empirical evidence of reverse-engineering, disclosing KONA BLUE, and stating it found no NDAs containing UAP-related information.

timeline.label: Historical Record Report Volume I released
timeline.text: AARO publishes Volume I: no empirical evidence of reverse-engineering, ~30 interviewees, the alleged sample identified as a terrestrial Mg-Zn-Bi alloy, Kona Blue disclosed, and the finding that AARO located no UAP-related NDAs. Tim Phillips fronts the rollout; Hicks does not endorse the findings.

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I
timeline.text: AARO states it partnered with 'the Special Access Program Control Offices for the DoD, IC, and DHS' and that its investigators had 'full access to all pertinent sensitive USG programs' - an assurance whose scope was defined by the offices under review.

timeline.label: AARO Historical Record Report Volume I is silent on money
timeline.text: The Pentagon's report on the historical record addresses retrieval and reverse-engineering claims at length and contains no discussion of misappropriated funds, illegal contracting, independent research and development, or contractor financial arrangements. The official rebuttal does not engage the financial allegation at all.

timeline.label: Burlison: 'They weren't transparent to us in a SCIF setting'
timeline.text: Burlison leads a bipartisan call for a House select committee on UAP focused first on expenditures, and states that DoD officials were not truthful to members in classified session.

timeline.label: Langley story surfaces
timeline.text: The War Zone publishes the Air Force's confirmation of the December 2023 incursions, three months after they ended.

timeline.label: 'ORNL Synopsis: Analysis of a Metallic Specimen'
timeline.text: Oak Ridge reports the specimen alleged to derive from a 1947 crash is a terrestrial magnesium alloy - while stating that neither AARO nor ORNL could verify its historical origin and that records of failed magnesium alloy designs are scant.

timeline.label: ORNL magnesium specimen analysis
timeline.text: AARO publishes the Oak Ridge synopsis of a metallic specimen with its own supplement - the first of only two physical-specimen characterisations it has released.

timeline.label: First UAP Transparency Act
timeline.text: Burchett introduces H.R. 8424. It dies in referral.

timeline.label: Kona Blue documents made public
timeline.text: The declassified DHS Kona Blue package, transmitted by Acting Deputy Secretary Kristie Canegallo on 5 February 2024, is published - a chartered prospective SAP intended to house UAP recovery and reverse-engineering, terminated 10 February 2012.

timeline.label: AARO and DHS publish the KONA BLUE history
timeline.text: The joint paper confirms that a DHS component head established a prospective special access program in 2011 and that the Deputy Secretary killed it six months later.

timeline.event: Statutory deadline under Sec. 6802(j)(1)(A) for the Historical Record Report (540 days after 23 Dec 2022 enactment); Volume II not delivered

timeline.label: UAPDA refiled as SA 2610
timeline.text: Rounds, for himself and Schumer, refiles the complete Act against the FY2025 NDAA with the eminent domain command unchanged. It is ordered to lie on the table and never called up.

timeline.label: ORNL reports the alleged crash specimen is terrestrial
timeline.text: AARO releases the Oak Ridge analysis of the magnesium alloy sample acquired from a private UAP organisation and the US Army: terrestrial isotopic composition, no waveguide capability, and an undocumented chain of custody.

timeline.label: Grusch sues over the records release
timeline.text: Files in Loudoun County Circuit Court against Sheriff Mike Chapman and a Sheriff's Office employee over the FOIA release of his emergency-custody records.

timeline.label: Off-World Technologies Division account published
timeline.text: Gerb documents witness 'RA', a Green Beret describing two non-human artifacts held underground near Crane, Indiana between 2013 and 2015, with alleged SAIC and Sandia connections.

timeline.label: Imminent published after a year of DOPSR review
timeline.text: Elizondo's memoir debuts at number one on the New York Times bestseller list. He later testifies that 'what is in the book is what I was told I am allowed to talk about'.

timeline.label: Kosloski named AARO director
timeline.text: Dr. Jon T. Kosloski, previously of the National Security Agency, becomes AARO's full-time director.

timeline.label: A signals technologist takes AARO
timeline.text: Jon Kosloski, a senior National Security Agency researcher, is named to lead AARO - placing the government's UAP analytic hub under someone whose professional formation is in the collection discipline that holds the most relevant withheld data.

timeline.label: Battelle's Mark Peters becomes MITRE CEO
timeline.text: MITRE's tenth president and CEO arrives directly from the post of executive vice president for laboratory management at Battelle Memorial Institute, having previously directed Idaho National Laboratory.

timeline.label: DoDD 5205.07 and DoDI 5205.11 reissued the same day
timeline.text: Both signed by Deputy Secretary of Defense Kathleen H. Hicks. The reissued Directive cancels the 2010 version and no longer contains the words 'waived', 'unacknowledged', 'carve-out' or a reference to 10 U.S.C. 119; those provisions now sit in DoDI 5205.11, which retains the glossary definitions, the para 1.2.f waiver designation, the Section 7 congressional access rules, and at para 1.2.i a scheduled phase-out of DCSA NISP oversight in July 2029.

timeline.label: DoDD 5205.07 reissued
timeline.text: The SAP policy directive is reissued, cancelling the 2010 version and incorporating the July 2023 SAP Enterprise Reform memorandum. The requirement to notify DoD SAPCO before briefing Congress with SAP material is carried forward.

timeline.label: DoD deletes acknowledged, unacknowledged, waived and carve-out from its SAP directive
timeline.text: The reissued DoD Directive 5205.07 cancels the 2010 version, incorporates the 11 July 2023 SAP Enterprise Reform guidance, and replaces the three-state taxonomy with 'Joint Force Integration SAP' and 'Strategic Enabler SAP'. Neither 10 U.S.C. 119(e) nor 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3) is repealed; the mechanisms survive while the vocabulary is removed from the public charter.

timeline.label: An MQ-9 fires a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen
timeline.text: The object appears struck and is not destroyed. The video is not shown publicly until Rep. Burlison plays it at a hearing eleven months later; the Department has never confirmed it.

timeline.label: The PDF of the Scott notes is created, per its own metadata
timeline.text: The file's own /CreationDate is 'D:20241017132510' and its /Producer and /Creator are both 'PDFium'. It is 9,172,025 bytes over 31 pages with 31 embedded JPEG page images and no text layer. Nothing in it establishes who held the notes between 1990 and 2024.
timeline.source: PDF metadata, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf, read 18 September 2026

timeline.label: Agency review deadline expires
timeline.text: The 300-day deadline in Sec. 1842(c)(1) for every Government office to review, identify and organise its UAP records passes.

timeline.label: The Debrief reports Immaculate Constellation
timeline.text: Micah Hanks publishes the first general-readership account of Shellenberger's alleged insider and the unacknowledged special access program, framed as an open question.

timeline.label: Immaculate Constellation surfaces publicly
timeline.text: The Debrief assesses the emerging Immaculate Constellation allegations weeks before the document reaches Congress.

timeline.label: Shellenberger publishes Immaculate Constellation
timeline.text: Public reports an alleged parent USAP consolidating UAP observations, sourced to a current or former US government official and confirmed to Shellenberger by a former intelligence community official.

timeline.label: UAP Gerb publishes 'Alien Reproduction Vehicle - the Testimony of Mark McCandlish'
timeline.text: Video id wF07QMm6joE, channel 'UAP Gerb', runtime 01:09:12. Its description opens 'In late 1988, accomplished aerospace illustrator Mark McCandlish came into information that indicated the United States ...'. This is the episode that brings the account to this board's corpus; several assertions attributed to Gerb in the corpus files are recorded on these nodes as unverified rather than as claims.
timeline.source: YouTube listing for video wF07QMm6joE, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wF07QMm6joE, opened 18 September 2026

timeline.label: Immaculate Constellation surfaces
timeline.text: An ODNI unclassified press item dated 22 October 2024 describes the alleged Immaculate Constellation programme; it is entered into the congressional record in November. AARO never addresses it in an annual report or statement for the record.

timeline.label: Guillot: no foreign nexus
timeline.text: The NORAD/NORTHCOM commander tells The War Zone 'I have not seen [and] I do not know of any organized or unorganized foreign nexus' to the Langley drones. NORAD's count stands at more than 600 drone reports over US installations since 2022.

timeline.label: First whistleblower bill
timeline.text: Burchett introduces H.R. 10111, the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act, with Mace, Luna and Burlison, the day before the Oversight hearing.

timeline.label: 'Immaculate Constellation' document entered into the congressional record
timeline.text: At the joint House Oversight hearing 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth', Chairwoman Mace enters into the record a 12-page Pentagon document describing 'the unacknowledged special access program called Immaculate Constellation', delivered to Congress by witness Michael Shellenberger. Witnesses: Gallaudet, Elizondo, Shellenberger, Gold. Printed as Serial No. 118-135 (CHRG-118hhrg57440).

sources.name: CHRG-118hhrg57440, printed hearing transcript, 'Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena: Exposing the Truth', Serial No. 118-135

timeline.label: Gallaudet discloses the recalled email
timeline.text: At the House Oversight joint hearing, Gallaudet testifies the January 2015 Fleet Forces Command safety message was deleted from all accounts within a day and concludes it 'must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency.' Shellenberger describes Immaculate Constellation.

timeline.label: Immaculate Constellation enters the Record
timeline.text: Shellenberger delivers a 12-page Pentagon document to Congress that morning; Chairwoman Mace moves it into the Congressional Record while every member on the dais reads it in real time.

timeline.label: Elizondo's SCIF-signed gag
timeline.text: Elizondo testifies that he signed a US Government document in a SCIF, before a security officer, permitting continued public speech on some topics but barring discussion of crash retrieval. Moskowitz walks him through the signing.

timeline.label: 'You'll be on some list'
timeline.text: Luna warns Mace from the dais that saying 'Immaculate Constellation' aloud will put her on a list. Mace says it anyway.

timeline.label: Grothman's access claim
timeline.text: Grothman states that no agency substantiated Grusch's claims 'despite our Committee Members endlessly questioning these agencies inside and outside of the SCIF' - a claim that cannot be reconciled with the read-in gate Luna documents ten months later.

timeline.label: Sworn testimony before House Oversight
timeline.text: Elizondo answers 'Yes' under oath to secret UAP crash retrieval programs and to their reverse-engineering purpose, and describes 'a culture of suppression and intimidation that I have personally been victim to'.

timeline.label: Elizondo corroborates Grusch under oath
timeline.text: Asked by Rep. Burchett whether he agreed the US has run a multi-decade UAP crash, retrieval and reverse engineering program, Luis Elizondo answers 'Yes, sir,' and discloses he worked with Grusch at US Space Force.

timeline.label: Shellenberger submits the Immaculate Constellation report
timeline.text: Michael Shellenberger testifies to a House Oversight subcommittee and hands over a twelve-page report describing a USAP secretly collecting UAP data outside acknowledged channels. The programme name enters the congressional record.

timeline.label: Elizondo confirms the blocked contractor transfer on the record
timeline.text: Rep. Burlison reads the Lockheed Martin - Bigelow Aerospace - CIA account into the hearing; Elizondo answers 'What I can say is that it was blocked.' Rep. Mace elicits confirmation that material is allocated to contractors by domain expertise.

timeline.label: A USAP name enters the Congressional Record
timeline.text: Shellenberger delivers a 12-page Pentagon document on Immaculate Constellation and Chairwoman Mace moves it into the Record; Elizondo declines to confirm or deny by name or trigraph.

timeline.label: House Oversight hearing: Exposing the Truth
timeline.text: Elizondo, Gallaudet, Gold and Shellenberger testify before joint House Oversight subcommittees, one day before AARO releases its FY2024 report.

timeline.label: A programme name enters the Congressional Record
timeline.text: Mace moves the twelve-page report into the record from the dais. Elizondo answers 'Yes' when asked whether the government has conducted secret UAP crash retrieval programs. Mace says certain individuals did not want the hearing to happen and does not name them.

timeline.event: FY2024 Consolidated Annual Report released - 757 reports, of which 392 are an FAA backfill; total holdings 1652

timeline.label: Michels interviews Shellenberger the next day
timeline.text: American Alchemy publishes the first long-form account of the document, one day after the hearing; 203,593 views.

timeline.label: AARO FY2024 annual report
timeline.text: 757 new reports, 1,652 total. The standing sentence appears for the first time: no evidence of extraterrestrial beings, activity, or technology. Kosloski says Volume II will follow within months.

timeline.label: FY2024 annual report and GREMLIN
timeline.text: 757 reports, 21 warranting further analysis, ~900 parked in the active archive. Kosloski discloses GREMLIN's 90-day collection and promises Volume II within months.

timeline.label: LANL publicly confirms the 1949 conference minutes
timeline.text: Los Alamos National Laboratory publishes that its National Security Research Center holds the minutes of the 16 February 1949 green fireballs conference and receives several UFO-related FOIA requests a year.

timeline.label: AARO reanalyses GO FAST
timeline.text: AARO's SASC case slides place the object at about 13,000 feet and 45 mph in 60-knot winds - 'did not demonstrate any anomalous speeds or flight characteristics.' Kosloski also concedes 'we do have some very anomalous objects.'

timeline.label: Kosloski testifies to the Senate
timeline.text: Over 1,600 reports held; no verifiable evidence of extraterrestrial beings, activity or technology; several cases 'truly anomalous'. No mention of whistleblowers, Immaculate Constellation, or Volume II.

timeline.label: The Scott notes are uploaded to arvp.co.uk
timeline.text: The PDF sits under the path /wp-content/uploads/2024/12/ on a site whose operator is not named anywhere on the pages opened. This is the point at which the only opened copy of the primary document enters the public record.
timeline.source: URL path, https://www.arvp.co.uk/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/SORENSEN-1990-INTERVIEW.pdf, read 18 September 2026

timeline.label: NARA Record Group 615 established
timeline.text: Under sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA (PL 118-31) the National Archives creates the UAP Records Collection, the first statutory records mechanism ever applied to this subject.

timeline.label: AARO briefs Congress on the New Jersey drone incursions
timeline.text: A classified briefing to lawmakers on the drone incursions spreading across New Jersey and neighbouring areas; content not disclosed publicly.

timeline.label: New Jersey drone wave peaks
timeline.text: Nocturnal drone sightings across New Jersey and neighbouring states generate more than 5,000 reports to the FBI.

timeline.label: Jesse Michels publishes the Eric Davis episode carrying the denial
timeline.text: Video id LnAiNChnuEQ, runtime 52:45, as opened on 18 September 2026 titled 'Eric Davis: A US President Was Briefed on UFOs!' on the channel 'Jesse Michels'. research/leads/michels-corpus-03.md file 04 recorded the same episode under the title 'CIA Scientist: George Bush Was Briefed on UFOs (ft. Eric Davis)' on 'American Alchemy'; the channel and the title now differ, and the corpus timestamp 0:36:24 to 0:38:00 falls inside the 52:45 runtime. The episode is identified by video id, not by title.
timeline.source: Jesse Michels, video id LnAiNChnuEQ, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LnAiNChnuEQ, opened 18 September 2026

timeline.label: Wright-Patterson closes its airspace
timeline.text: The base closes airspace for nearly four hours over unauthorized drone activity, days before the federal statement that nothing anomalous had been identified.

timeline.label: Four-agency joint denial
timeline.text: DoD, DHS, FBI and FAA: 'We have not identified anything anomalous.' About 100 of more than 5,000 reports were run down and attributed to commercial, hobbyist and law enforcement drones, manned aircraft, helicopters and stars.

timeline.label: Reissued ICD 906 posted
timeline.text: The reissued ICD 906, Controlled Access Programs, carries a PDF creation date of 19 December 2024 and states that it supersedes the ICD 906 signed 17 October 2015. It requires annual written re-justification of every unacknowledged CAP, terminates any CAP not submitted and approved, and vests non-discoverability approval in the DNI or PDDNI subject to annual re-validation.

sources.name: ICD 906 (current) — Internet Archive capture of dni.gov

timeline.label: Reissued ICD 906 released
timeline.text: The PDF of the reissued ICD 906 posted by ODNI carries a creation date of 19 December 2024 and states that it supersedes the ICD 906 signed 17 October 2015. It retains unacknowledged CAPs, adds the requirement that all CAPs and accesses be recorded in Scattered Castles subject only to DNI or PDDNI exemption, and confirms that neither it nor the DoD regime reaches 'special access programs under the purview of the National Security Council, such as covert action'.

timeline.label: Deadline passes for the SAP access-population reports
timeline.text: FY2024 IAA sec. 7606(c) required each agency head authorized by E.O. 13526 to establish a SAP to review, within one year of enactment (22 December 2023), the number of agency personnel eligible for access to such programs and report to a nine-committee list including both Judiciary Committees. No public record of any such report was located.

sources.name: Public Law 118-31 (FY2024 NDAA incl. FY2024 IAA) — full text, GPO

timeline.label: Deadline passes for the SAP access population reports
timeline.text: Section 7606(c) of the FY2024 Intelligence Authorization Act required each of the six officials authorised by E.O. 13526 to establish special access programs to report to nine congressional committees, including House Oversight, on how the number of personnel eligible for SAP access will be limited to the minimum required. The one-year deadline expired on this date. No such report has been publicly released.

timeline.label: FY2025 NDAA orders a GAO review of AARO and sunsets the Historical Record audits
timeline.text: Public Law 118-159 is approved. Title LXVIII sec. 6801 directs the Comptroller General to review AARO's implementation of 50 U.S.C. 3373; sec. 6802 ends the GAO briefing and reporting cadence on the UAP Historical Record Report a set period after AARO delivers its final volume.

sources.name: Public Law 118-159, Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for FY2025 (full text, GPO)

timeline.label: Congress bars moving a capability from a CAP into a SAP without notice
timeline.text: Pub. L. 118-159 sec. 6603 amends 50 U.S.C. 3091a(b) to prohibit an IC element head from transferring a capability from a controlled access program 'to a special access program (as defined in section 1152(g) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 1994 (50 U.S.C. 3348(g))), or to anything else outside the controlled access program' until notice of intent goes to the appropriate committees and congressional leadership -- with self-certified exceptions for an 'urgent counterintelligence issue' or 'organizational restructuring'. Sec. 6602 separately cuts off NIP funds for any new CAP until the subsection (b) notification is submitted.

sources.name: Public Law 118-159, Servicemember Quality of Life Improvement and National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2025 (incl. div. F, Intelligence Authorization Act for FY2025) — full text, GPO

timeline.label: FY2025 enacted with no disclosure regime
