timeline.text: P.L. 118-159 contains only a GAO review of AARO and a sunset on audit briefings. The FY2024 funding bar on undisclosed UAP special access programmes is not renewed.

timeline.label: FY2025 NDAA sunsets the Historical Record Report audit requirement
timeline.text: Section 6802 of the FY2025 NDAA ties the quarterly and semiannual audit and reporting requirements on the UAP Historical Record Report to 90 and 180 days after delivery of the final volume. The same Act does not re-enact the section 1687(a) funding bar, which lapsed with fiscal year 2024.

timeline.label: Congress prohibits moving a capability from a CAP into a SAP without notice
timeline.text: Sections 6602 and 6603 of Public Law 118-159 add a funding cutoff to 50 U.S.C. 3091a and prohibit the head of an IC element from transferring a capability from a controlled access program to a special access program, or to anything else outside the CAP, without prior notice to the intelligence and appropriations committees and congressional leadership - subject to exceptions for urgent counterintelligence and organisational restructuring.

timeline.label: Lacatski publishes 'New Insights'
timeline.text: The third volume of the DOPSR-cleared series continues releasing AAWSAP-derived material through trade publication rather than through FOIA or testimony.

timeline.label: Rubio leaves the Senate
timeline.text: The SSCI Vice Chairman who cosponsored the eminent domain text departs on confirmation as Secretary of State, removing the disclosure coalition's most senior intelligence-committee Republican.

timeline.label: Michels breaks Jake Barber
timeline.text: American Alchemy publishes Jake Barber's account of helicopter-borne craft retrieval; 1,010,989 views. An independent YouTube channel breaks a crash-retrieval whistleblower to a million people.

timeline.label: Task Force created
timeline.text: Chairman Comer establishes the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets and names Luna chairwoman; Comer and Luna write Rubio, Hegseth and Ratcliffe for all UAP records. Burchett files H.R. 1187 the same day.

timeline.label: Luna task force declassification push
timeline.text: The House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets lists UAP and unidentified submerged objects among its declassification priorities and requests an administration update.

timeline.label: Michels platforms UAP Gerb
timeline.text: 'The New Area51 Is HERE in Utah!' tours Air Force bases, deep underground facilities and FFRDCs associated with reverse engineering, tracing the effort from the 1947 Interplanetary Phenomenon Unit and Battelle's Project Stork forward; 450,091 views.

timeline.label: The Age of Disclosure premieres at SXSW
timeline.text: Dan Farah's documentary premieres in Austin with 34 senior government, military and intelligence figures on record, including James Clapper, Marco Rubio, Andre Carson and Jay Stratton.

timeline.label: 'The Age of Disclosure' premieres
timeline.text: Dan Farah's documentary premieres at SXSW with Puthoff, Davis, Travis Taylor and Nolan among 34 interviewees alongside serving and former officials.

timeline.label: Grusch joins the House staff
timeline.text: Eric Burlison hires David Grusch as a senior adviser on UAP issues for a four-month term.

timeline.label: Grusch becomes Special Advisor to Rep. Burlison
timeline.text: The central whistleblower in the record takes a formal position inside the legislative branch, with a brief on UAP transparency and service on the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.

timeline.label: NARA issues transfer guidance
timeline.text: Sixteen months after enactment and roughly six months after the statutory agency deadline, the National Archives issues guidance on transferring publicly releasable UAP records into Record Group 615.

timeline.label: Mellon says DoD improperly withholds unclassified UAP imagery
timeline.text: Christopher Mellon argues publicly that the Department is improperly withholding unclassified UAP imagery; AARO under Kosloski agrees to locate a specific F-18 video for declassification review.

timeline.label: USS Jackson footage surfaces publicly
timeline.text: The 2023 W-291 recording and independent analysis of it reach the public through journalists rather than through the Navy or AARO.

timeline.label: National Archives releases UAP records from four agencies
timeline.text: Under sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA, NARA publishes records transferred from ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the NRC into the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Collection, with rolling additions promised.

timeline.label: NARA digitisation continues
timeline.text: The National Archives UAP topic page records ongoing rolling accession into RG 615 and digitisation of legacy holdings. No AMC T-2 series and no CIRVIS report series have been identified.

timeline.label: First statutory UAP records transfer
timeline.text: NARA releases records from ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission. CIA, NSA, NRO, NGA, DIA, DOE, DHS and the military departments transfer nothing.

timeline.label: Nell publishes through Sol
timeline.text: Karl Nell's 'The UFO Enigma: A Call for US Government Disclosure' appears in the Sol Foundation white-paper series.

timeline.label: Elizondo's claimed 600-1,000-foot disc identified as an irrigation circle
timeline.text: At a UAP Disclosure Fund hearing Luis Elizondo presents an image described as a gigantic disc; analysts including Mick West identify it as an irrigation circle. The correction comes from the sceptic community, not the government.

timeline.label: AARO solicits a JWICS-hosted case management system
timeline.text: Its first market research solicitation, three years after standing up: a custom case system on the Top Secret/SCI intranet to track UAP data, interactions and records and to support a planned public reporting mechanism. Capability statements due 9 June 2025.

timeline.label: Canada's Sky Canada Project reports
timeline.text: The Office of the Chief Science Advisor of Canada publishes 'Management of Public Reporting of Unidentified Aerial Phenomena in Canada', recommending that a federal lead be identified and a dedicated service established to collect testimony, investigate and publish, and that Canada partner with AARO and NASA, GEIPAN and SEFAA. It is the first G7 report of the 2020s to name which foreign arrangements it would copy.

timeline.label: UAPx field results published
timeline.text: Szydagis, Knuth, Kugielsky and Levy publish the first peer-reviewed UAP field-expedition results in Progress in Aerospace Sciences - a published protocol with explicit false-positive handling.

timeline.label: WSJ reports the 'Yankee Blue' disinformation practice
timeline.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that the Air Force falsely convinced personnel they were on a reverse-engineering programme for decades, and that OSD ordered the practice halted in spring 2023.

timeline.label: Yankee Blue exposed
timeline.text: The Wall Street Journal reports that the Air Force ran a fictitious alien-technology programme on its own personnel for decades - NDAs, saucer photographs, threats - halted by an OSD memorandum in spring 2023. DNI Haines was briefed that hundreds and hundreds were affected. DoD says the findings will appear in Volume II.

timeline.label: Gillibrand's FY2026 claim
timeline.text: Gillibrand announces her FY2026 defense bill wins; her only UAP item is 'language to update congressional briefing requirements for UAP.'

timeline.label: Crane writes DoD on the Grusch reprisal
timeline.text: Rep. Eli Crane writes the Secretary of Defense about the removal of Grusch's clearance, denial of promotion and loss of medical retirement. The Department does not reply.

timeline.label: Rep. Crane writes DoD on Grusch's reprisal
timeline.text: Crane notifies the Department that Grusch suffered removal of his clearance, denial of promotion, and loss of medical retirement for his participation in UAP disclosure. He receives no reply.

timeline.label: AARO sponsors an unannounced UAP research workshop
timeline.text: Roughly 40 government, academic and independent researchers meet in the Washington DC area, hosted by Associated Universities, Inc., to standardise UAP data capture and analysis. No attendee list is published; the event is not reported publicly until March 2026.

timeline.label: JIATF-401 established
timeline.text: The Department stands up Joint Interagency Task Force 401 under Brig. Gen. Matt Ross to handle drone incursions over US installations.

timeline.label: AARO data-standardisation workshop
timeline.text: AARO holds a private workshop on UAP data standardisation with civilian researchers and academia, later reflected in a published white paper on narrative data and analysis.

timeline.label: AARO data standardization workshop
timeline.text: AARO holds a private workshop hosted by Associated Universities, Inc. in the Washington area on UAP data standardisation; the white paper is published in February 2026.

timeline.label: Privacy suit dismissed with prejudice
timeline.text: The court holds Virginia's mental health confidentiality statute reaches court files rather than police records and that the redacted release complied with FOIA - establishing that no legal shield protected the whistleblower's records.

timeline.label: Whistleblower bill refiled
timeline.text: Burchett reintroduces the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act as H.R. 5060 with Luna and Crane.

timeline.label: AARO explains why it cannot declassify
timeline.text: AARO publishes a declassification information paper: it cannot declassify independently, must request review from originating offices, and is bound by DOPSR. The process is 'deliberate and time-intensive.'

timeline.label: Executive Order 14347 signed
timeline.text: 'Restoring the United States Department of War' authorises secondary designations while leaving statutory references to the Department of Defense controlling, and directs a recommendation on permanent renaming within 60 days.

timeline.label: NDAA amendment killed by staff
timeline.text: Burlison's UAP disclosure amendment to the NDAA is ruled non-germane overnight - 'mostly deemed by staff, not even an elected official.'

timeline.label: Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets holds its UAP whistleblower hearing
timeline.text: Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna convenes 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' in HVC-210 with witnesses Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and minority witness Spielberger. Rep. Crane submits a letter to the Secretary of Defense on the Grusch reprisal. Printed as Serial No. 119-44 (CHRG-119hhrg61718).

sources.name: CHRG-119hhrg61718, printed hearing transcript, 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection', Serial No. 119-44

timeline.label: House Oversight UAP transparency hearing
timeline.text: The House Oversight Committee holds 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection', with military witnesses and new whistleblower-protection legislation under discussion.

timeline.label: Operators testify: Wiggins, Nuccetelli, Borland, Knapp
timeline.text: The Task Force hearing seats an active-duty Navy senior chief describing a sensor-recorded encounter, two Air Force veterans, and a journalist. Wiggins: 'that is first and foremost a safety issue.'

timeline.label: Third House UAP hearing
timeline.text: The Task Force hears Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and Spielberger in HVC-210; Biggs, Begich, Ogles, Titus and Moskowitz are waived on.

timeline.label: Luna documents the read-in gate
timeline.text: Luna states that DoD told committee staff only HASC and HAC-D members could be read in on UAP special access programs, and that any other member needs approval from the chairman and ranking member of both.

timeline.label: First active-duty witness
timeline.text: Navy Senior Chief Alexandro Wiggins becomes the first currently serving military member to testify publicly to Congress on UAP, describing a 2023 USS Jackson encounter.

timeline.label: The Yemen Hellfire footage
timeline.text: Burlison publicly unveils footage recorded 30 October 2024 of an MQ-9 tracking an orb off Yemen while a second MQ-9 fires a Hellfire missile; the object appears struck and continues.

timeline.label: A decade of reprisal
timeline.text: Dylan Borland testifies that his career was 'deliberately obstructed' and that he has endured 'sustained reprisals from government agencies for more than a decade.'

timeline.label: 'We are definitely being lied to'
timeline.text: Moskowitz, waived onto the Task Force, says he does not know what is true on this subject but knows when the government is lying, and that it is.

timeline.label: Luna task force holds its first UAP hearing
timeline.text: 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' — the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets takes testimony from Nuccetelli, Borland, Wiggins, Knapp and POGO's Joe Spielberger.

timeline.label: Task Force hearing on UAP transparency and whistleblower protection
timeline.text: Crane enters the reprisal letter into the record; George Knapp tells the Task Force from the witness table that extra-legal reprisals against Grusch were occurring in recent days; Nancy Mace states his medical information was leaked to discredit him. Grusch attends but does not testify.

timeline.label: Lockheed Martin named on the record, with an executive
timeline.text: George Knapp testifies that Bigelow negotiated with senior Lockheed Martin executives for material held in California that 'was not made here'; tells Rep. Burchett that Lockheed is one of the holders and offers a list; and names Dr. James Ryder at Lockheed and Glenn Gaffney of CIA as gatekeepers.

timeline.label: The hinge hearing
timeline.text: Luna's Task Force hears Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland; the committee finds agencies withheld information and that UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach. Witnesses say AARO holds unreleased video.

timeline.label: House Task Force hearing on UAP transparency
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland testify. Wiggins is the first active-duty Navy official to do so publicly. Borland describes retaliation. Witnesses tell the Task Force AARO holds additional video records. Burlison presents drone-versus-orb footage from Yemen.

timeline.label: House Oversight Task Force hears five UAP witnesses
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp, Borland and Spielberger testify in HVC-210. Rep. Burlison plays previously unseen video of an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024; the object appears struck and not destroyed.

timeline.label: Luna states the read-in gate on the record
timeline.text: 'For a non-committee member to be allowed to view these documents and videos, individual members must be approved by the Chairman and Ranking Member of both HASC and HAC-D.' Mace adds: 'if you do not know it, you cannot get the information.'

timeline.label: The Task Force turns to the machinery
timeline.text: Nuccetelli, Wiggins, Knapp and Borland testify. The committee finds agencies withheld information and that UAP spending flows to entities outside FOIA reach. Nuccetelli names AARO and the FBI as custodians of Vandenberg records.

timeline.label: Oversight returns to whistleblower protection
timeline.text: The House Oversight Committee holds 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection', following the reintroduction of the UAP Whistleblower Protection Act as H.R. 5060 on 29 August 2025. The 2025-2026 phase of the fight is procedural rather than revelatory.

timeline.label: Herrera's written testimony entered into a hearing record by motion, sourced to Steven Greer
timeline.text: Rep. Eric Burlison moved into the record of the House Oversight Task Force hearing 'further witnesses of courageous individuals. It was given to me by Dr. Steven Greer, including Michael Herrera and his testimony', naming also Roderick Castle, Randy Anderson and Steven Digna. Chairwoman Luna: 'No objection.' He did not appear and was not sworn.
timeline.source: Serial CHRG-119hhrg61718, https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CHRG-119hhrg61718/html/CHRG-119hhrg61718.htm , 2025-09-09

timeline.label: Pentagon: no records of the Yankee Blue memo
timeline.text: OSD responds in FOIA case 25-F-3514 that no records of the alleged cessation memo could be identified; AFOSI reports no records of any related investigation.

timeline.label: Pentagon denies the YANKEE BLUE memo
timeline.text: After the Wall Street Journal reports an alleged Air Force practice of showing fabricated recovered-craft material to personnel, the Department denies any such memo exists - then reopens the search on 15 December 2025.

timeline.label: NARA transfer deadline for UAP records passes
timeline.text: NARA's guidance directed agencies holding releasable UAP records to initiate transfers before 30 September 2025. As of 28 August 2026 eight agencies appear in RG 615 - FAA, NRC, ODNI, OSD, NSA, State, FBI and the Department of the Air Force - and NARA has published no compliance list and no statement about agencies that did not transfer. Seven of the eight were in place by 22 May 2026; the Air Force arrived on 28 August 2026, eleven months after the deadline.

timeline.label: Pentagon spokesperson cannot confirm the memo
timeline.text: Susan Gough: 'Regarding the alleged memo: I cannot confirm the existence of any department-level memo as described in the article.'

timeline.label: Plates link nuclear tests to transients
timeline.text: Bruehl and Villarroel publish in Scientific Reports that POSS-I transients may be associated with above-ground nuclear testing and with contemporaneous UAP reports - physical-archive evidence for the programme's origin period, immune to classification.

timeline.label: Pre-Sputnik plates, nuclear correlation
timeline.text: Bruehl and Villarroel publish in Scientific Reports that transients in the Palomar Observatory Sky Survey may be associated with nuclear testing and with reports of unidentified anomalous phenomena. The data are photographic plates exposed between 1949 and 1957 and cannot have been contaminated by satellites.

timeline.label: 2025 Sol Foundation Symposium
timeline.text: Four days on Lake Maggiore in northern Italy with Karl Nell, Jacques Vallee, Garry Nolan, Jake Barber, Dylan Borland, Jeff Nuccetelli, Tim Gallaudet and Gen. Pierre Bescond. The movement internationalises.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes the Sandia investigation
timeline.text: The named-laboratory case for the AEC-custody thesis, citing Edgar Fouche on the TR-3B propulsion device and former New Mexico State Representative J. Andrew Kissner on materials held by AEC laboratories.

timeline.label: 3I/ATLAS: an anomalous object and a furloughed government
timeline.text: The US government fields questions about the third known interstellar object during a shutdown, with no standing scientific body chartered to answer.

timeline.label: 'The Age of Disclosure' released
timeline.text: Limited theatrical release in New York, Los Angeles and Washington DC, plus Prime Video.

timeline.label: Galileo variometer paper
timeline.text: Vervelidou, Little and colleagues publish the deployment of a geomagnetic variometer station as auxiliary UAP instrumentation in a Copernicus geophysics journal.

timeline.label: AARO releases PR-016, PR-017, PR-018
timeline.text: Five weeks after the hearing, AARO begins publishing official UAP imagery: short European infrared clips, one resolved as birds at >95% likelihood, one declared insufficient for a determination.

timeline.label: AARO releases PR-012, PR-014, PR-015
timeline.text: Three more infrared sensor videos of 2022 European incidents, 13 to 55 seconds each, all assessed as physical objects with unremarkable characteristics and left unresolved.

timeline.label: FY2026 NDAA UAP provisions
timeline.text: Congress directs AARO to brief on NORAD/NORTHCOM UAP intercepts back to 2004 and to account for its UAP security classification guides.

timeline.label: FY2026 NDAA carries three UAP provisions
timeline.text: The conferenced bill requires AARO to brief Congress on NORAD/NORTHCOM UAP intercepts since 2004 including data collected, to account for UAP-related security classification guides, and to streamline agency data-sharing.

timeline.label: No open amendment process
timeline.text: The FY2026 NDAA is moved with seventeen amendments in total; the only Senate floor amendment proposed is a leadership amendment by Senator Thune 'to improve the bill.' There is no process in which the UAPDA could be offered.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes the NRO investigation
timeline.text: Alleges the NRO's Sentient AI fed IMINT and SIGINT to Immaculate Constellation, established 2017; that the NRO ran a retrieval team out of the Nevada Test and Training Range; and that gatekeepers are identifiable through USD(A&S) and DDNI(AT&F).

timeline.label: FOIA appeal granted; search remanded
timeline.text: A Department of War FOIA appellate decision grants the appeal and remands for additional searches, finding a search limited to the Correspondence Management Division inadequate under Oglesby v. U.S. Dep't of Army.

timeline.label: FY2026 NDAA orders a NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept accounting back to 2004
timeline.text: Public Law 119-60 is approved. Sec. 1671 requires every AARO briefing to detail UAP intercepts flown by NORAD or USNORTHCOM and requires the first such briefing to reach back to 1 January 2004 for intercepts 'not previously provided'. Sec. 1672 repeals 50 U.S.C. 3373a and adds a sources-and-methods qualifier to the immediate-data-availability mandate. Sec. 1673 orders an accounting of the security classification guides governing UAP information and authorises a consolidated UAP classification matrix.

sources.name: Public Law 119-60, National Defense Authorization Act for FY2026 (full text, GPO)

timeline.label: FY2026 enacted; funding bar lapses again
timeline.text: P.L. 119-60 carries a three-section housekeeping subtitle: intercept briefings back to 2004, repeal of a duplicative report, and an accounting of classification guides. No Review Board, no eminent domain, and for the second consecutive year no funding bar on undisclosed UAP special access programmes.

timeline.label: FY2026 NDAA: classified annex given statutory force; UAP reporting trimmed
timeline.text: Public Law 119-60 is approved. Section 4001(d) applies the funding-table authorisation to 'any classified annex that accompanies this Act'; section 6102 provides that intelligence amounts 'are those specified in the classified Schedule of Authorizations' which the President 'shall not publicly disclose'. Section 1672 repeals 50 U.S.C. 3373a; section 1673 orders AARO to inventory the security classification guides covering UAP within 180 days.

timeline.label: Restricted-airspace sightings up 26 percent
timeline.text: Drone sightings in restricted airspace rose 26 percent during 2025.

timeline.label: ORNL aluminium specimen analysis
timeline.text: AARO publishes the Oak Ridge analysis of an aluminium specimen with a January 2026 supplement, its second and last published materials characterisation.

timeline.label: Sol Briefing No. 1
timeline.text: The Sol Foundation publishes 'Robust Evidence of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena in Pre-Satellite Era Night-Sky Images', translating the VASCO plate results into a policy artefact.

timeline.label: Oak Ridge returns a conventional result
timeline.text: AARO publishes its Aluminum Materials Analysis Supplement, reporting that Oak Ridge National Laboratory found a specimen recovered near Flint Ridge, Ohio to match conventional aluminium-silicon casting alloys, with casting defects and no radioactive emissions. The materials domain's most recent test returned negative, and the board records that.

timeline.label: AARO releases PR-011 and PR-013
timeline.text: The office's last imagery release before PURSUE: two more European infrared clips from 2021 and 2022, both unresolved, analysis ongoing.

timeline.label: The structural episode
timeline.text: Michels and Gerb publish the three-hour reconstruction of how the effort is organised - the contractor pyramid, the modern control group, the Office of Global Access, MITRE, the DOE NEST, the 1954 Atomic Energy Agreement; 514,729 views.

timeline.label: Pax River storage claim surfaces
timeline.text: Liberation Times reports that an exotic vehicle of unknown origin has been stored for decades at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, with contingency relocation plans, and that Elizondo's written congressional testimony placed the base among sites prepared for the blocked Lockheed-Bigelow transfer.

timeline.label: Varginha witnesses brief three members of Congress
timeline.text: In Rep. Tim Burchett's office, neurosurgeon Ítalo Venturelli, forensic pathologist Armando Fortunato and ultralight pilot Carlos de Sousa brief Burchett, Anna Paulina Luna and Eric Burlison. Five days later a National Press Club conference follows, at which retired USAF Colonel Fred Claussen sets out the Air Mobility Command paperwork trail any American retrieval flight would have generated and appeals to participants to come forward.

timeline.label: DODIG-2026-045 issued
timeline.text: The DoD Inspector General evaluates ten installations with drone incursions and 31 DoD components, finding inconsistent policies, unclear 'covered facility' designations and approval processes that delayed counter-drone deployment.

timeline.label: Base commanders' authorities expanded
timeline.text: Updated guidance removes the fence-line limitation, defines unauthorized surveillance as an explicit threat and grants commanders 'totality of circumstances' discretion.

timeline.label: Gerb maps the Air Force
timeline.text: 'The Hidden Wing' names SAF/AQ, SAF/AQL Special Programs, SAF/AA, SAF/AAH, SAF/AZ, AF/TE and AFOSI/PJ, and proposes Russell Wyler and William Maclure as the referents of Christopher Mellon's unnamed Air Force SES-2 gatekeeper.

timeline.label: AARO's workshop white paper recommends metadata standards
timeline.text: Standardised metadata templates, AI with human oversight and open narrative reporting - published three months before a release programme that adopted none of them.

timeline.label: Coulthart endorses Gerb on air
timeline.text: NewsNation publishes 'Ross Coulthart on UAP Gerb's claims: I think he's on the money' - a network correspondent vouching for a pseudonymous YouTube researcher's structural model.

timeline.label: FY2026 Defense Appropriations Act enacted
timeline.text: Public Law 119-75 is approved. Section 8005 carries $6 billion of transfer authority; section 8006(a) gives the classified annex tables the force of statutory text; section 8006(b) exempts annex line items from the transfer ceiling; section 8009 requires 30 days notice before initiating or materially modifying a special access program; section 8084(b) makes 'the levels specified in the classified annex' the baseline for NIP reprogramming.

timeline.label: Trump directs UAP records release
timeline.text: A presidential directive instructs the Secretary of War and other agencies to identify and release government files connected to UAP and extraterrestrial life, creating PURSUE.

timeline.label: PURSUE runs parallel to statutory reporting
timeline.text: The Department of War states it will continue separate reporting on resolved UAP cases as mandated by statute. The historical-records release and the contemporary programme reporting line remain distinct - a structure permitting maximal apparent transparency about the past while present reporting is unchanged.

timeline.label: The President orders a release
timeline.text: Trump posts on Truth Social that he will direct Hegseth and relevant departments to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs.

timeline.label: Presidential direction to release UAP files
timeline.text: President Trump states he will direct the Secretary of War to begin identifying and releasing government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life and related UAP matters.

timeline.label: Trump directs release of UAP files by Truth Social post
timeline.text: The originating instrument of PURSUE: a social-media direction to Secretary of War Hegseth and other departments to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. No signed executive order has surfaced.

timeline.label: Trump orders a file release
timeline.text: The President pledges to direct Hegseth and relevant agencies to begin identifying and releasing government files on UAP and extraterrestrial life; PURSUE follows.

timeline.label: President directs identification and release of UAP files
timeline.text: Trump announces he will direct the Secretary of War and other departments and agencies to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. No deadline is specified. Luna, as Task Force chair, publicly thanks him.

timeline.label: The department acknowledges the directive
timeline.text: Parnell says the department looks forward to working with the interagency to fulfil the directive. Mellon: 'This might be a consequential moment, but the impact will depend on the follow-through.'

timeline.label: The research community's first asks
timeline.text: Mellon: the impact depends on the follow-through. Gallaudet: 'I'll believe it when I see it.' Loeb: 'One step that can be taken immediately is to declassify events from 50 years ago.' Parnell: the department looks forward to working with the interagency.

timeline.label: Presidential directive to release UAP files
timeline.text: The President directs the Pentagon and federal agencies to identify and release files on UAP and extraterrestrial matters - a directive that operates on executive-order classification and therefore cannot reach Restricted Data held by DOE.

timeline.label: Hegseth commits the Department: 'full compliance with that executive order'
timeline.text: At an Arsenal of Freedom stop in Louisville, Colorado, the Secretary of War describes a deliberative process and declines a timeline. Sue Gough confirms AARO's caseload has passed 2,000, with about 1,000 reports in an Active Archive for insufficient data.

timeline.label: 2,000 cases, half unanalysed
timeline.text: Hegseth commits to full compliance while declining a schedule. Spokesperson Sue Gough discloses AARO is examining over 2,000 cases, roughly 1,000 of which lack sufficient data and sit in an Active Archive.

timeline.label: AARO says it is transferring records to NARA
timeline.text: A Department of War news story records that AARO is coordinating with the White House and across agencies to consolidate UAP record collections and has made progress transferring records to the National Archives.

timeline.label: The Department of War publicly takes the file
timeline.text: Hegseth: 'We've got our people working on it right now... We're going to be in full compliance with [the president's request].' Asked about extraterrestrial life: 'We'll see. I get to do the review and find out along with you.' Press Secretary Kingsley Wilson says AARO is coordinating with the White House and across agencies to consolidate existing records.

timeline.label: Luna recommends defunding AARO
timeline.text: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna recommends the office's complete defunding to the DOGE subcommittee, citing systematic obstruction.

timeline.label: Michels puts Eric Davis on record with Eric Weinstein
timeline.text: A four-hour session working through the Wilson-Davis memo, the count of crashes, crash-retrieval program structure and the legacy program; 766,314 views.

timeline.label: Barksdale raises FPCON Charlie
timeline.text: A B-52 base issues a shelter-in-place order after drone reports over the installation; waves of 12-15 jam-resistant drones are later reported over the flight line, following the launch of Operation Epic Fury.

timeline.label: White House registers alien.gov and aliens.gov
timeline.text: Neither domain is connected to a site. Anna Kelly: 'Stay tuned!' The release programme ships seven weeks later on war.gov/UFO instead.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes the Northrop/TRW breakaway analysis
timeline.text: Alleges Northrop used IRAD funds after 9/11 to self-fund its own retrieval and exploitation programs, unaccountable to its government handler; traces Stephanie O'Sullivan from TRW to Principal Deputy DNI to the Aerospace Corporation board.

timeline.label: Luna demands 46 UAP video files from the Department of War
timeline.text: Chairwoman Anna Paulina Luna writes to Secretary Pete Hegseth demanding 46 UAP video files with an April 14 deadline, finding AARO's responses 'less than adequate'. The FLIR1/Gimbal/GoFast release chain of 2017-2020 is the precedent she is invoking.

timeline.label: Luna demands 46 UAP videos from the Secretary of War
timeline.text: The letter sets a 14 April 2026 deadline. It passes with the Department stating it will respond directly to the author and a congressional source offering a future briefing; Luna says the letter was not passed to the appropriate authorities.

timeline.label: GEIPAN's forty-ninth-year figures
timeline.text: GEIPAN reports more than 9,897 testimonies representing about 5,170 observation cases in 49 years, with 3,336 published; 66.5 per cent classed A or B, 30.3 per cent class C for lack of data, and 3.2 per cent class D - unexplained after investigation.

timeline.label: Sol Foundation publishes peer-reviewed analysis of possible UAP material
timeline.text: Science and Policy Briefing No. 3 by Marik von Rennenkampff reports atomic and isotopic analysis of physical material associated with a multi-witness event, conducted by Garry Nolan - the private-sector counterpart to AARO's two Oak Ridge specimen studies.

timeline.label: Terry K. Patton becomes FASAB chairman
timeline.text: Patton, professor emeritus at Midwestern State University, takes the chair of the body that owns SFFAS 56 and alone can withdraw it or issue the Interpretations under paragraph 8(c) authorising further unspecified modifications to public financial reports.

timeline.label: Luna demands AARO's video files
timeline.text: Chairwoman Luna writes Secretary Hegseth for UAP video files that whistleblowers told the Task Force AARO holds.

timeline.label: Luna writes to Hegseth
timeline.text: The Task Force chair demands AARO's UAP video holdings, citing the September 2025 testimony that the office holds additional video records.

timeline.label: Sol Briefing No. 3
timeline.text: Marik von Rennenkampff's briefing sets out the full evidentiary architecture of the Council Bluffs analysis and the physical reason for each excluded hypothesis. Kirk McConnell's Briefing No. 2, proposing a UAP whistleblower restitution fund, appears the same month.

timeline.label: Luna letters Hegseth for AARO's videos
timeline.text: The Task Force chair writes to the Secretary of War demanding UAP video files held by AARO, following September 2025 testimony that the office holds additional records.

timeline.label: Bill introduced to abolish AARO
timeline.text: Rep. Tim Burchett introduces H.R. 8197: abolish the office, bar any successor, redistribute functions to the military departments, repeal the enabling statutes. Referred to HASC and HPSCI.

timeline.label: Nick Pope dies
timeline.text: The only person to have run Britain's MoD UFO desk and then spent thirty years describing it dies at home aged 60, two months after disclosing a stage 4 oesophageal cancer diagnosis and writing of 'the secrets I've been privy to'. Obituaries follow in The Telegraph, The Times, The Economist and The New York Times.

timeline.label: Lacatski: 'the world's largest UFO data warehouse'
timeline.text: In conversation with Jeremy Corbell, Lacatski says AAWSAP produced more than 100 detailed reports, doubts the files will ever be released, and hints a smaller KONA BLUE-related effort continued after AAWSAP ended.

timeline.label: Deadline missed; subpoena raised
timeline.text: The Pentagon misses Luna's video deadline. She publicly raises a subpoena. None has issued.

timeline.label: The UFO General vanishes; Oversight opens a probe
timeline.text: Comer and Burlison open an investigation into eleven deaths and disappearances of people in nuclear and rocket work since 2022, triggered by the February 2026 disappearance of retired Maj. Gen. William Neil McCasland, former AFRL commander at Wright-Patterson. Burlison's staff had been trying to reach him about a separate congressional investigation.

timeline.label: 'Sleeping Dog' LANL document trove reported
timeline.text: Jeremy Corbell states he received a trove of documents from the son of a deceased former Los Alamos cybersecurity chief, including material said to concern a secret 1991 meeting at the laboratory.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes 'Manhattan Project 2.0' Vol.1
timeline.text: The origin argument: a 1947 centralized effort borrowing the Manhattan Project's secrecy wholesale, AEC custody, the NSC 5412 Committee, the Atomic Energy Act of 1954, Vannevar Bush and George C. Marshall's Alsos Missions and T-Force.

timeline.label: Judicial Watch On Watch interview
timeline.text: Grusch restates to Chris Farrell that elements of the US government thwarted congressional oversight, withheld information from proper executive branch officials, and illegally concealed recovery and reverse-engineering programs.

timeline.label: PURSUE launches
timeline.text: The Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters publishes its first tranche under a directive from President Trump, implemented by the Department of War with ODNI, FBI, State, NASA and AARO.

timeline.label: First PURSUE drop
timeline.text: About 160 declassified files are released through a war.gov portal, at least 100 redacted. Mellon: 'Data alone is not disclosure.'

timeline.label: Department of War releases UAP files
timeline.text: The administration announces a release of UAP files. Gillibrand, author of the surviving statute, calls it 'another important step' and says she will fight to ensure the administration 'finally meets its legal obligation' — nineteen months after the deadline.

timeline.label: Burlison writes to MIT Lincoln Laboratory
timeline.text: Burlison asks Lincoln Laboratory to locate and preserve reel-to-reel recording AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52 - naming the file by its exact designation - and to coordinate with NARA on archival review.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 01
timeline.text: The Department of War publishes the first tranche of declassified UAP records. The Sol Foundation issues a press statement the following day.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 01 posted at war.gov/UFO
timeline.text: The first PURSUE tranche: a 1.2GB document bundle and a 1.3GB video bundle, 160 files spanning 1944 to 2026, published at war.gov/UFO with no manifest, no metadata and no assessment.

timeline.label: Department of War publishes the first PURSUE tranche
timeline.text: The war.gov/UFO portal opens with the first release of UAP files. Senator Gillibrand issues a statement the same day.

timeline.label: The US release reaches the allies
timeline.text: More than 160 UAP files are published on the US Department of Defense website. Within days Kyodo News reports that the footage shows a football-shaped object near Japan, The Japan Times reports Tokyo analysing the trove, and the Buenos Aires Times reports that the release documents the 31 July 1995 Aerolíneas Argentinas Bariloche encounter in a section on investigations conducted outside the United States - citing the 1999 French COMETA report as a source.

timeline.label: The Black Vault publishes a searchable mirror of Release 01
timeline.text: Three days after the first tranche, John Greenewald strips password protection from the released PDFs, runs OCR, generates transcripts and subtitles and adds agency categorisation - supplying the index the government did not.

timeline.label: Eighth consecutive disclaimer; $859 billion unsupported in two quarters
timeline.text: DOWIG-2026-081, 'The FY 2025 DoW Financial Statement Audit Explained', records a disclaimer of opinion for the eighth consecutive year, twenty-six material weaknesses including 'Unsupported Accounting Adjustments', 'Universe of Transactions' and 'Fund Balance with Treasury', and states that in the last two quarters of FY2025 the Department's adjustments exceeded $859 billion.

timeline.label: SCU finds PURSUE Release #1 deficient
timeline.text: The Scientific Coalition for UAP Studies reports that critical metadata was stripped, roughly 70 percent of the FBI files already existed in the FOIA Vault, 1974-2015 is missing, and DOE, DIA, NRO, NSA and CIA contributed nothing.

timeline.label: Deputy IG testifies to House Oversight on the $859 billion
timeline.text: Brett A. Mansfield tells the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform that unsupported adjustments exceeded $859 billion in two quarters, that the Department manages more than $4.7 trillion in assets, and that reporting entities will consolidate from twenty-two to seven in FY2027 with an independent public accounting firm taking the group auditor role. It is the same committee that heard David Grusch in July 2023.

timeline.label: Japan confirms it holds UAP footage
timeline.text: Following its review of the US release, coverage reports that the Japanese government has confirmed possession of UAP footage taken near Japanese airspace and that Japan will release files of its own. Japan has no standing UAP office of the GEIPAN or SEFAA kind.

timeline.label: 'Data alone is not disclosure'
timeline.text: Mellon concedes the scale of the holdings is itself a revelation and rejects context-free files; Gallaudet and Rojas identify the missing metadata; a War Department official confirms the Department will offer no assessment on any file.

timeline.label: DefenseScoop reports the programme's name: PURSUE
timeline.text: DefenseScoop publishes the acronym - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters - and the research community's reaction. Christopher Mellon: 'Data alone is not disclosure.' Ryan Graves: 'Ambiguous imagery without that surrounding data is hard for pilots, researchers, or the public to evaluate responsibly.'

timeline.label: An FFRDC blinks
timeline.text: Burlison announces MIT Lincoln Laboratory's attorneys have agreed to comply within 30 days with his demand for a classified 1952 'flying saucer talk' recording. 'Congressional letters carry weight. We're going to keep sending them.'

timeline.label: Kosloski apologises to members
timeline.text: Luna and Burlison review the second tranche with Kosloski. Luna then backs him publicly, saying he apologised for the prior leadership's conduct and that the earlier office was intentionally set up to block, stonewall and suppress information.

timeline.label: Samantha Ravich elected to MITRE's board
timeline.text: A former vice chair of the President's Intelligence Advisory Board joins MITRE's trustees three days before the congressional UAP records demand arrives.

timeline.label: Lake Huron shootdown video released
timeline.text: Infrared footage of the 12 February 2023 engagement is published through PURSUE, with the entry noting a lack of substantiated chain of custody.

timeline.label: The MITRE demand
timeline.text: Burlison sends MITRE a ten-page letter with 40+ production requests covering UAP, anomalous materials and reverse engineering back to 1930, due in 45 days in native format with metadata.

timeline.label: Burlison's 10-page production request to MITRE
timeline.text: The first congressional records demand ever addressed to an FFRDC operator on UAP: more than 40 requests covering crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering programmes, Special and Controlled Access Programs, sensor data and materials analysis back to 1930.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 02
timeline.text: 64 files including 51 sensor videos and ODNI-UAP-D001, a serving senior intelligence officer's first-person account of a one-hour multi-witness encounter from a military helicopter in late 2025.

timeline.label: Burlison demands MITRE's UAP records back to 1930
timeline.text: A ten-page letter with over 40 production requests, a 45-day deadline, native electronic format with complete metadata, naming eleven other contractors in scope. MITRE says it will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 02: 51 sensor videos and ODNI-UAP-D001
timeline.text: A 5.6GB video bundle, the largest of the five, plus the first-person narrative of a serving senior intelligence officer describing a one-hour multi-witness encounter from a military helicopter in late 2025.

timeline.label: MITRE routes the answer to its sponsors
timeline.text: A MITRE spokesperson confirms archives are being reviewed and states that 'if any relevant material is found, we will coordinate with the federal agencies responsible for the work' - the FFRDC disclosure structure asserting itself against a congressional demand.

timeline.label: The Senate's FY2027 base text contains no UAP provisions
timeline.text: S. 4784 as reported (S. Rept. 119-127) returns zero occurrences of 'unidentified', 'UAP' or 'Anomaly Resolution'. The House-adopted disclosure framework must survive conference against a chamber that did not legislate on the subject at all.

timeline.label: Grusch returns to the Capitol
timeline.text: Lawmakers and whistleblowers gather at the Capitol; Luna asks the White House for whistleblower immunity, Burlison asks the President to waive all NDAs, and Grusch says political appointees have not complied with the disclosure law.

timeline.label: Grusch joins Task Force members on UAP declassification
timeline.text: David Grusch appears with bipartisan members of the House Oversight Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, arguing agencies continue to resist congressional efforts and that spending has been hidden.

timeline.label: Capitol press conference: slush funds and several kinds of NHI
timeline.text: Grusch alleges slush funds of billions of dollars per annum, calls it a fraud, waste and abuse issue, accuses DIA of withholding documents, and says the government is aware of several kinds of non-human intelligence. Luna, Burchett, Burlison and Moskowitz appear with him.

timeline.label: Grusch speaks on the Capitol steps at a Luna press conference
timeline.text: David Grusch tells reporters the government is aware of 'several' kinds of alien life, describing 'a continuum from corporeal bipedal type life to what I would consider as sentient plasmoid life,' and references four different species. It is his most specific public claim about biology.

timeline.label: Special Report No. 14 republished in PURSUE Release 03
timeline.text: The Department of War publishes the 1955 Battelle report again as CIA-UAP-015 - the third government publication of the same document in seventy years, with the underlying case data still never independently reanalysed.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 03
timeline.text: 72 files with the FBI the largest contributor at 29, including a 2021-2025 orb corpus, an FD-1057 by two FBI special agents, and a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel report.

timeline.label: Government disclosure release
timeline.text: Loeb's own account of the council's formation references a government disclosure release date of 12 June 2026, immediately preceding his tasking.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 03: 72 files, FBI the largest contributor
timeline.text: 53 documents, 10 images, 6 videos, 3 audio files; 29 FBI files including agents' own first-hand orb observations; a less-redacted CIA Robertson Panel report; documents 826MB, video 4.6GB.

timeline.label: Third PURSUE tranche
timeline.text: Cases include a 2008 disc over Harare International Airport, a 2024 Colorado Springs object assessed with low confidence, and a 2025-2026 northeastern orb assessed as sky lanterns.

timeline.label: FY2027 NDAA reported with no UAP provisions
timeline.text: S. 4784, Report No. 119-127, is reported by the Armed Services Committee containing zero occurrences of 'unidentified', 'UAP' or a citation to 50 U.S.C. 3373. Second consecutive cycle in which the subject is absent from the Senate base text.

timeline.label: Interagency UAP Governance Board convenes
timeline.text: ODNI, with the FBI and the Department of War, stands up a UAP Governance Board to coordinate investigation and declassification in support of AARO, with outside science advisory groups attached. No published charter provision addresses contractor holdings.

timeline.label: UAP Science Advisory Council announced
timeline.text: A council formed at the request of the White House in coordination with AARO, ODNI, the FBI and other agencies is announced, chaired by Avi Loeb and drawn overwhelmingly from the private technical layer - with no budget and no classified access.

timeline.label: Rounds's markup wins contain no UAP item
timeline.text: Rounds announces roughly forty provisions he secured in the FY2027 committee markup. None concerns unidentified anomalous phenomena.

timeline.label: DoW OIG withholds its UAP evaluation methodology under (b)(1)
timeline.text: Fourth interim release in DODIG-2021-000806: the 'Potential Benefits' section withheld on national-security grounds, background sections marked (S//NF) blacked out, methodology steps 3-8 redacted, October 2020 UAP Task Force leadership meeting withheld as deliberative. Approximately 245 pages still pending.

timeline.label: UAP Science Advisory Council formed
timeline.text: ODNI, AARO and the White House ask Avi Loeb to assemble a 14-member scientific council to advise on resolving the nature of UAP and support a new interagency UAP Governance Board. Tim Gallaudet, who testified alongside Elizondo in 2024, is a member.

timeline.label: UAP Science Advisory Council announced
timeline.text: A science advisory council is announced between the third and fourth tranches; no charter, roster or product has appeared on AARO's or the Department's pages as of August 2026.

timeline.label: UAP Science Advisory Council announced under Avi Loeb
timeline.text: Avi Loeb announces a twelve-plus-member scientific advisory council reporting to the UAP Governance Board, five weeks into a release programme that assesses nothing it publishes.

timeline.label: The council's ceiling is set on day one
timeline.text: All data shared with the UAP Science Advisory Council will be unclassified - a scientific advisory body without access to the classified holdings whose existence is the entire question.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes 'Special Access Required' Vol.2
timeline.text: The legal-mechanism argument: the 1994 SAP restructuring, and the claim that the portfolio hides in 'Non-Covert Action Programs' with managed need-to-know access and completely waived reporting and budgetary requirements.

timeline.label: Sol leadership named to the ODNI UAP Science Advisory Council
timeline.text: ODNI, with FBI support, establishes a council led by Avi Loeb reporting to an interagency UAP Governance Board. Garry Nolan, Peter Skafish, Tim Gallaudet, Jacob Haqq-Misra and Ross Howard are named. All data shared with the council will be unclassified.

timeline.label: The council will see only unclassified data
timeline.text: ODNI's UAP Science Advisory Council is announced with the explicit condition that all data shared with it will be unclassified. The movement's most credentialed figures are given a formal seat, a reporting line to an interagency governance board, and a guarantee that they will never be shown classified material.

timeline.label: Sol Foundation confirms its co-founders sit on the federal advisory council
timeline.text: Nolan and Skafish are named to the UAP Science Advisory Council, which the foundation says was announced by ODNI with FBI support and reports to an interagency UAP Governance Board. All data shared with the council will be unclassified.

timeline.label: Disclosure Forum 2026
timeline.text: Burlison announces at the first Disclosure Forum that MIT Lincoln Laboratory has agreed to make the 1952 Washington sightings recording available.

timeline.label: Rounds announces a fourth attempt
timeline.text: At the 2026 Disclosure Symposium Rounds says he is 'once again cosponsoring' the UAP Disclosure Act as an amendment to this year's NDAA — nine days after the committee reported a bill with nothing in it to amend.

timeline.label: Lincoln Laboratory agrees to release the 1952 recording
timeline.text: Burlison announces the laboratory will disclose AF-ATIC-FILM, 03/52 - the first FFRDC-held UAP record produced to Congress. His method: 'We told MIT Lincoln Labs we know the exact video file you are holding, by name, and we want it.'

timeline.label: The publishing party cold-calls the second Ellsworth witness
timeline.text: Dated on air: on 26 June 2026 the producer telephoned a Michael Johnson in South Carolina, located from a viewer's Facebook tip by an unnamed recruiter, and withheld the frame, saying nothing about November-5 and nothing about a UFO. Mario Woods was then patched in and within two minutes supplied the site, the date and, after Johnson first answered 'No', the category. NO DATED PUBLIC STATEMENT BY JOHNSON ABOUT THE EVENT EXISTS BEFORE THIS CALL.
timeline.source: Jesse Michels, video rjUdn6FklAU, at 00:03:06-00:03:45, 00:05:19-00:05:46 and 00:07:29-00:07:46, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rjUdn6FklAU

timeline.label: Loeb publishes the tasking
timeline.text: Loeb writes on Medium that he was 'tasked by' the White House, AARO, ODNI, the FBI and all Intelligence Community members to create a research team, naming Cloete, Sarmiento, Szydagis, Nandal and Eldadi.

timeline.label: No budget, no clearances
timeline.text: The Associated Press reports that the council will have no budget and no access to classified material - an advisory body constituted to advise on the part of the record nobody disputes.

timeline.label: Task Force holds MKULTRA hearing
timeline.text: 'Mind Control and Accountability: Uncovering the Truth of the CIA's MKULTRA Project' - the same declassification task force that carries the UAP file turns to CIA behavioural programmes, establishing that its remit is agency secrecy generally.

timeline.label: The Task Force's 2026 hearing is about MKULTRA
timeline.text: Kinzer and O'Neill testify on the CIA programme whose records a Director of Central Intelligence ordered destroyed. No UAP witness appears in 2026.

timeline.label: An artifact-search advocate inside the tent
timeline.text: Avi Loeb publishes his account of agreeing to lead a UAP Science Advisory Council for the US government, after the Disclosure Foundation announced on 14 June 2026 that he had been asked to assemble and chair a twelve-member multidisciplinary council. It is a directive-layer creation rather than a statutory one, and can be unmade the same way.

timeline.label: MITRE's 45-day production deadline falls
timeline.text: No public production has been reported as of 12 August 2026 in response to Burlison's 22 May demand for records back to 1930.

timeline.label: Burlison demands CIA and FBI records on Varginha 1996
timeline.text: The congressional records demand crosses a border for the first time, aimed at the two agencies whose positions on the UAP record are most conspicuous.

timeline.label: 1949 Los Alamos green fireballs records publicised
timeline.text: Newly declassified records on the February 1949 conference reach mainstream reporting, confirming through federal release what LANL had already published on its own site in 2024.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 04
timeline.text: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video spanning the 1940s to 2026, published without a stated file count, and with assessment language reappearing: balloons and sensor artefacts, no clear evidence of unknown aircraft.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 04: no file count published
timeline.text: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video, content dating to the 1940s. The Department publishes no file count - by the fourth tranche the release programme had stopped stating what it was releasing.

timeline.label: Congress asks the FBI and CIA about Varginha
timeline.text: NewsNation reports that a lawmaker - contemporaneous coverage names Rep. Eric Burlison - has asked the FBI and the CIA for information on the Varginha case, six months after the Brazilian witnesses testified on Capitol Hill.

timeline.event: FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report posted under Department of War branding - 319 reports; Section G states no USG or private entity has ever captured or exploited UAP-derived materials

timeline.label: AARO FY2025 report, nine months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 1,870 total cases, 370 resolved, 191 to active archive, 9 meriting further analysis; 'AARO did not receive reports indicating flight safety concerns,' yet two cases describe avionic interference near an operational aircraft.

timeline.label: Presidential directive waives UAP-related NDAs
timeline.text: Agencies are directed to waive nondisclosure agreements for former employees and contractors speaking to cleared AARO or PURSUE officials. Officials stress it is not a declassification directive. Burlison recommends anyone using it bring counsel and request congressional presence.

timeline.label: AARO again denies possession while writing custody procedures
timeline.text: The FY2025 annual report, released months after the statutory cycle, rejects claims that the US government possesses recovered UAP material and states the office is developing procedures for handling such material should any ever come into US government possession.

timeline.label: AARO FY2025 annual report, months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 1,870 total holdings, 370 resolved, one Navy report of approximately 100 airborne UAP off Virginia under investigation - and no mention anywhere of PURSUE.

timeline.label: NDAs waived - to investigators only
timeline.text: The administration directs DoW and the IC to waive UAP-related NDAs for former employees and contractors speaking with authorised investigators. Officials stress it is 'not a declassification directive.'

timeline.label: FY2025 annual report, months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 370 resolutions, 9 flagged, holdings at 1,870. Fifty UAS notifications near nuclear infrastructure, up from 18. And roughly 100 airborne UAP with two likely uncrewed surface systems off Virginia, unresolved.

timeline.label: Navy reports ~100 UAP and two uncrewed surface systems off Virginia
timeline.text: Disclosed the same day AARO's FY2025 annual report appeared; the sole maritime case in that report; no case number, date, hull or unit made public.

timeline.label: AARO publishes the FY2025 annual report, months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 370 resolutions all to conventional causes, 50 UAS notifications near nuclear infrastructure against 18 the year before, and 255 of 262 secure-channel submissions assessed out of scope.

timeline.label: House adopts the UAP Disclosure Act as an FY2027 NDAA amendment
timeline.text: A permanent National Archives collection, a Senate-confirmed Records Review Board with subpoena power, statutory transfer timelines, and disclosure obligations extended to covered government contractors. First time such a framework has cleared a chamber.

timeline.label: House adopts the Burlison UAP records amendment
timeline.text: Attached to the FY2027 NDAA, it would require transfer of UAP records to NARA on a statutory timeline, create a Senate-confirmed Review Board with subpoena power, and extend disclosure duties to certain contractors holding covered records.

timeline.label: House adopts the Burlison disclosure amendment
timeline.text: The FY2027 NDAA amendment would impose statutory transfer timelines, create a Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena power, and extend disclosure obligations to government contractors.

timeline.label: The House votes a records framework
timeline.text: The House approves an amendment offered by Rep. Eric Burlison creating a framework for UAP records disclosure - the records domain remaining the only front on which the disclosure movement reliably moves legislation.

timeline.label: Burlison offers a congressional channel
timeline.text: Burlison says he had been calling for the NDA waiver, offers his office as a channel, and recommends anyone participating request congressional presence alongside legal counsel.

timeline.label: Burlison publicises the Presidential UAP NDA-waiver directive
timeline.text: He offers his office's assistance to witnesses, warns that it is unclear whether the abrogation covers testimony given to Congress before referral to the executive branch, and recommends witnesses bring both an attorney and a member of Congress.

timeline.label: ODNI memorandum ES 2026-00818 published: PURSUE is a Task Force
timeline.text: Aaron Lukas, Principal Deputy DNI, directs release of all IC UAP information to the PURSUE Task Force for review and declassification, waives NDAs, agreements, oaths and commitments for those speaking to AARO or PURSUE, and requires every IC element to name a PURSUE designee within 30 days.

timeline.label: Coulthart and Gerb on Kona Blue
timeline.text: Reality Check devotes a full episode to the alleged Lockheed-to-DHS transfer, the Immaculate Constellation document, FFRDCs/UARCs/GOCOs, gatekeeping, alleged directed-energy attacks on whistleblowers and alleged EMP downings of civilian aircraft; 176,430 views.

timeline.label: UAP Gerb publishes the MITRE investigation
timeline.text: A two-hour open-source investigation places an FFRDC rather than a prime contractor at the centre of the legacy programme thesis, alleging a Navy reverse-engineering role since 1958 and MITRE processing of data on a large Atlantic USO.

timeline.label: Gerb publishes the MITRE investigation
timeline.text: The FFRDC arbitration thesis in full: MITRE as the missing link, two alleged Navy-spearheaded programs, an Atlantic USO tracking mission, and a 2011 restriction on historical briefings about program incumbents.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 05
timeline.text: The fifth tranche of declassified UAP records is published the same day as Gerb's MITRE investigation.

timeline.label: The Navy's 1953 finding surfaces
timeline.text: A Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis assessing the Tremonton objects as self-luminous and intelligently controlled, inconsistent with known aerospace technologies, is published for the first time in seventy-three years.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 05: the Gulf of Oman gunship engagement
timeline.text: 41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - including six AC-130J videos and DOW-UAP-D101 on the 8 September 2021 Gulf of Oman encounter, and the 1953 Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis of the Great Falls and Tremonton films.

timeline.label: EOP-UAP-D001: the Executive Office of the President becomes an originator
timeline.text: Release 05 carries a November 1963 Brazil incident report prefixed EOP, alongside DOS-UAP-D002, a State Department cable on the same events - the release programme reaching into White House holdings.

timeline.label: Parnell: additional files 'on a rolling basis'
timeline.text: The Department's only statement of forward intent: the material continues to be housed on WAR.GOV/UFO and more will follow. No schedule, no scope, no manifest.

timeline.label: State of play
timeline.text: MITRE's 45-day unclassified production deadline has passed with no public production; no letter has been made public to RAND, Aerospace, IDA or Sandia; the FY2027 NDAA contractor-records provision awaits the Senate.

timeline.label: AARO Volume II still unpublished
timeline.text: As of August 2026, more than two years after Volume I promised further findings, the second volume of AARO's historical record report has not been released.

timeline.label: Volume II still unpublished
timeline.text: As of 12 August 2026 Historical Record Report Volume II has not appeared - after the FY2025 annual report, after five PURSUE tranches, and over two years after it was promised.

timeline.label: Historical Record Report Volume II remains unpublished
timeline.text: Promised within months in November 2024, said in June 2025 to carry the Yankee Blue findings and scheduled for late 2025, and absent from AARO's Congressional and Press Products page on 12 August 2026 - after five PURSUE tranches and an IC-wide NDA waiver.

timeline.label: Five agencies ordered to release UAP information have no series in the statutory archive
timeline.text: CIA, DIA, NRO, NGA and DOE are addressees of ODNI ES 2026-00818 and absentees from Record Group 615. NARA publishes no compliance list and no statement identifying non-compliant agencies.

timeline.label: Eleven months, no UAP hearing
timeline.text: Between 9 September 2025 and 12 August 2026 - covering the February 2026 release directive, five PURSUE tranches, the late FY2025 annual report, the NDA waiver and the Burlison amendment - Congress holds no hearing on UAP.

timeline.label: Twenty-one months of silence on Immaculate Constellation
timeline.text: No AARO annual report, statement for the record or PURSUE tranche has addressed a programme name entered into the Congressional Record on 13 November 2024. The Department's position remains 'no record'.

timeline.label: State of the record, August 2026
timeline.text: The retrieval literature stands where Stringfield left it: a large, internally consistent, unauditable testimony corpus. The nuclear-incursion strand stands materially higher, on FOIA-released NORAD, NMCC and Air Force paper plus named affiants. The only judicial findings in the domain are that a UFO injury claim fails on the pleadings and that a UFO records search was inadequate.

timeline.label: Reckoning scheduled for publication
timeline.text: Elizondo's second book, promising 'previously undisclosed evidence', is scheduled for HarperCollins release with a 20-date speaking tour. Its DOPSR status is not yet public.

timeline.label: Air Force becomes the first military department to transfer into RG 615
timeline.text: The National Archives accessioned 'Records from the Department of the Air Force Relating to Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena' (catalog series 656595571, accession TR-0615-2026-0003) into Record Group 615: 30 PDF files dated 25 October 1945 to 31 December 1969, access and use both Unrestricted, carrying contiguous UAP Record Identifiers 342UAP00001 to 342UAP00030. It is the eighth agency series in RG 615 and the first from a military department in its own right. The documents' own declassification blocks show the Air Force Declassification Office cleared them on 5 May 2025 under the FY24 NDAA authority now codified at 44 U.S.C. 2107, fifteen months before the records reached NARA.

timeline.label: The Ellsworth claim is published with both witnesses, and contradicts its own recording
timeline.text: Jesse Michels published video rjUdn6FklAU, 2:47:21, presenting Mario Woods and Michael Johnson on the 18 November 1977 Launch Facility November-5 claim. Its on-camera retelling of the moment of recognition at 00:17:46-00:18:11 says Johnson recognised the event with nothing supplied; its own recording of that moment at 00:07:29-00:07:46 shows an initial 'No', then Woods naming the UFO twice, then assent. Both passages are timestamped in the same episode. This is the dated artefact on which the claim rests.
timeline.source: Jesse Michels, video rjUdn6FklAU, 7 September 2026, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rjUdn6FklAU

timeline.label: Scheduled: DCSA NISP oversight phase-out
timeline.text: DoDI 5205.11 para 1.2.i: 'Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) oversight for the administration of the National Industrial Security Program will be phased out in July 2029 in accordance with the carve-out provision.' Forward-dated commitment recorded in a 12 September 2024 issuance.

(2) Status briefings: DI_Brief_2008 (16 Dec 2008), DI_Brief_2009 (8 May 2009), Contract_Status_24Aug09, and an undated Contract_Status_Briefing. (3) The Reid file: three DIA talking papers (5 Jan 2009, 4 May 2009, 19 Nov 2009), the Reid briefing deck of 8 May 2009, and Reid's SAP request of 24 Jun 2009. (4) The SAP decision chain: deliverables review U-429-09-DWO-IM (30 Oct 2009), OUSDI_IM_on_AATIP_Final, DIA memo U-09-2660CE-IM (13 Nov 2009), and the 18-page packet presented to the Deputy Secretary of Defense (17 Nov 2009). (5) The transition file: DIA info memo U-10-2552CE-IM-ATL to USD(AT&L), released in draft and in a four-page final under FOIA-00255-2022. What is NOT in the record: the BAASS Ten Month Report (leaked, never officially released), the Utah ranch investigation report (DIA reports no records), the 19 Jun 2007 Lacatski-to-Bigelow letter (DIA reports no records), the SECRET/NOFORN version of DIRD 37, obligation-by-year funding data, the AAWSAP personnel roster, and whatever comprises the 100-plus reports Lacatski describes.

uapda-2023.desc:
Key statutory definitions as passed by the Senate (Sec. 9003):

(5) 'controlling authority' means any Federal, State, or local government department, office, agency, committee, commission, commercial company, academic institution, or private sector entity in physical possession of technologies of unknown origin or biological evidence of non-human intelligence.

(11) 'legacy program' means all Federal, State, and local government, commercial industry, academic, and private sector endeavors to collect, exploit, or reverse engineer technologies of unknown origin or examine biological evidence of living or deceased non-human intelligence that pre-dates the date of the enactment of this Act.

(13) 'non-human intelligence' means any sentient intelligent non-human lifeform regardless of nature or ultimate origin that may be presumed responsible for unidentified anomalous phenomena or of which the Federal Government has become aware.

(2) 'close observer' means anyone who has come into close proximity to unidentified anomalous phenomena or non-human intelligence.

The Sec. 9003(23) definition of a 'unidentified anomalous phenomena record' reaches twenty-four categories of holder, expressly including the Department of Defense 'and its progenitors, the Department of War and the Department of the Navy'; the Air Force Office of Special Investigations by name; the Department of Energy 'and its progenitors, the Manhattan Project, the Atomic Energy Commission, and the Energy Research and Development Administration'; the CIA 'and its progenitor, the Office of Strategic Services'; the NRO, DIA, NSA, NGA, NASA, FBI, FAA, NOAA and the Library of Congress; and, at subparagraph (X), 'any private sector person or entity formerly or currently under contract or some other agreement with the Federal Government.'

ndaa-fy2024.desc: Section-by-section map of the UAP content of Public Law 118-31. Division A, Title XVI: sec. 1687, limitation on use of funds for certain unreported programs (137 Stat. 621-622), note 50 U.S.C. 3373 note at subsection (b). Division A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C: sec. 1841, UAP Records Collection at NARA (note 44 U.S.C. 2107 note, 137 Stat. 699-701); sec. 1842, review, identification, transmission and public disclosure by Government offices (137 Stat. 701-705), including the 300-day agency review deadline at (c)(1) and the 25-year full-disclosure deadline with Presidential certification escape at (g)(2)(D); sec. 1843, grounds for postponement (137 Stat. 705-707), including the 'clear and convincing evidence' standard applied by the original classification authority at (a) and the Senior Agency Official withdrawal power at (b). Division G (IAA FY2024), Title LXXIII: sec. 7341, shifting the annual report duty to the AARO Director (137 Stat. 1062-1063); sec. 7343, funding limitation and IR&D cost-allowability rule (137 Stat. 1063-1064).

ndaa-fy2023.desc: Public Law 117-263 carries UAP provisions in two separate divisions. Division A, Title XVI: sec. 1673, note 50 U.S.C. 3373b, UAP reporting procedures (136 Stat. 2959-2962) - the authorized-disclosure channel, the NDA and Atomic Energy Act override, the anti-reprisal rule, the 72-hour congressional notification for disclosures touching unreported SAPs, and the NDA-identification duty extending to federal contractors. nimitz-2004.desc: The 14 November 2004 encounter between Carrier Strike Group 11 and an unidentified object roughly 30 miles off Baja California is the founding event of the modern observational record, and this board treats it as the clearest available cross-section of how the concealment works in practice. Four things are documented beyond argument. First, the object existed and was described in an official Navy record: the range fouler report released via FOIA on 13 January 2023 calls it 'solid white, smooth, with no edges ... uniformly colored with no nacelles, pylons, or wings ... approximately 46 feet in length.' Second, it was tracked for two weeks by a US Navy Aegis cruiser descending from above 80,000 feet, per Fravor's sworn statement. Third, its infrared signature was captured by a US Navy targeting pod and, sixteen years later, the Department of Defense authenticated the footage while declining to explain it. Fourth, the reporting went nowhere: 'Reporting terminated at 3rd Fleet, there was no process to share the reporting.' Around that documented core sit two contested claims that pull in opposite directions. Fravor testified under his own name that 'the incident was never investigated, none of my crew were ever questioned, tapes were never taken.' Princeton crewmen Kevin Day and Gary Voorhis say recording media were removed by personnel who did not identify themselves within about 48 hours. Both can be true if collection was aimed at the ship's sensor archive rather than at the squadron - which would be the more sophisticated behaviour, not the less. What is certain is the outcome: two decades on, no Princeton radar data, no CEC recording, and no investigative file for the incident exists in any public release, while the object's own infrared portrait hangs in the Pentagon's press archive labelled 'unidentified.'

gallaudet-2015-email.desc: The recalled January 2015 US Fleet Forces Command message is the highest-value single artefact on the aviator strand, and it deserves separate treatment because of what it rules out. A refusal to comment is consistent with indifference. A classification decision is consistent with ordinary secrecy. But the retroactive deletion of an already-distributed fleet-wide flight-safety warning from the inboxes of every subordinate commander is not consistent with either. It requires that someone with authority over Navy messaging systems decided, within 24 hours, that a safety-of-flight warning about repeated near-midair collisions was more dangerous distributed than the near-midairs themselves. Gallaudet, a serving flag officer at the time and later acting NOAA Administrator, drew the only available inference in sworn testimony: the information 'must have been classified within a special access program managed by an intelligence agency.' The message is also the connective tissue between the two halves of the aviator record. It carried GO FAST - one of the three videos DoD later released as authentic and unidentified - and it described exactly the problem Ryan Graves's squadron was filing unacknowledged safety reports about in the same airspace in the same period. Nine years later, AARO reanalysed GO FAST on parallax grounds and concluded it showed nothing anomalous. That analysis, whatever its merits, has no bearing on why the warning was withdrawn. No agency has ever acknowledged withdrawing it, and the sender, message identifier and recall authority remain unidentified.

langley-2023-incursions.desc: The December 2023 Langley incursions are where the historical UAP record and the contemporary homeland-defence problem stop being separable. For at least seventeen nights beginning 6 December 2023, unidentified aircraft operated over a front-line F-22 base in Virginia. The response was not what an installation mounts against hobbyists: F-16 combat air patrols with tanker support, NASA's WB-57F high-altitude research aircraft flying surveillance orbits, FBI coordination routed through NORTHCOM. At least one object was described by Gen. Mark Kelly as roughly 20 feet long, moving at more than 100 mph at 3,000 to 4,000 feet. F-22s were moved; by October 2024 the Air Force was evaluating protective netting for the aircraft on the ground. And the commander of NORAD and US Northern Command, having made the incident the centrepiece of his 90-day assessment, said on the record that he knew of no organized or unorganized foreign nexus. The pattern then repeated and escalated: New Jersey in December 2024, met with a four-agency statement that resolved about 100 of more than 5,000 reports and generalised the result; UK bases in November 2024; a joint interagency task force in August 2025; an Inspector General finding in January 2026 that ten evaluated installations lacked coherent counter-drone authority; and in March 2026 waves of 12 to 15 jam-resistant drones over a nuclear-capable B-52 base during an active bombing campaign. Whatever these objects are, the record they generate is identical in shape to the record the 2004 and 2015 encounters generated: detected, tracked, unattributed, and officially minimised.
